मणि: Maṇi, Maṇināga m.: A mythical ser-pent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 10, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 6; according to Kṛṣṇa, Maṇināga had his residence (आलय) near Girivraja in the Magadha country; due to his presence the land of Magadha could never be avoided by the clouds (अपरिहार्या मेघानां मागधेयं मणेः कृते) 2. 19. 9-10.
मणिमत्: Maṇimant m.: A mythical serpent. One of the serpents who, without feeling fatigue, wait on Varuṇa in his सभा; marked with banner (पताकिन्) and round spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 9, 10, 11; according to Kṛṣṇa, he and the नाग Kauśika continue to favour the Magadha country 2. 19. 10.
Maṇimant1 m.: Name of a mountain. One of the mountains in the north crossed by Arjuna when he went to propitiate Śiva to get from him his Pāśupatāstra 7. 57. 27.

Maṇimant2 m.: Name of a sacred place. One who observes chastity and has concentrated his mind (ब्रह्मचारी समा-हितः), if he visits this place and stays there for a night (एकरात्रोषितः) he will get the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 80. 109.
मणिमन्त्: Maṇimant m.: A mythical serpent. One of the serpents who, without feeling fatigue, wait on Varuṇa in his सभा; marked with banner (पताकिन्) and round spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 9, 10, 11; according to Kṛṣṇa, he and the नाग Kauśika continue to favour the Magadha country 2. 19. 10.
Maṇimant1 m.: Name of a mountain. One of the mountains in the north crossed by Arjuna when he went to propitiate Śiva to get from him his Pāśupatāstra 7. 57. 27.

Maṇimant2 m.: Name of a sacred place. One who observes chastity and has concentrated his mind (ब्रह्मचारी समा-हितः), if he visits this place and stays there for a night (एकरात्रोषितः) he will get the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 80. 109.
मणिस्कन्ध: Maṇiskandha m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग) and ‘having excess of poison’ (वीषोल्बण) 1. 52. 17, 13.
मण्डलक: Maṇḍalaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those who were offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 7, 6, 9.
मधुपर्क: Madhuparka m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 14, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because engaged in destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
मलय: Malaya m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 14, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahmin-hood because engaged in destroying his kins-men 5. 99. 2-8.

Malaya1 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the seven principal mountains of Bhārata-varṣa (सप्तैते कुलपर्वताः) 6. 10. 10; on the southern ocean, near the mountain Sahya and Dardura 3. 266. 42. B. Description: Glorious (श्रीमन्त्) 3. 264. 34; 6. 7. 53; great mountain (महाशैल) 3. 264. 34; red in colour (ताम्रवर्ण) 6. 7. 53. C. Characteristics: (1) The two Apsarases, Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti, visit the mountain constantly (यं नित्यम् उपसेवते) 12. 319. 20; (2) Sandalwood is known as growing on the mountain Malaya (मलयज) 1. 23. 4 (the forest to which the Nāgas were carried by Suparṇa was marked by sky-high (sandal-wood) trees which grow on mountain Malaya उपजिघ्रद्भिर् आकाशं वृक्षैर् मलयजैर् अपि 1. 23. 4; (3) Malaya mountain formed the head of the Jambudvīpa which had the form of a hare having two Dvīpas, the Nāgadvīpa and the Kaśyapadvīpa, for its two ears 6. 7. 52-53. D. Past events: (1) Malaya was the first mountain beyond which Śuka sojourned in his journey upwards through the space (ततः समतिचक्राम मलयं नाम पर्वतम्) 12. 319. 20; (2) Nahuṣa, when he became the king of heaven, enjoyed in the company of the Apsa-rases and Devakanyās on Malaya and other mountains 5. 11. 9; (3) Mārkaṇḍeya saw Malaya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 104; (4) Hanūmant and others when they came out of a cave in the south they saw the mountains Malaya, Sahya and Dardura near the ocean; when they went up the moun-tain Malaya they realized the expanse of the ocean and were dejected. E. Importance: Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2. F. Similes: (1) Sugrīva with a garland around his neck looked like the great mountain Malaya, circled by a garland of clouds 3. 264. 34; (2) Malaya, is one of the four mountains with which Yudhiṣṭhira compared his four brothers 3. 297. 14; (3) The banner (केतु) on the chariot of the king of the Pāṇḍyas, adorned with चन्दन and अगुरु, is compared with Malaya 8. 15. 32; (4) The narrative of Nārāyaṇa was collected (समुद्धृतम्) by Vaiśaṃpāyana from the Mahābhārata as one collects the sandalwood from Malaya 12. 331. 3.

Malaya2 m.: Name of a mountain of the Śākadvīpa; also called Jalada. One of the seven mountains of the Śāka-dvīpa 6. 12. 12, 14; described as extending to-wards the east (प्रागायत); clouds originate there and appear everywhere (यतो मेघाः प्रवर्तन्ते प्रभवन्ति च सर्वशः) 6. 12. 14; hence referred to also as Jalada 6. 12. 23; all the seven mountains of Śākadvīpa are said to be decked with gems (मणि-भूषिताः) and are mines of jewels (रत्ना-कराः) 6. 12. 13; the extent of all the seven mountains of the Śākadvīpa is double that of the one preceding it in the order of their enu-meration (तेषां योजनविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 12. 22; the Varṣa related to this mountain is Kumudottara 6. 12. 23.

Malaya m. (pl.): Name of a people. Described as very strong (महाबल) 2. 27. 8; they were vanquished by Bhīma-sena in his expedition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 27. 1, 7; 2. 23. 9) before the Rājasūya (विजिग्ये … मत्स्यान् मलयांश् च) 2. 27. 7-8. [For Malaya1, 2 names of mountains see Vol. I pp. 407-408].
महाजय: Mahājaya m.: A mythical serpent. Vāsuki gave two snakes, Jaya and Mahājaya, to the son of Agni (i. e. Skanda) 9. 44. 48.
महापद्म: Mahāpadma m.: A mythical elephant. One of the great elephants (महानागस्), the दिङ्नागस्, created by Ghaṭotkaca with his माया; Rākṣasas mounted them and follow-ed Ghaṭotkaca on his Airāvata (also created by माया) when he attacked Bhagadatta on his elephant; they all were of huge shape, with rut flowing from temples, very strong and endowed with lustre; they had four tusks 6. 60. 51, 50, 52, 54; excellent elephants born in the कुल of Mahāpadma were killed by Sātyaki in the war 7. 97. 24, 26.

Mahāpadma nt.: Name of a city. Situated on the southern bank of Gaṅgā (गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तीरे); described as ex-cellent city (पुरोत्तम); a certain pious Brāhmaṇa, deliberating on the nature of Dharma, lived there 12. 341. 1, 6-7.
महाहनु: Mahāhanu m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 16, 13.
महोदर: Mahodara m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 15, 2.
मातङ्गी: Mātaṅgī f.: A mythical female ele-phant. One of the nine self-born (आत्मसं-भवा) daughters of Krodhavaśā (or of Tāmrā (?) 1. 60. 54; in that case क्रोधवशा ‘irascible’); she gave birth to elephants 1. 60. 58, 59, 64.
मातरिश्वन्: Mātariśvan m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas to 5. 99. 14, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahmin-hood because engaged in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
मानव: Mānava m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 15, 13.
मानस: Mānasa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; some of the serpents in this family were dark-red others white; all of them were terrific, of huge shape, having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 5, 4, 6.

Mānasa1 nt. (sg., pl.): Name of a lake. A. Location: In the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां तस्माद् दिशम्) 2. 24. 1; situated beyond the Himavant and the Śveta moun-tains 2. 24. 27; 2. 25. 1; beyond the country of the Kiṃpuruṣas; near the Hāṭaka country (हाटकान् अभितः) of the Guhyakas and the Gandharva country 2. 25. 1-3, 5. B. Des-cription: Holy (पुण्य) 13. 105. 45; heavenly (दिव्य) 13. 140. 23 (not named); best (उत्तम) 2. 25. 4; having fruits and flowers of all seasons (सर्वर्तुफलपुष्पेषु मान-सेषु सरःसु च) 1. 143. 26. C. Chara-cteristics: (1) Dwelling place of swans, hence they are called मानसौकसः 6. 114. 91; 8. 28. 20; 8. 43. 64; (2) Owing to the boon given by Brahman to the lake (ब्रह्म-दत्तवरं सरः), the Khalin demons, when killed in war, repeatedly bathed there and came out alive (हता हता वै ते तत्र जीवन्त्य् आप्लुत्य दानवाः) 13. 140. 18. D. Holiness: The high-souled persons and those who observe vows if they visit the Mānasa lake they assume heavenly form, become auspicious, and putting on heavenly garlands and rich in holy fragrance they enjoy in the Goloka (? मोदन्ति गवां विमाने) 13. 105. 45, 44, 48 (for citation see Kara-toyinī). E. Epic events: (1) Hiḍimbā, after she was allowed to take Bhīma as her husband, delighted him at many places (रमयाम् आस पाण्डवम्), some of those being the Mānasa lakes (माणसेषु सरःसु च) 1. 143. 26; (2) Arjuna saw it in his expedition to the north and then conquered Hāṭaka, the country of the Guhyakas, along with the country of the Gandharvas 2. 25. 4-5; (3) Lomaśa showed to Yudhiṣṭhira the gate of the Mānasa (एतद् द्वारं महा-राज मानसस्य प्रकाशते) 3. 130. 12; (4) When Bhīṣma decided to extend his life till the advent of the Uttarāyaṇa, Gaṅgā sent great sages to him in the form of swans living in the Mānasa lake 6. 114. 91. F. Past and mythological events: (1) The illustri-ous Rāma (Jāmadagnya) established a place for him to reside on the mountain (Hima-vant) and near the gate of the Mānasa (एतद् द्वारं महाराज मानसस्य प्रकाशते । वर्षम् अस्य गिरेर् मध्ये रामेण श्रीमता कृतम् ॥ ) 3. 130. 12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 130. 12: वर्षं वसतिस्थानम्); (2) The Ādityas once performed a सत्र near the Mānasa lake; sage Vasiṣṭha also lived near it; the demons, called Khalins, disturbed the sacrifice of the Ādityas; Śakra (Indra) sought help from Vasiṣṭha and the latter burnt the demons by his lustre 13. 140. 16-22; (3) Vasiṣṭha brought the river Gaṅgā, flowing towards Kailāsa. to the lake Mānasa; the river broke the lake and hence the river came to be known as Sarayū (सरो भिन्नं तया नद्या सरयूः सा ततो ऽभवत्) 13. 140. 23-24; (4) Indra, afraid of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa, divided it into two (तस्यां द्वैधीभूतायां ब्रह्मवध्यायाम्) and went to a lotus flower (नलिनीम्) in the Mānasa lake; there he became of the size of an atom and entered a knot on the lotus stalk (अणुमात्रो भूत्वा बिसग्रन्थिं प्र-विवेश) 12. 329. 28 (1); goddess Upaśruti took Indra's wife, Śacī, to the lotus in the Mānasa lake and showed her Indra who had entered the knot on the stalk 12. 329. 34 (6). G. Fable: A certain crow, who thought much of himself, once dared to challenge one of the swans living in the Mānasa lake 8. 28. 20. [See Uttaramānasa]

Mānasa2 m.: Name of a mountain. Indra went to the Mānasa mountain in search of a leader for the army of the gods (देवसेना) which was overpowered by the demons; there he heard the cry of a woman (who was Devasenā); the two sisters Deva-senā and Daityasenā, daughters of Prajāpati, used to come there with their friends for pleasure; from this mountain the demon Keśin took away Daityasenā, who longed for him, but Devasenā was rescued by Indra 3. 213. 17.

Mānasa3 nt.: A metaphorical तीर्थ। One should bathe in the mental lake which is unfathomable, dirt-free, pure, has truth for water and forbearance for lake (अगाधे विमले शुद्धे सत्यतोये धृतिह्रदे । स्नातव्यं मानसे तीर्थे … ) 13. 111. 3.

Mānasa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada of the Śākadvīpa. Listed by Saṃjaya among the four Janapadas of Śākadvīpa (मानसा मन्दगास् तथा) 6. 12. 33; described as holy (पुण्य) and honoured by the people (लोकसंमत) 6. 12. 33; the Vaiśya people of the Mānasa Janapada earned their livelihood by doing their work; they obtained all their desires, were brave and clear in their minds about धर्म and अर्थ (the two पुरुषार्थस्) (मानसेषु महाराज वैश्याः कर्मोप-जीविनः । सर्वकामसमायुक्ताः शूराः धर्-मार्थनिश्चिताः ॥ ) 6. 12. 5.
माल्यपिण्डक: Mālyapiṇḍaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 13, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
मिश्रिन्: Miśrin m.: A mythical serpent. One of those who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and ent-ering the ocean 16. 5. 14, 12.
मुखर: Mukhara m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 16, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 14, 2.
मुण्ड: Muṇḍa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Kauravya, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 12, 1.

Muṇḍa m. (pl.): Name of a people (?). Kṛṣṇa had seen Muṇḍas and many others acting as servants in the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (जागुडान् रमठान् मुण्डान्  … आगतान् अहम् अद्राक्षं यज्ञे ते परि-वेषकान्) 3. 48. 21-22; on the fourteenth day of war, Sātyaki told his charioteer that he would kill the army of Muṇḍas again and again (मुण्डान् एतान् हनिष्यामि  … मुण्डानीके हते सूत … चासकृत्) 7. 95. 20-21 (मुण्ड, name of a people or does the word here describe (shaven) Jāguḍas, Ramaṭhas and others like Kāmbojas 7. 95. 20 or Mlecchas 7. 68. 44 ?).
मुण्डवेदाङ्ग: Muṇḍavedāṅga m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 15, 13, 1.
मुद्गर: Mudgara m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the family of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 9, 7, 1
मुद्गरपर्णक: Mudgaraparṇaka m.: A mythical ser-pent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 13, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
मुद्गरपिण्डक: Mudgarapiṇḍaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 9, 2.
मूक: Mūka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 8, 7, 9.
मूषकाद: Mūṣakāda m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 12, 2. [See Mūṣikāda]
मूषिकाद: Mūṣikāda m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 14, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; described as marked with jewel, स्वस्तिक, circles and कमण्डलु, having many heads and faces, and of huge shape 5. 101. 5-7; he, among other serpents, waits without feeling fatigue (विगतक्लम), upon Varuṇa in his सभा; marked with banner (पताकिन्) and round spots (मण्डलिन्), and hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 10. [See Mūṣakāda]
मृगमन्दा: Mṛgamandā f.: A mythical female animal. One of the nine self-born (आत्मसं-भवा) daughters of Krodhavaśā (or of Tāmrā (?) 1. 60. 54; in that case क्रोधवशा ‘irascible’); she gave birth to bears, musk deer (?सृमर) and yaks 1. 60. 58, 60.
मृगी: Mṛgī f.: A mythical female deer. One of the nine self-born (आत्मसं-भवा) daughters of Krodhavaśā (or of Tāmrā (?) 1. 60. 54; in that case क्रोधवशा ‘irascible’); she gave birth to deer 1. 60. 58, 60.
मेघकृत्: Meghakṛt m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 12, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on ser-pents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
मेघपुष्प: Meghapuṣpa m.: Name of one of the four horses yoked to the chariot of Kṛṣṇa. They all were of excellent Kamboja-breed (परमकाम्बोज) 10. 13. 1; decorat-ed with gold strings (हेममालिन् 10. 13. 1) and gold harness (हेमभाण्डविभूषित 7. 122. 45); endowed with all excellences (सर्वसंपद्-) 5. 81. 19; very swift (महावेग) and could go where they desired (कामग) 7. 122. 45; 10. 13. 9; when they sped along they appeared to swallow the sky (ते ग्रसन्त इवाकाशं वेगवन्तो महा-बलाः) 12. 53. 22-23; all the horses specially marked for their speed, hence Uttara com-pared his horse with Meghapuṣpa 4. 40. 19; Meghapuṣpa is one of the two side-horses (पार्ष्णिवाह), his position being to the left 4. 40. 19; 10. 13. 2 (according to 4. 40. 19, however, Meghapuṣpa was not a पार्ष्णिवाह, but one bearing the left side of the yoke); Meghapuṣpa mentioned among the four horses when Kṛṣṇa's chariot was got ready on various occasions—(1) while he pro-ceeded to Hāstinapura on his peace mission 5. 81. 19; (2) for Kṛṣṇa's likely interven-tion in war to kill Karṇa, Droṇa and the rest and to enable Arjuna to kill Jayadratha within the stipulated time 7. 50. 35, 25-37; (3) for the use of Sātyaki when he lost his chariot in his duel with Karṇa 7. 122. 44-46; (4) when Kṛṣṇa followed Bhīma who had left in pursuit of Aśvatthāman 10. 13. 1, 2; and (5) when Kṛṣṇa went to visit Bhīṣma, lying on his bed of arrows at Kurukṣetra 12. 53. 21.
मेचक: Mecaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 14, 13.
मैन्द: Mainda m.: A monkey-chief. One of the four councillors (सचिव) of Sugrīva 3. 264. 23; according to Tārā, wife of Vālin, all the four were noble-minded (महात्मन्), intelligent (बुद्धि-मन्त्) and very strong (महाबल) 3. 264. 24; Mainda was one of the guardians of the army of Rāma when it marched towards the southern ocean 3. 267. 19; he, with other monkey-chiefs, kept watch over the bodies of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa lying on the ground bound by the arrows of Indrajit 3. 273. 4; he, along with others, applied to his eyes water sent by Kubera so that he could see even invisible beings 3. 273. 10-13 (in all above references Mainda is mentioned together with Dvivida); Mainda and the other monkey-chiefs surrounded Rāvaṇa when he rushed forward to attack Rāma 3. 274. 3.
मोद: Moda m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Airāvata, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1 52. 10, 11.
मकर: Makara, Mākara (8. 7. 14) m.: Name of a particular way of arranging the army (व्यूह). A. Description: Tormentor of the enemies (शत्रुतापन) 6. 71. 4; hard like वज्र (वज्रकल्प) 6. 76. 5. B. Its use: (1) Bhīṣma arranged the Kaurava army that way on the fifth day of the war to counter the Śyenavyūha of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 65. 7; Bhīṣma guarded it on all sides 6. 6. 65. 4; Bhīma entered the Makaravyūha from the front (मुखतः) and attacked Bhīṣma with arrows 6. 65. 13; (2) On the sixth day of the war Yudhiṣṭhira asked Dhṛṣṭadyumna to arrange the army acco-rding to the Makaravyūha 6. 71. 4; its ‘head’ (शीरस्) was formed by Drupada and Arjuna; its ‘eyes’ (चक्षुषी) were Sahadeva and Nakula; its ‘mouth’ (तुण्ड) was Bhīmasena; its ‘neck’ (ग्रीवा) were Abhimanyu, the sons of Draupadī, Ghaṭot-kaca, Sātyaki and Yudhiṣṭhira; its ‘back’ (पृष्ठ) was formed by Virāṭa and Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna with a large army; its ‘left side’ (वामपार्श्व) was formed by the five Kekaya brothers, and the ‘right side’ (दक्षिण पार्श्व) by Dhṛṣṭaketu and Karakarṣa; its ‘two feet’ (पादौ) were Kuntibhoja and Śatā-nīka with a large army; its ‘tail’ (पुच्छ) was Śikhaṇḍin, surrounded by Somakas, and Irāvant 6. 71. 6-12; Duryodhana complained to Bhīṣma that when he entered the Makara vyūha (6. 75. 1) he was overpowered by Bhīma with arrows 6. 76. 5; (3) Karṇa arranged Kaurava army according to the Mākara vyūha (8. 7. 14) on the sixteenth day of the war; its ‘mouth’ (तुण्ड) was Karṇa; its ‘eyes’ (नेत्रे) were Śakuni and Ulūka; its ‘head’ (शिरस्) was Aśvatthāman; its ‘neck’ (ग्रीवा) was formed by Duryodhana's brothers; at its ‘waist’ (मध्य) was Duryodhana with a large army; at the ‘left foot’ (वामपाद) was Kṛtavarman with Gopālas from the army of Nārāyaṇa and at the ‘right foot’ (दक्षिण पाद) Kṛpa surrounded by the Trigartas and the Dākṣiṇā-tyas; at the ‘left hind-foot’ (वाम अनुपाद) was Śalya with a large Madra army; at the ‘right (hind-foot)’ (दक्षिण) was Suṣeṇa with one thousand chariots and a hundred elephants; at the ‘tail’ (पुच्छ) were the brothers Citrasena and Citra (the Abhisāra princes) who stood there with a large army; 8. 7. 15-21; to counter this Mākara vyūha of the Kauravas, Arjuna used the Ardha-candra vyūha 8. 7. 27.
मणिपुष्पक: Maṇipuṣpaka m.: Name of a conch. It belonged to Sahadeva; he blew it on the first day of the war when the two armies were arrayed against each other 6. 23. 16; he blew it the next day at the start of the war 6. 47. 26, (and presumably on all the following days).
मण्डल: Maṇḍala m.: Name of a particular arrangement of the army (व्यूह). Described as bristling with many weapons (नानाशस्त्रसमाकुल) 6. 77. 12; very large (सुमहाव्यूह); difficult to be penetrated (दुर्भेद्य); difficult to be reached by the enemies (अरीणां दुरासदः) 6. 77. 20; very terrible (परमदारुण) 6. 77. 21; Bhīṣma arranged the Kaurava army according to this व्यूह on the seventh day of the war 6. 77. 11-12; it faced the west (प्रत्यङ्मुख) 6. 77. 20; it was surrounded on all sides by many thousands of chariots, large troops of horsemen holding ऋष्टिस् and तोमरस्; every elephant was guarded by seven chariots, and every chariot by seven horsemen; near every horseman were stationed ten archers, and seven swordsmen (चर्मिणः lit. ‘holding shields’) stood guard near every archer 6. 77. 13-14; to counter the Maṇḍalavyūha the Pāṇḍavas used the Vajravyūha 6. 77. 21.
मण्डलार्ध: Maṇḍalārdha m.: Name of a particular arrangement of the army (व्यूह). Yudhiṣṭhira arranged the army of the Pāṇḍavas according to this व्यूह on the twelfth day of the war to counter the Suparṇa-vyūha of the Kauravas 7. 19. 4.
महाव्यूह: Mahāvyūha m.: Name of a particular way of arranging the army (व्यूह). Described as extremely invincible (सुदुर्जय) 6. 95. 38; (1) Bhīṣma, Droṇa and Duryodhana arranged on the second day of the war the Kaurava army according to Mahāvyūha to counter the Krauñca vyūha of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 47. 1, 10; 6. 48. 10; in this arrangement Bhīṣma, sur-rounded by a large army, was in the front; he was followed by Droṇa, accompanied by the Kuntalas, Daśārṇas, Māgadhas and many others; Śakuni with his army, as also the Gāndhāras, Sindhusauvīras, the Śibis, and the Vasātis, moved with Droṇa to protect him; Duryodhana, with his brothers, and the Aśvātakas, the Vikarṇas, the Śar-milas and the Kośalas, and many others took positions to offer protection to the army of Śakuni; Bhūriśravas, Śala, Śalya, Bhaga-datta, Vinda and Anuvinda of the Avanti, stood on the left side of the vyūha (वाम-पार्श्व); Saumadatti (Bhūriśravas) Suśar-man, Sudakṣiṇa of the Kāmboja country, Śatāyu and Śrutāyu took care of the right side (दक्षिण पार्श्व); Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman with a large army guarded the rear (सेनापृष्ठे व्यवस्थिताः); kings of many countries, Ketumant, Vasudāna, and the son of the Kāśī king acted as the rear-guards of the army (पृष्ठगोपाः) 6. 47. 11-20; (2) Apparently the Kaliṅga king, when asked by Duryodhana to protect Droṇa and attack Bhīma (6. 49. 37, 38; 6. 50. 1, 3 ff.), had arranged his army in the Mahā-vyūha way (महाव्यूहः कलिङ्गानाम् 6. 50. 113); in that vyūha many elephants, horse-men, and chariot fighters took part (नागा-श्वरथसंकुलः); Bhīma, by himself, was able to crush it 6. 50. 113; (3) Bhīṣma arranged the Kaurava army according to the Mahāvyūha on the eighth day of the war 6. 83. 5, 13, 15; it looked like an ocean (सागर-प्रतिम) 6. 83. 5, (सागरोपम) 6. 83. 16; the vyūha was led by Bhīṣma, accompanied by the Mālavas, Dākṣiṇātyas, and the Āvan-tyas; he was followed by Droṇa, accompa-nied by Pulindas, Pāradas, Kṣudrakas, and the Mālavas; Droṇa was followed by Bhaga-datta, accompanied by the Māgadhas, the Kaliṅgas, and the Piśācas; behind him was Bṛhadbala of the Kosala country, accompa-nied by the Mekalas, the Traipuras, and the Cicchilas; then came Trigarta (Suśarman), the ruler of Prasthalas accompanied by many Kāṃbojas and the Yavanas in thousands; Aśvatthāman followed Trigarta; behind Aśvatthāman marched Duryodhana surround-ed by his brothers; Kṛpa followed Duryo-dhana 6. 83. 6-13; (4) The Pāṇḍavas arranged their army in the Mahāvyūha way (6. 95. 38) on the ninth day of the war to counter the Sarvatobhadravyūha of the Kauravas (6. 95. 26); in the forefront of this vyūha stood Bhīmasena (6. 95. 40), along with Yudhiṣṭhira, Nakula and Saha-deva; Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Virāṭa and Sātyaki apparently followed them; they seem to have been followed by Śikhaṇḍin, Vijaya (Arjuna), the Rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, Cekitāna and Kunti-bhoja, all of them encircled by large armies; the rear seems to have been made up by Abhimanyu, Drupada, and five Kekaya brothers (6. 95. 34-38); (but Arjuna had advised Dhṛṣṭadyumna to see that Śikhaṇḍin confronted Bhīṣma and that he would pro-tect Śikhaṇḍin (शिखण्डिनं नरव्याघ्र भीष्मस्य प्रमुखे ऽनघ । स्थापय-स्वाद्य पाञ्चाल्य तस्य गोप्ताहम् अप्य् उत 6. 95. 25; according to Duryodhana's infor-mation, in that position Yudhāmanyu would guard the left wheel of Arjuna and Utta-maujas the right wheel 6. 95. 21).
महास्त्र: Mahāstra nt.: The ‘great’ missile, not named, employed by Arjuna on his Añjalika arrow (8. 67. 16). Arjuna, who knew the मन्त्रस् of this missile, charged his arrow with the Mahāstra when he shot it at Karṇa to kill him (युक्त्वा महास्त्रेण परेण मन्त्रवित्); he then described his arrow as Mahāstra (अयम् महास्त्रो ऽप्रतिमो धृतः शरः) 8. 67. 19; he also strengthened it with the power of truth by making a सत्यक्रिया (तपो ऽस्ति तप्तं गुरवश् च तोषिता मया यद् इष्टं सुहृदां तथा श्रुतम् । अनेन सत्येन नि-हन्त्व् अयं शरः सुदंशितः कर्णं अरिं ममाजितः) 8. 67. 20; the arrow was then to work like a fierce अथर्वाङ्गिरसी magic and bring victory to Arjuna (कृत्याम् अथर्-वाङ्गिरसीम् इवोग्रां … अयं शरो मे विज-यावहो ऽस्तु) 8. 67. 21-22.
माकर: Mākara adj.: of a व्यूह। [See Makara].
माधव: Mādhava nt.: Name of a missile. A favourite (दयित) missile of Deva-rāja (Indra); described as great (परम) and having sharp lustre (तिग्मतेजस्); used by Arjuna while fighting with the demons called the Nivātakavacas who were enemies of Indra; with the might of this missile (अस्त्र-वीर्य) Arjuna was able to cut the swords, the tridents (त्रिशूलस्), and तोमरस् in thousands hurled against him by the demons 3. 167. 19-20.
Mādhava m.: Name of a month. [See Vaiśākha].
मारुत: Māruta nt.: Name of a missile. Mentioned along with Āgni, i. e. the Āgneyāstra (उभे चैवाग्निमारुते); it was meant to be used by Arjuna against the Kauravas in the war 5. 140. 6.
मानुष: Mānuṣa adj.: of missiles specific to human beings. They are not named but are distinguished from such divine missiles as Vāruṇa, Āgneya Brāhma, Aindra and Nārāyaṇa astra; Droṇa reputed to have the knowledge of both these kinds of missiles 7. 166. 2.

Mānuṣa2 adj.: of व्यूहस् (arrange-ments of the army) known to men. Bhīṣma knew different kinds of व्यूहस्, some of them known as Mānuṣa vyūhas 5. 162. 8. 10; 6. 19. 2; he arranged the Kaurava army everyday in a different way, one of the ways being Mānuṣa (vyūha) 6. 20. 18; Dhṛṣṭadyumna, who led the Pāṇḍava army, also knew these different vyūhas 5. 56. 11.

Mānuṣa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated at a distance of one क्रोश to the west of the river Āpagā 3. 81. 55; one should proceed to the Mānuṣatīrtha from the Daśāśvamedhika 3. 81. 52-53; described as famous in the world (लोकविश्रुत) 3. 81. 53; black antelopes, when afflicted by a hunter, jumped into this तीर्थ and became human beings (which explains the name of the तीर्थ) (यत्र कृष्णमृगा राजन् व्या-धेन परिपीडिताः । अवगाह्य तस्मिन् सरसि मानुषत्वम् उपागताः) 3. 81. 53; one who observes chastity and has controlled his sense organs (ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः), if he bathes there he is cleansed of all sins and is glorified in heaven 3. 81. 54.
माहेन्द्र: Māhendra1 adj.: of a missile belonging to Mahendra (Indra), (different from Aindra ?). Yudhiṣṭhira employed this missile to defeat the Aindra and the Prājāpatya missiles used simultaneously against him by Droṇa (प्रादुश्चकारास्त्रम् अहीनतेजा माहेन्द्रम् अन्यत् स जघान ते ऽस्त्रे) 7. 132. 32. [See Aindrāstra]

Māhendra2 adj.: of the bow Vijaya which belonged to Indra; used in the epic war by Karṇa. It is one of the only three divine bows (the other two being Gāṇḍiva of Varuṇa and Śārṅga of Viṣṇu) 5. 155. 5-6. [See Vijaya]
मुसल: Musala m., nt.: A weapon specially mentioned in relation to Jaya. Jaya held it when he came to the aid of Indra in his fight with Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna at the Khāṇḍava forest (जगृहे … मुसलं च जयस् तथा) 1. 218. 32; (also Balarāma is called मुसलायुध 9. 35. 2; 9. 48. 6).
मृत्युदण्ड: Mṛtyudaṇḍa m.: Missile of the god of Death. [See Daṇḍa]
मोहनास्त्र: Mohanāstra nt.: Name of a missile. [See Pramohanāstra]
मन्त्रपर्वन्: Mantraparvan nt.: Name of the 21st पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 39, 33, 70. Referred to as ‘the beginning of the Rājasūya’ (राजसूयस्य चारम्भः) while listing the contents of the Sabhāparvan 1. 2. 98; comprises the अध्यायस् 2. 12-17.
महाप्रस्थानिक: Mahāprasthānika nt.: Name of the 97th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 68, 33, 70; name of the 17th पर्वन् among the 18 major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata. 1. 2. 230. In this पर्वन् the Pāṇḍavas, having abandoned the kingdom, attained, along with Draupadī, the highest perfection (सिद्धिं परमिकां गताः) 1. 2. 230; the sage who sees the truth (i. e. Vyāsa, not named) has said that the पर्वन् has three अध्यायस् and has counted its stanzas to be one hundred and twenty (सांख्यातास् तत्त्वदर्शिना) 1. 2. 231; related to the अध्यायस् 17. 1-3.
महोपनिषद्: Mahopaniṣad f.: Name (?) of a sacred text 6. 114. 12. (1) Bhīṣma, when he fell down from his chariot, resorted to Yoga and started reciting Mahopaniṣad; in that condition he waited for the arrival of proper time for giv-ing up his life (महोपनिषदं चैव योगम् आस्थाय वीर्यवान् । जपञ् शान्तनवो धीमान् कालाकाङ्क्षी स्थितो ऽभवत् ॥ ) 6. 114. 112; (2) Bhūriśravas, when his right hand was cut off by Arjuna, gave up fighting with Sātyaki and started meditating on the Mahopaniṣad; he then became a sage engaged in Yoga (ध्यायन् महोपनिषदं योग-युक्तो ऽभवन् मुनिः) 7. 118. 18. [See Mahopaniṣada]
महोपनिषद: Mahopaniṣada nt.: Name (?) of a section (12. 326. 20-99) in the Śāntiparvan 12. 326. 100. Described as being in conformity with the four Vedas and composed according to Sāṃkhya and the Yoga, and following the Pañcarātra (इदं महोपनिषदं चतुर्-वेदसमन्वितम् । सांख्ययोगकृतं तेन पञ्चरात्रानुशब्दितम् ॥ ) 12. 326. 100: it was sung by Nārāyaṇa (नारायणमुखोद्-गीत 12. 326. 101) to Nārada when he visited the great Śvetadvīpa (12. 325. 1); in it Nārāyaṇa is described to Nārada as one eternal Person, Vāsudeva (एकं पुरुषं वासुदेवं सनातनम् 12. 326. 31), who is called the soul of the world (लोकस्यांएति कथ्यते 12. 326. 21) or the soul of all beings (सर्वभूतात्मभुतो हि वासुदेवः 12. 326. 31); that Puraṣa is devoid of activity and can be seen only through knowledge; there is nothing beyond that eternal Puruṣa (पुरुषो निष्क्रियश् चैव ज्ञानदृश्यश् च कथ्यते 12. 326. 23; अव्यक्तं पुरुषे ब्रह्मन् निष्क्रिये संप्रलीयते । नास्ति तस्मात् पर-तरं पुरुषाद् वै सनातनात् 12. 326. 30); one should know him to be the eternal, highest self Vāsudeva (12. 326. 24); he, the क्षेत्रज्ञ, enjoys the three गुणस् सत्त्व, रजस् and तमस्, but is not affected by them (12. 326. 27, 21); that Vāsudeva himself (क्षेत्रज्ञ) is Saṃkar-ṣaṇa (जीव), from whom arises Pradyumna (मनस्), and from Pradyumna arises Ani-ruddha (अहंकार) (12. 326, 38-39; 35-37, 68-69); all gods and sages resort to him and the entire world is contained in him (12. 326, 47-55); his incarnations from Varāha to Kṛṣṇa are narrated in 12. 326. 71-93; having thus told Nārada all that was past. and also the future, with its secret the blessed God disappeared (एतत् ते सर्वम् आख्यातं ब्रह्मन् भक्तिमतो मया । पुराणं च भविष्यं च सरहस्यं च सत्तम ॥ एवं स भगवान् देवो विश्व-मूऋतिधरो ऽव्ययः । एतावद् उक्त्वा वचनं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥ ) 12. 326. 97-98; Nārada narrated what he heard from Nārā-yaṇa again to Brahman in his abode (नाराय-णमुखोद्गीतं नारदो ऽस्रावयत् पुनः । ब्रह्मणः सदने तात यथा दृष्टं यथा श्रुतम् ॥ ) 12. 326. 101. [See Mahopa-niṣad]
मातङ्गवचन: Mātaṅgavacana nt.: A stanza attribu-ted to Mātaṅga 5. 125. 19-20. Duryodhana, when under pressure from all quarters to come to terms with the Pāṇḍavas, while replying to Kṛṣṇa quoted the authority of Mātaṅga in support of the course of action chosen by him (viz. not bowing down before the enemy for fear of losing life); Mātaṅga had said: “One should rise up and not bow down, for rising up means manliness; one may break one's bone (lit. ‘which has no joints’), but not bow down before any one” (उद्यच्छेद् एव न नमेद् उद्यमो ह्य् एव पौरुषम् । अप्य् अपर्वण्त् भज्येत न नमेद् इह कस्यचित् । ) 5. 125. 19 (However Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 127. 19: अपर्वणि अप्रस्तावे); this dictum of Mātaṅga is cherished by those who seek their welfare (इति मातङ्गवचनं परी-प्सन्ती हितेप्सवः) 5. 125. 20.
मात्स्यक: Mātsyaka adj.: of a Purāṇa (इत्य् एतन् मात्स्यकं नाम पुराणं परिकीर्तितम् । 3. 185. 53. Also called आख्यान which removes all sins (आख्यानम् इदम् आख्यातं सर्व-पापहरं मया) 3. 185. 53; the Purāṇa narrates the story of Manu and the fish 3. 185. 1-54; one who always listens to the story of Manu from the very beginning becomes happy, all his objectives are ful-filled, and he goes to heaven 3. 185. 54.
मानवी: Mānavī adj.: of Arthavidyā proclaimed by Manu 7. 5. 34. Droṇa, while accepting Duryodhana's proposal to lead the army after the fall of Bhīṣma, informed him that besides knowing the Veda with its six auxiliary sciences, he knew the Arthavidyā proclaimed by Manu (वेदं षडङ्गं वेदाहं अर्थविद्यां च मानवीम्) 7. 5. 34.

Mānavī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 31, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
मार्कण्डेयसमस्या: Mārkaṇḍeyasamasyā f.: Name of the 37th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 45, 33, 70. Listed in the contents of the Āraṇyaka-parvan; many narratives (उपाख्यानस्) are told in this समस्या 1. 2. 124 (मार्कण्डेय-समस्यायाम् उपाख्यानानि भागशः); related to the अध्यायस् 3. 179-221.
म्र्गस्वप्नभय: Mrgasvapnabhaya nt.: Name of the 40th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 46, 33, 70. Not listed in the contents of the Āraṇya-kaparvan (i. e. at 1. 2. 125); related to the अध्याय 3. 244.
मोक्षधर्म: Mokṣadharma m.: Name of the 88th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 64. Described as the best among the धर्मस् followed by those who observe rhe four religious stages of life (धर्मम् आश्रमिणां श्रेष्ठम्) 12. 168. 1; referred to in the brief mention of the contents of the Śāntiparvan as one where various मोक्षधर्मस् are exten-sively detailed (मोक्षधर्माश् च कथिता विचित्रा बहुविस्लराः) 1. 2. 198; related to the अध्यायस् 12. 168-353. Mausala nt.: Name of the 96th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 68, 33, 70; name of the 16th पर्वन् in the list of the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 220, 229. Described as frightful (घोर) 1. 2. 68, (दारुण) 1. 2. 220; in this पर्वन् is described how the great heroes (the Yāda-vas), in a drunken state, crushed by the Brahmadaṇḍa and incited by fate, killed one another near the ocean with the वज्रस् in the form of एरका grass; how Rāma (i. e. Balarāma) and Keśava could not go beyond Time when it arrived (नातिचक्रमतुः कालम् प्राप्तं 1. 2. 222); how Arjuna hav-ing seen the Dvāravatī without the Vṛṣṇis (the Yādavas) was dejected and excessively grieved; he cremated his maternal uncle Śauri (Vasudeva) and saw the great destruction of the Yadus at the drinking party near the ocean (समीपे लवणाम्-भसः । आपाने) 1. 2. 220-224; Arjuna cremated the bodies of Vāsudeva, Rāma and the principal Vṛṣṇis; he then took with him the aged and the children and after leaving Dvāravatī experienced the defeat of this Gāṇḍīva bow in an adverse calamity; he also experienced non-availablity to him of all his heavenly missiles (ददर्शापदि कष्टायाम् गाण्डीवस्य पराभवं ॥ सर्-वेषां चैव दिव्यानाम् अस्त्राणाम् अप्रसन्-नताम् 1. 2. 226-227; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 2. 361.: अप्रसन्नताम् अस्फुरणम्); (on way) the Vṛṣṇi women were lost; having thus realized the transient nature of this powers (नाशं वृष्णिकलत्राणाम् प्रभावानाम् अनित्यताम् । दृष्ट्वा 1. 2. 227-228), Arjuna, overcome by the feeling of disregard for the world and urged by the advice of Vyāsa (निर्वेदम् आपन्नो व्यासवाक्यप्रचोदितः) 1. 2. 228) recommended संन्यास to Dharma-rāja when he met him (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 2. 362: संन्यासं राज्यत्यागम्) 1. 2. 220-228; according to the Parvasaṃgraha, the Mausala parvan has eight अध्यायस् and three hundred श्लोकस् 1. 2. 229.
मघा: Maghā f. (pl.): Name of a नक्षत्र। A. Event: Mythological: Sunda and Upasunda, after performing at night the ceremonies suitable for moving out, marched out under the constellation Maghā for their conquest of the three worlds (कृत्वा प्रास्था-निकं रात्रौ मघासु ययतुस् तदा) 1. 202. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 210. 2: मघासु गमनार्थं निषिद्धे ऽपि नक्षत्रे असुर-त्वाद् ययतुः). B. Importance: A cer-tain तीर्थ named jointly after the Kṛttikā and the Maghā; by visiting this तीर्थ one ob-tained the merit of performing the Agniṣṭoma and the Atirātra sacrifices (कृत्तिकामघयोश् चैव तीर्थम्) 3. 82. 46. C. Omens: (1) Vyāsa told Dhṛtarāṣṭra before the start of the war that a calamity was predicted for the two armies by the planet Mars making retro-grade movement under the Maghā (मघास्व् अङ्गारको वक्रः) 6. 3. 13; (2) Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that rhe armies of the Kauravas gathered for war at Kurukṣetra on the day when the moon entered the Maghā and the seven principal planets, shining, came together in the sky (मघाविषयगः सोमस् तद् दिनं प्रत्यपद्यत । दीप्यमानाश् च संपेतुर् दिवि सप्त महाग्रहाः ॥ ) 6. 17. 2 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 17. 2 has a long com-mentary trying to reconcile the astronomical statements. He does not interpret मघा-विषय as the region of the constellation Maghā but as पितृदेश: मघा पित्रयं नक्-षत्रं तस्य विषयो देशः पितृलोकस् तद्गतः सोमः । … एतेन युद्धारंभं प्रकृत्य ‘मघाविषयगः सोमस् तद् दिनं प्रत्य-पद्यत’ इति भीष्मपर्वणि सञ्जयवाक्यान् मघायां युद्धारंभ इत्य् अपि निरस्तम् ।  … महाग्रहाः राहुकेत्वोर् उपग्रहत्वात् सप्तैव). D. Religious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that by offering plates (? rather ‘heaps’) full of sesame one had many sons and cattle in this life and enjoyed life after death (मघासु तिलपूर्णानि वर्धमानानि मानवः । प्र-दाय पुत्रपशुमान् इह प्रेत्य च मोदते) 13. 63. 12; (2) श्राद्ध: Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under the Maghā (मघासु) one became eminent among kinsmen 13. 89. 5; (3) Bhīṣma recited for Yuḍhiṣṭhira the गाथास् sung by the manes which were recited for him formerly by the venerable Sanatkumāra; according to these गाथास् the manes cherished a wish that some one would be born in their line who would offer to them on the thirteenth day under the Maghā, during the Dakṣiṇāyana, rice boiled in milk, together with clarified butter or meat of red goat, that was fanned, according to the rites, by the (elephant's) ear, under the shadow of an elephant (गाथाश् चाप्य् अत्र गायन्ति पितृगीता युधिष्ठिर । सनत्कुमारो भग-वान् पुरा मय्य् अभ्यभाषत ॥ अपि नः स कुले जायाद् यो नो दद्यात् त्रयो-दशीम् । मघासु सर्पिषा युक्तं पायसं दक्षिणायने ॥ आजेन वापि लौहेन मघास्व् एव यतव्रतः । हस्तिच्छायासु विधिवत् कर्णव्यजनवीजितम् ॥ ) 13. 88. 11-13. (In-terpretation of हस्तिच्छाया as an eclipse in this context is not favoured by the commen-tators on the Manusmṛti; on Manu 3. 274, which has the reading प्राक्छाये कुञ्जरस्य च, Kullūka observes: हस्तिनः पूर्वां दिशं गतायां छायायाम् … न तु त्रयो-दशीहस्तिच्छाययोः समुच्चयः । ; Medhātithi on the same stanza: तथा कुञ्जरस्य हस्तिनः प्राक्छाये प्राच्यां दिशि गतायां छायायाम् अपराण्हेतरे काल इत्य् अर्थः । … यत् तु व्याचक्षते राहूपरागो हस्तिच्छायो-च्यते … तद् अयुक्तम् । ; Rāghavānanda: कुञ्जरस्यैव छाया विवक्षिता न तु योग-विशेषः । कर्णव्यजनवीजितम् इति वाक्यान्-तराच् चेति which latter is an obvious reference to the Mbh. passage).
माघ: Māgha, Māghamāsa m.: Name of a month. A. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 13. 153. 28. B. Epic Event: Bhīṣma, lying on the bed of arrows, realized that the holy month of Māgha had arrived (मासो ऽयं समनुप्राप्तो मासः पुण्यो युधिष्ठिर); he guessed that it must be the eighth day of the bright fortnight of that month (त्रि-भागशेषः पक्षो ऽयं शुक्लो भवितुम् अर्हति) 13. 153. 28 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 167. 28: तेनाद्याष्टमीत्य् अर्थः). C. Religious rites: (1) Vedic: Aśvamedha: when the return of the horse, wandering on the earth, was reported to Yudhiṣṭhira, he, noticing that the day was the twelfth of the (bright) fortnight of the month of Māgha and that the constellation (viz. Puṣya) was favourable, he asked Bhīma to make prepa-rations for the horse sacrifice (एतस्मिन्न् एव काले तु द्वादशीं माघपाक्षिकीम् । इष्टम् गृहीत्वा नक्षत्रं) 14. 86. 4 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 85. 4: इष्टं नक्षत्रं पुष्यम्); (2) Non-Vedic: (a) स्नान: Aṅgiras told Gautama that if one who had controlled his mind and had strictly observed the vows bathed at Prayāga in Māgha he was puri-fied of the sins and went to heaven 13. 26. 36; (b) दान: One who offered sesame to Brāh-maṇas in Māgha did not go to hell 13. 65. 7; (c) उपवास: If one, who is devoted to father (पितृभक्तः), spends the month of Māgha taking food only once a day he becomes eminent in his illustrious family and among his kinsmen (श्रीमत्कुले ज्ञातिमध्ये स महत्त्वं प्रपद्यते) 13. 109. 20. D. Smile: Bhīṣma said that the arrows which pierced his vitals, as (the winter time शैशिरः कालः 6. 113. 7) in the month of Māgha pierced the vitals of cows, were those of Arjuna and not of Śikhaṇḍin (कृन्तन्ति मम गात्राणि माघमासे गवाम् इव । अर्जुनस्य इमे बाणा नेमे बाणाः शिखण्डि-नः) 6. 114. 60 (see the Editor's note on the stanza, Cr. Ed. Vol. 7, p. 795; for the reading माघमा (or मागमा) सेगवाम् इव and the commentator's explanations of it, see the Critical Apparatus on the stanza (p. 677), and for Nī.'s expl. see Bom. Ed. 6. 119. 66). [See Māghī]
माघी: Māghī f.; adj.: The day of full moon in the month of Māgha; of the month of Māgha. A. Importance: Aṅgiras told Gautama that on the Māghī (माघ्याम्) three crores and ten thousand तीर्थस् visit Prayāga 13. 26. 35. B. Auspicious: (1) for Vedic rites: Yudhi-ṣṭhira asked his brothers to make prepara-tions for the Aśvamedha since the roaming horse had returned and the day was the full moon of the month of Māgha (अभितो वर्-तते हयः । माघी च पौर्णमासीयम्) 14. 86. 8; (2) for non-Vedic rites: (a) The sages, Aṅgiras and others, while on a तीर्थयात्रा, went to the holy river Kauśikī on the Māghī (माघ्याम्) 13. 96. 6 (for the river Kauśiki see the Editor's note on 13. 3. 10, Cr. Ed. Vol. 17, part II, p. 1054); (b) On every Māghī (as well as on the Āṣāḍhi) Virūpākṣa, the king of the Rākṣasas used to give excellent and well-garnished food, as desired, to the Brāhmaṇas (तस्य (i. e. of Virūpākṣa) नित्यं तथाषाष्ह्यां माघ्यां च बहवो द्विजाः । ईप्सितं भोज-नवरं लभन्ते सत्कृतं सदा ॥ ) 12. 165. 15. [See Māgha]
मार्गशीर्ष: Mārgaśīrṣa m.: Name of a month. A. Importance: Bhagavān, while describing his विभूतिस् to Arjuna, said that he was the Mārgaśīrṣa among the months (मासानां मार्गशीर्षो ऽहम्) 6. 32. 35. B. Religious rites: उपवास: Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira that one who spent the month of Mārgaśirṣa taking food only once a day and fed the twice-born with devotion would be freed from diseases and sins; he would also be born enjoying all blessings, possess-ing all medicinal herbs, reaping good harvest, wealthy, and would have many sons (सर्व-कल्याणसंपूर्णः सर्वौषधिसमन्वितः । कृषिभागी बहुधनो बहुपुत्रश् च जायते) 13. 109. 18.
मार्गशीर्षी: Mārgaśīrṣī f.: The full moon day of the month of Mārgaśirṣa. A. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas, toge-ther with Dhaumya and other forest dwellers, started on their pilgrimage from the Kāmyaka forest under the constellation Puṣya when the full moon day of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa had passed (मार्गशीर्ष्याम् अतीतायां पुष्येण प्रययुस् ततः) 3. 91. 25. B. Proper time for army manoeuvre: Marching out of the army for attack on the full moon day of the month of Caitra or of Mārgaśīrṣa is recommended since the crops the are ripe and water is ample; it is then also neither too hot nor too cold 12. 101. 9-10 (for the citation, see above Caitrī, p. 246. 1).
मूल: Mūla m., nt.: Name of a constellation. Religious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that by giving as a gift with composed mind (समाहितः) roots and fruits to the Brāhmaṇas under the con-stellation Mūla (मूले मूलफलं दत्त्वा) one delights the manes, and gets the desired state after death (गतिम् इष्टां च गच्छति) 13. 63. 24; (2) श्राद्ध: Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under the Mūla one becomes healthy (मूले त्व् आरोग्यम् अर्च्छेत) 13. 89. 10.
म्र्गोत्तम: Mrgottama nt.: Name of the constella-tion Mṛgaśiras; also called Tārāmṛga (m.) (3. 262. 19) and Somadaivata (13. 63. 7). A. Religious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that those who gave as a gift a milch cow with a calf under the constellation Somadaivata (नक्षत्रे सोमदैवते) went to the excellent heaven from the world of mortals (गच्छन्ति मानु-षाल् लोकात् स्वर्गलोकम् अनुत्तमम्) 13. 63. 7 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 64. 7: सौम्य-नक्षत्रे मृगशिरसि); (2) श्राद्ध: Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that one desirous of vigour should offer a श्राद्ध under the constellation Mṛgottama (ओजस्कामो मृगोत्-तमे) 13. 89. 3 (Unknown commentator: मृगोत्तमे मृगशिरसि, cf. Editor's note on the stanza Cr. Ed. Vol. 17, p. 1090). B. Simile: Rāma ran after the deer as did Rudra after the Tārāmṛga (अन्वधावन् मृगं रामो रुद्रस् तारामृगं यथा) 3. 262. 19 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 278. 20: तारामृगं तारारूपं मृगम् … तद् एतन् मृगशीर्षं नाम नक्षत्रम्).
मैत्र: Maitra1 nt.: Name of the constellation Anurādhā. Balarāma, angered, left for the तीर्थयात्रा on the river Sarasvatī under the sun's con-junction with Maitra (ततो मन्युपरीतात्मा जगाम … । तीर्थयात्रां हलधरः सरस्-वत्यां महायशाः । मैत्रे नक्षत्रयोगे स्म … ॥ ) 9. 34. 12 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 9. 35. 14 मैत्रनक्षत्रयोगे अनुराधायाम्; see Puṣya1 B (4) above p. 256; however, see the Editor's note on this stanza: “There is no real inconsistency between this passage on the one hand and 9. 33. 5 and 9. 34. 14 on the other. The latter evidently refer to the Nakṣatra (that is, Puṣya) occupied by the moon, while मैत्रे नक्षत्रयोगे refers to the sun's conjunction with the Nakṣatra Maitra (= Anurādhā)” Cr. Ed. Vol. 11, p. 489). [See Anurādhā]

Maitra2 m.: Name of a मुहूर्त। On the day when Kṛṣṇa wanted to go to Hāstinapura he woke up and finished his early morning rites when sun rose and the Maitra Muhūrta had set in (सूर्ये विमल उद्गते । मैत्रे मुहूर्ते संप्राप्ते । … कृत्वा पौर्-वाण्हिकं कृत्यम्) 5. 81. 6, 9 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 5. 83. 6: मैत्रे जन्मर्क्षाद् अष्टमतारायाम् दूतस्य हि स्वामिबलेनैव बलवत्त्वम् इत्य् अर्थः).
मकरवाहिनी: Makaravāhinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 32, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
मञ्जु: Mañju f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 32, 13 (for other details see Makaravāhinī above).
मणिजला: Maṇijalā f.: Name of a river. A river of the Śākadvīpa 6. 12. 30; all the rivers of this Dvīpa contain holy water (पुण्यजलाः) 6. 12. 29, (पुण्योदाः) 6. 12. 31, are holy (पुण्याः) and excellent rivers (सरिद्वराः) 6. 12. 32.
मणिनाग: Maṇināga m.: Name of a holy place. Sacred to a serpent called Maṇināga (?); by visiting the place one obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 82. 91; by living there for a night one is freed of all sins 3. 82. 92; one who eats the food offered to Maṇināga is not affected by the poison even when bitten by a venomous snake (नैत्यकं भुञ्जते यस् तु मणिनागस्य मानवः । दष्टस्याशीविषेणापि न तस्य क्रमते विषम् ॥ ) 3. 82. 91-92 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 105: नित्यकं नैवेद्यं नैत्यकं च तद् एव).
मतङ्गवापी: Mataṅgavāpī f.: Name of a sacred tank. Sacred to the sage Mataṅga; one who bathes there obtains perfection (सिद्धि) in one night, and can dive, even without support, in the eternal Andhaka world (? मतङ्गवाप्यां यः स्नायाद् एकरात्रेण सिध्यति । विगाहति ह्य् अनालम्बम् अन्धकं वै सनातनम् ॥ ) 13. 26. 31 (Comm. unknown, however, अन्ध-कं तीर्थम् अनालम्बं शववद् यो विगाहति स सनातनं नित्यस्थानं लभेत इति शेषः । He also explains some other readings Cr. Ed. Vol. 17, p. 1067, note on 13. 26. 31).
मतङ्गस्य: Mataṅgasya kedāraḥ m.: Name of a sacred place. Sacred to the sage Mataṅga, it was locat-ed on the mountain Mahendra 3. 83. 14-15; 3. 85. 16; also known as Mataṅgasya Āśramaḥ 3. 85. 19; described as sanctifying (पवित्र), auspicious (मङ्गलीय), famous in the world (ख्यातो लोके) and eternal (सनातन) 3. 85. 19; by bathing there one obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 83. 15.

Mataṅgasya āśramaḥ m.: An आश्रम of Mataṅga. A. Location: In the east (पूर्वं प्राचीं दिशं … कीर्तयिष्यामि) 3. 85. 3. B. Description: Sanctifying (पवित्र), auspicious (मङ्गलीय), known in the world (ख्यातो लोके), ancient (सनातन), great (महन्त्), best (उत्तम) 3. 85. 19. C. Special feature: Mataṅga had his field there (केदारश् च मतङ्गस्य) 3. 85. 19.
मदर्वीक: Madarvīka m.: Name of a mountain. The mountain, along with the lands bordering on it, was conquered by Bhīma in his expedition before the Rājasūya; from there he went northwards (मदर्वीकं महीधरं । सोपदेशं विनिर्जित्य प्रय-याव् उत्तारामुखः) 2. 27. 9.
मधुवटी: Madhuvaṭī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। It was sacred to Devī (देव्यास् तीर्थम्); one who has a controlled mind and is pure (प्रयतः शुचिः) if he bathes there and wor-ships gods and manes (अर्चयेद् देवान् पितॄंश् च) he gets, with the consent of the Devī (देव्या समनुज्ञातः) the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 81. 79.
मधुवन: Madhuvana nt.: Name of a forest. Described as dense (स्फीत) and large (महत्); it was first protected by Vālin and then by Sugrīva; Hanūmant, Aṅgada and others who went to the south in search of Sītā, rested there for a while on their return journey 3. 266. 26-27.
मधुविला: Madhuvilā f.: Name of a river, also called Samaṃgā. Situated near Kardamila, the bathing place of Bharata; it was pointed out to Yudhiṣṭhira by Lomaśa (एषा मधुविला राजन् समंगा संप्रकाशते) 3. 135. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 135. 1: मधुविलेति अष्टावक्रा-ङ्गसमीकरणात् पूर्वं समङ्गाया एवं नाम); Indra lost his lustre after killing Vṛtra (अलक्ष्म्या किल संयुक्तो वृत्रं हत्वा शचीपतिः); he was freed from all sins when he bathed in the river Samaṃgā 3. 135. 2.
मधुस्रव: Madhusrava nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Pṛthūdaka तीर्थ; by bathing there one gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 81. 130.
मनोजव: Manojava nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the Vyāsavana; one who has a controlled mind and takes limited food (नियतो नियताशनः) if he bathes there he gets the fruit of giving a thousand cows 3. 81. 78.
मनोह्रदा: Manohradā f.: Name of one of the seven forms of Sarasvatī (सप्त सरस्व-त्यः); also called Mānasahradā (9. 37. 4). Described as the best of the rivers (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा) 9. 37. 23; when Auddālaka performed a sacrifice in the Uttara Kosala country he thought of Sarasvatī; the river came to that region for the sake of the sage and was worshipped by the sages; the river was there known as Manohradā; the river was so called because it was brought there by the mind of the sages (मनोह्रदेति विख्याता सा हि तैर् मनसा हृता) 9. 37. 21-23.
मन्दगा: Mandagā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 31, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
मन्दर: Mandara m.: Name of a mountain; also referred to as Mahāmandara (7. 57. 29). A. Location: (1) In the north (अस्यां दिशि … उत्तरायां 5. 109. 3.) 5. 109. 9; 13. 20. 28; beyond the Uśīrabīja, the Maināka and the Śveta mountains 3. 140. 1; close to the Śvetagiri (श्वेतं गिरिं प्रवेक्ष्यामो मन्दरं चैव पर्वतम्) 3. 140. 4; the river Śailodā flows between the Meru and the Mandara 2. 48. 2; (2) Mandara covers the entire earth up to the ocean in the east (प्राचीं दिशम् … असौ सागरपर्यन्तां भूमिं आवृत्य तिष्ठति) 3. 160. 3-4; (3) The root of the Himavant reaches in the west (cf. 5. 108. 1-2) eternally up to the Mandara mountain so deep that one cannot reach its end even after a thousand years (अत्र मूलं हिमवतो मन्दरं याति शाश्वतम् । अपि वर्षसहस्रेण न चास्यान्तो ऽधिगम्यते) 5. 108. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 110. 9: मन्दरं समुद्रे मग्नं एतेन हिमवन्मूलस्य समुद्रजलस्य चाप्रमेयत्वम् उक्तम्). B. Descrip-tion: (1) Excellent mountain (पर्वत-वर) 1. 16. 1; (शैलवर) 3. 99. 14; (2) big mountain (महाद्रि) 1. 16. 19; (महा-शैल) 3. 43. 24; 13. 20. 29; (महामन्दर) 7. 57. 29; eleven thousand योजनस् high (above the earth), and established the same number of योजनस् deep below the earth 1. 16. 3; all the gods together could not lift it 1. 16. 4; but king Duḥṣanta was capable of lifting it with its forest and carry it on his arms (उद्यम्य मन्दरं दोर्भ्यां हरेत् स-वनकाननम्) 1. 62. 11; (3) King of mountains (पर्वतराजन्) 1. 16. 7; (शैल-राज) 3. 43. 21; 3. 160. 4; (अद्रिराज) 3. 43. 24; (4) Adorned with summits which were like towering clouds (अभ्रशिखराकारैर् गिरिः शृङ्गैर् अलंकृतम्) 1. 16. 1; its peaks were formed of gold and silver (हेमरूप्य-मयैः शृङ्गैः) 7. 57. 26; (5) Its caves were attractive (चारुकन्दर) 3. 220. 22; (6) Full of तीर्थस् (तीर्थवन्त्) 3. 43. 24; (7) Covered with the network of creepers (लताजालसमावृत) 1. 16. 1; (8) Resound-ing with sounds of many birds (नानाविहग-संघुष्ट) 1. 16. 2; (9) Beset with many tusked animals (नानादंष्ट्रिसमाकुल) 1. 16. 2 (10) Resorted to by the Kiṃnaras, the Apsarases, and even by gods 1. 16. 2; 7. 57. 29; (11) Resort of sages (मुनि-संश्रय) 3. 43. 24; (also see the next section C). C. Characteristics: (1) The Meru and the Mandara mountains adorn the earth (मेरुमन्दरभूषणां … वसुन्ध-राम्) 3. 187. 10; the sun circles untiringly round the Meru and returns to the Mandara (in the east to start his course the next day) (एवम् एव परिक्रम्य महामेरुम् अतन्द्रि-तः । … पुनर् गच्छति मन्दरम्) 3. 160. 28; (2) Mandara is the place of Śaṅkara (शङ्करस्थानम्); Śaṅkara lives there; un-less one goes to the Mandara one cannot see Śiva 7. 69. 55-56; (3) Yakṣa Māṇicara and Kubera, the king of the Yakṣas, live there; thousands of Gandharvas, Kiṃpuruṣas and Yakṣas, having varied forms and equipped with different weapons, wait upon Māṇibhadra, the lord of the Yakṣas (यक्षेन्द्रं … माणि-भद्रम् उपासते) 3. 140. 4-6; in the bowers of Mandara the Gandharvas sing गाथास् which enchant one's mind and intelligence (अत्र मन्दरकुञ्जेषु … । गन्धर्वा गान्ति गाथा वै चित्तबुद्धिहराः) 5. 107. 9; the regions of the Mandara resound with songs of the Kiṃnaras 7. 57. 26; (4) The regions of the Mandara were illuminated by the different kinds of herbs and by its gold and silver peaks (हेमरूप्यमयैः शृङ्गैर् नानौषधिविदीपितान्); they were also adorn-ed by blossoming Mandāra trees 7. 57. 26; (5) The mountain is one of those which are looked upon as difficult of access (दुर्-गमाः पर्वताः) 3. 140. 8; (6) Mandara was the place of resort of the pious sages who longed for heaven; by the grace of the Mandara, the Brāhmaṇas, the Kṣatriyas, and the Vaiśyas reach heaven and live there with gods, free from distress 3. 43. 22, 23; (7) The mountain had many peaks, bowers, rivers streams and many holy तीर्थस् on it (तव सानूनि कुञ्जांश् च नद्यः प्रस्रवणानि च । तीर्थानि च सुपुण्यानि) 3. 43. 25; (8) Various tribes like the Khaśas, the Ekāśanājyohas (? एकाशना ज्योहाः ?), the Pradaras, the Dīrghaveṇus, the Paśupas, the Kuṇindas, the Taṅgaṇas and the Parataṅgaṇas lived there 2. 48. 3. D. Epic events: (1) At the time of the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest a huge peak of the Mandara mountain was uprooted by Indra and hurled, along with trees on it, at Arjuna 1. 218. 47; (2) The tribes living along the Śailodā river flowing between Meru and Mandara brought tributes of various kinds to Yudhiṣṭhira for his Rājasūya 2. 48. 2-5; (3) Arjuna, in the company of Mātali, started from this mountain for his journey to Indraloka; while taking leave of the mountain, Arjuna said that he had lived there happily and had seen there many peaks, bowers, rivers and holy तीर्थस् 3. 43. 21, 24, 25; (4) Lomaśa pointed out Mandara to Yudhiṣṭhira as they were about to enter it after crossing the Uśīrabīja, the Maināka, the Śveta and the Kālaśaila 3. 140. 1, 4; (5) Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa saw the mountain Mandara on their way while they were going to the Kailāsa 7. 57. 26, 29. E. Mythological and past events: (1) When gods were advised by the god Nārāyaṇa to churn the great Kalaśodadhi (1. 15. 11-12), they went to the Mandara but could not lift it (for using it as a churning rod) 1. 16. 1, 4; then, at the bidding of Brahman, the serpent Ananta lifted it for them 1. 16. 5-7; when gods took it to the ocean and told it that they wanted to churn the ocean for अमृत, the ocean asked for a share in it as it would bear the pounding by the Mandara 1. 16. 8-9; gods then requested Akūpāra, the king of tortoises, to offer support to the mountain; it agreed and then Indra fixed the top of the mountain on the tortoise with some mechanism (तस्य शैलस्य चाग्रं वै यन्त्रेणेद्रो ऽभ्यपीडयत्); gods then started churning the ocean using Man-dara as the churning rod 1. 16. 10-12; from the top of the mountain showers of flowers fell on gods and demons and there arose a loud noise as the ocean was being churned; the great mountain crushed many acquatic creatures and they perished by hundreds; the mountain destroyed many creatures belonging to Varuṇa who lived in Pātāla; huge trees, as they rubbed against each, other, fell down, together with the birds on them, from the top of the mountain when the ocean was being churned; fire which arose due to the rubbing of the trees engulfed the Mandara mountain; the fire burnt elephants, lions and other creatures (on the mountain) 1. 16. 17-23; when gods were tired, Viṣṇu gave them strength and exhorted them to agitate the Kalaśa ocean by rotating Mandara 1. 16. 31; when at the end gods got victory over demons they honoured the mountain and replaced it on its original site 1. 17. 29; the water of the ocean which was churned by gods and demons using Mandara as a churning rod was mixed with the milk of four cows, the daughters of Surabhi, who guarded the four directions (आसां तु पयसा मिश्रं पयो निर्मथ्य सागरे) 5. 100. 11, (1, 7); (2) When gods, led by Indra, were defeated by Vṛtra they sat down on the top of the mountain Mandara and prayed to Viṣṇu; thereupon Viṣṇu showed them the way 5. 9. 52, (5. 10. 6-13); (3) In another version, Viṣṇu advised gods, Indra and the rest, to go to Mandara to see Śiva; only then they would be able to kill their enemy (Vṛtra); then gods, together with Brahman, went to Mandara and saw Śiva there 7. 69. 56; (4) When Śiva's chariot was assembled for his fight with the three sons of Tāraka, riding the त्रिपुरस्, Mandara was made the axle of the chariot (मन्दरं पर्वतं चाक्षम्) 8. 24. 69; (5) Viṣṇu once hurled Mandara (against his enemy) 3. 99. 14; (6) As directed by Vadānya, Aṣṭāvakra, in his journey towards the north to meet the old female ascetic, came across mountains Kailāsa, Mandara, and Haima, and he went beyond them (सर्वान् अनुचचार ह ॥ तान् अतीत्य महाशैलान्) 13. 20. 28-29; (7) Nahuṣa, after he became the king of heaven, sported with the Apsarases and the Deva-kanyās on mountain Kailāsa, Himavant, Mandara and Śveta 5. 11. 9; (8) Mārka-ṇḍeya saw, among other mountains, Mandara in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārā-yaṇa 3. 187. 4) 3. 186. 103. F. Impor-tance: Finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2. G. Bad omen related to it: Among the bad omens noticed by Vyāsa before the war mention is made of the falling down of the summits of the mountains Kailāsa, Mandara and Himavant 6. 3. 35. H. Similes: (1) Hanūmant assumed a form as huge as Vindhya and Mandara 3. 149. 10; (2) The golden moun-tain with Skanda on it shone like Mandara with the sun having a circle of rays around it 3. 220. 22; (3) Karṇa with his arrows in his chariot appeared like Mandara with the sun full of rays 8. 26. 15; (4) The towers on the gates of Indraprastha were (huge) like Mandara (गोपुरैर् मन्दरोपमैः) 1. 199. 31; (5) The वज्र was hurled by Indra at Vṛtra as Mandara was hurled by Viṣṇu 3. 99. 14.

Mandara m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the fourteenth day of war, Man-dara warriors were among those three thousand horse-riders who, led by Duryo-dhana, attacked Sātyaki (त्रीणि सादिसह-स्राणि दुर्योधनपुरोगमाः । अभ्यद्र-वन्त शैनेयम्) 7. 97. 13-14. [For Man-dara mountain see Vol. I, pp. 403-405].
मन्दवाहिनी: Mandavāhinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 31, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
मन्दाकिनी: Mandākinī1 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 33, 13; on the Citrakūṭa mountain in the Janasthāna 13. 26. 27; 3. 83. 55. B. Description: Des-cribed as a river that frees one from sins (पापप्रमोचनी) 3. 83. 55; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Holiness: (1) By bathing there and by being engaged in worshipping gods and manes (तत्राभिषेकः कुर्वाणः पितृदेवार्चने रतः) one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and the highest state (after death) (गतिं च परमां व्रजेत्) 3. 83. 56; (2) One who fasts and bathes there obtains royal glory (विगाह्य वै निरा-हारो राजलक्ष्मीं निगच्छति) 13. 26. 27. D. Importance: Finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 17, 2.

Mandākinī2 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: In the north 13. 20. 2, 36; 5. 109. 3, 9; (13. 19. 14); on the mountain Himavant, near Kailāsa 13. 20. 2, 6-7, and near the mountain Mandara 5. 109. 9; near the residence of the old female ascetic (who was really the northern direction 13. 22. 4) 13. 20. 36 [See also E (1) below]. B. Relationship: It belongs to Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera) 13. 105. 18; 13. 20. 7. C. Des-cription: (1) Full of Mandāra flowers (मन्दारपुष्पैः संकीर्णा) 13. 20. 36; (2) It has great enjoyments (महाभोगा), and as such is fit to be entered by those who are devoted to enjoyments (भोगिजनप्र-वेश्या), and is liked by the Gandharvas, the Yakṣas and the Apsarases (गन्धर्वयक्-षैर् अप्सरोभिश् च जुष्टा) 13. 105. 18. D. Holiness: Those who consider hospita-lity as a vow, who observe (other) vows, who give shelter to Brāhmaṇas, and who eat the remainder (of the food) after serving it to the dependents—such people adorn the Mandākinī (अतिथिव्रता सुव्रता ये जना वै प्रतिश्रयं ददति ब्राह्मणेभ्यः । शिष्टा-शिनः संविभज्याश्रितांश् च मन्दाकिनीं ते ऽपि विभूषयन्ति) 13. 105. 19. E. Past events: (1) Aṣṭāvakra, in his journey to the north to meet the old female ascetic (13. 19. 24), came across the river Mandā-kinī 13. 20. 7; Aṣṭāvakra saw Mandākinī in a beautiful forest spot further to the north (13. 20. 28) of the residence of Kubera, and arrived at it when he crossed the Kailāsa, the Mandara, the Haima and the Kairāta-sthāna 13. 20. 28-29, 31, 36; (2) The Brāh-maṇa Gautama offered to take the crocodile named Dhṛtarāṣṭra (who was really Indra) to the river Mandākinī in lieu of his elephant that was snatched by the crocodile 13. 105. 6, 18. [See Vasor dhārā2]

Mandākinī3 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Flowing high up in the mid-region (ततो मन्दाकिनीम् … उपरिष्टाद् … ददर्श) 12. 320. 16. B. Description: Charming (रम्या); having forests of flower-ing trees (on its banks) (पुष्पितद्रुम-कानना) 12. 320. 16. C. Characteristic: Apsarases sport and bathe there (तस्यां क्रीडन्त्य् अभिरताः स्नान्ति चैवाप्सरोगणाः) 12. 320. 17, 28. D. Past event: In his upward journey through the space Śuka saw Mandākinī when he went through the two peaks of the mountains Himavant and Meru which were torn asunder; the mountain could no longer check his gait 12. 320. 16, 8-11; when Vyāsa followed his son Śuka flying up (उत्तमां गतिम् आस्थाय) and reached the mountain peaks rent asunder by Śuka he sat down on the slope of the mountain think-ing about his son (निषसाद गिरिप्रस्थे); he saw there Apsarases sporting on the bank of Mandākinī; they were all confused and lost their senses when they saw the sage (आसाद्य तम् ऋषिं सर्वाः संभ्रान्ता गत-चेतसः) 12. 320. 18, 27-28. [See Vasor dhārā2]
मरुतां: Marutāṃ Tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। [See Pavanasya hradaḥ]
मरुद्गण: Marudgaṇa m., nt. (?): Name of a तीर्थ। A person by bathing at this तीर्थ is purified and himself becomes a तीर्थ (मरु-द्गण उपस्पृश्य … शुचिः … तीर्थभूतो भवेन् नरः ॥ ) 13. 26. 37.
मलदा: Maladā f.: Name of a river. One should proceed to this river from the Vimalatīrtha 3. 80. 103, 105; described as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुताम्) 3. 80. 105; one should bathe in it in the evening twilight according to the pre-scribed rites and offer a चरु according to one's mite in the fire having seven flames; such an offering to manes is considered to be inexhaustible (पश्चिमायां तु संध्यायाम् उपस्पृश्य यथाविधि ॥ चरुं नरेन्द्र सप्तार्चेर् यथाशक्ति निवेदयेत् । पितॄणाम् अक्षयं दानं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥ ) 3. 80. 105-106; offering such a चरु is more meritorious than gifting a hundred thousand cows, than a hundred Rājasūya sacrifices, and a thousand Aśvamedha sacrifices 3. 80. 107.
मलवासस्: Malavāsas f.: Name of a river. Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa (मलवासाश् च नद्य् अपि) 13. 151. 20, 2.
महत्सरस्: Mahatsaras, Mahāsaras nt.: Name of a holy lake. Those high-souled ones who visit this lake (प्रभासं मानसं पुण्यं पुष्क-राणि महत्सरः । … ये प्रयान्ति 13. 105. 45, 47) become auspicious, assume heavenly form, wear heavenly garlands, and full of holy fragrance they reach the Goloka (? मोदन्ति गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44) 13. 105. 45, 48 (for citation see Karatoyinī); one who visits Mahāsaras shall again get life in this life (?) (महासरः … गन्तासि लब्धायुर्जीविते पु-नः) 12. 148. 11.
महद्द्युमन्: Mahaddyuman nt.: Name of a sacred place. According to one of the stanzas in praise of the Nāgas, recited by Uttaṅka, the youngest brother of Takṣaka, known as Śrutasena, lived at Mahaddyuman praying to become the chief of the Nāgas (जघन्यजस् तक्षकस्य श्रुतसेनेति यः श्रुतः । अवसद् यो महद्-द्युम्नि प्रार्थयन् नागमुख्यताम् ॥ ) 1. 3. 146 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 1. 3. 142: महद्युम्नि तीर्थविशेष इति प्राञ्चः । म-हद्युम्नि सूर्ये तत्समीपे नागमुख्यतां प्रार्थयन् कुरुक्षेत्र ऽवसद् इति पूर्वेण संबन्धः कुरुक्षेत्रवासमात्राद् एव महत् स्थानं प्राप्यत इत्य् आशयः । ).
महाकाल: Mahākāla m.: Name of a holy place sacred to Śiva. One should reach there from Yayāti-patana; the Koṭitīrtha is situated there 3. 80. 68.
महाक्रौञ्च: Mahākrauñca m.: Name of a mountain of the Krauñcadvīpa. Located in the Krauñcadvīpa; it is a mine of heaps of jewels (रत्नचयाकरः); it is always worshipped by people of the four castes (संपूज्यते महाराज चातुर्-वर्ण्येन नित्यदा) 6. 13. 7.
महागङ्गा: Mahāgaṅgā f.: Name of a river. According to the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras to Gautama (13. 26. 3-4) one who bathes in the Mahāgaṅgā at the junction of the Kṛttikās with the Mars and observes fast for a fortnight becomes pure and goes to heaven (महागङ्गाम् उपस्पृश्य कृत्तिका-ङ्गारके तथा । पक्षम् एकम् निराहारः स्वर्गम् आप्नोति निर्मलः ॥ ) 13. 26. 20.
महागिरि: Mahāgiri m.: Name of a mountain. After visiting Dhārā and after paying homage to Mahāgiri (महागिरिं नमस्-कृत्य) one should go to Gaṅgādvāra 3. 82. 23.
महागौरी: Mahāgaurī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 32, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇa).
महानद: Mahānada m.: Name of a river (or an epithet of Lohitya ?). Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa (लोहित्यश् च महानदः) 13. 151. 16, 2.
महानदि: Mahānadi1 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 26, 13; in the east (प्राचीं दिशम् अभिप्रेप्सुः 1. 207. 5) 1. 207. 7; 3. 85. 3; near Gayā, Gayāśiras and Brahmaśiras (महानदी च तत्रैव) 3. 85. 8; (पुण्या चैव महानदी) 3. 93. 10. B. Description: Described as holy (पुण्या) 3. 93. 10; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Epic event: Arjuna, during his exile, came across the Mahānadī while he was proceeding towards the east 1. 207. 7, 5. D. Past event: One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95. E. Holiness: By bathing (उपस्पृश्य) in this river and by satisfying manes and gods (by giving offerings to them) one gets imperishable worlds and rescues his family (अक्षयान् प्राप्नुयाल् लोकान् कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत्) 3. 82. 73. F. Impor-tance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 15, 2.
महानदी: Mahānadī2 f.: Name of a river of the Śākadvīpa. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Śākadvīpa 6. 12. 30; all the rivers of the Śākadvīpa contain holy water (पुण्यजलाः) 6. 12. 29, (पुण्योदाः) 6. 12. 31; all of them are holy and excellent rivers (पुण्यास् ता हि सरिद्वराः) 6. 12. 32; Vāsava (Indra) gives rain after collecting water from these rivers (यतो वर्षति वासवः) 6. 12. 31.

Mahānadī3 f. (sg., pl.): Epithet of certain rivers. (1) When Śiva's chariot was made ready for his fight with demons who fought from the Tripuras, the Mahānadī's were made its hind parts (जङ्घास् तस्य महानदीः) 8. 24. 69 (by Mahānadīs (pl.) are probably meant rivers like Kuśadhārā, Gaṅgā, Car-maṇvatī, Pūrṇāśā, Bāhudā2, Yamunā, Vadhū-sarā, Vandanā, which are described as ‘great rivers’); (2) When Pāṇḍu with his two wives went to the north beyond the Śataśṛṅga mountain, he saw the regions of the king of mountains and banks of big rivers (महा-नदीनितम्बान्) 1. 111. 5-7; (3) Just as a person who knows the other bank is not afflicted while crossing a big river so are those who know the highest knowledge (महानदीं हि पारज्ञस् तप्यते न तरन् यथा । एवं ये विदुः … ज्ञानम् उत्तमम्) 12. 187. 53.
महानन्दा: Mahānandā f.: Name of a river. One who is controlled (दान्तः) and who does not cause injury to others (अहिंसकः) if he visits the Mahānandā (महानन्दां च सेव्य वै) he is served by the Apsarases in the Nandana forest 13. 26. 42.
महापगा: Mahāpagā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 27, 13 (for other details see Mahānadī1, section B).
महापुर: Mahāpura nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who bathes (उपस्पृश्य) in this तिर्थ and fasts for three nights has no fear from living (lit. moving) beings and non-moving objects and from bipeds (त्रसानां स्थावराणां च द्विपदानां भयं त्यजेत्) 13. 26. 24 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 26: त्रसानां जङ्गमानाम्).
महालय: Mahālaya m.: Name of a sacred place. By staying at Mahālaya for a month and by taking food only in the evening of every third day (षष्ठकालोपवासेन) one is freed of all sins and gets much gold (विन्द्याद् बहु सुवर्णकम्) 3. 82. 49.
महाशङ्ख: Mahāśaṅkha m.: Name of a tree. A. Location: On the bank of the river Sarasvatī (महाशङ्खम् … सरस्वत्यास् तटे जातं नगम्) 9. 36. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 9. 37. 21: नगं वृक्षम्); near the Śaṅkha-tīrtha 9. 36. 19-20. B. Description: Lordly tree (वनस्पतिः) 9. 36. 22, 24; as high as the mountain Mahāmeru (महा-मेरुम् इवोच्छ्रितम्) 9. 36. 20; looking like the Śveta mountain (श्वेतपर्वतसंकाशम्) 9. 36. 20; resorted to by sages (ऋषिसंघैर् निषेवितम्) 9. 36. 20. C. Characteristic: Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, Rākṣasas, Piśācas and Siddhas give up taking food there and eat only the fruit of that tree at proper intervals observing certain vows and rules; they then move about separately observing these regu-lations and are unseen by men; the tree was renowned for this (ते सर्वे ह्य् अशनं त्यक्त्वा फलं तस्य वनस्पतेः । व्रतैश् च नियमैश् चैव काले काले स्म भूञ्जते ॥ प्राप्तैश् च नियमैस् तैस् तैर् विचरन्तः पृथक् पृथक् । अदृश्यमाना मनुजैर् व्य-चरन् पुरुषर्षभ ॥ एवं ख्यातो नर-पते लोके ऽस्मिन् स वनस्पतिः) 9. 36. 21-24.
महाह्रद: Mahāhrada nt.: Name of a तीर्थ (13. 151. 23). A. Location: On the Bhṛgutuṅga moun-tain 13. 26. 17. B. Description: Ex-cellent among all तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थवर) 3. 82. 125. C. Holiness: (1) By stay-ing at this तीर्थ one does not meet with bad condition and gets much gold (यो वसेत महाह्रदे । न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नोति विन्देद् बहु सुवर्णकम्) 3. 82. 125; (2) By bathing in the lake one has done one's duty and becomes pure (अत्र स्नातः कृतकृत्यो विशुद्धः) 3. 113. 25; (3) According to the Tīrthavaṃśa proclaimed by Aṅgiras (13. 26. 3), one who is free from desire (अलोलुपः) if he bathes (उपस्पृश्य) in the lake and fasts for three nights he is freed from the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa (मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया) 13. 26. 17; (4) According to the same authority one who has a pure mind, if he bathes (उपस्पृश्य) there and fasts for a month he gets the condition obtained by Jamadagni (जमदग्निगतिं लभेत्) 13. 26. 45; (5) The high-souled ones who visit the Mahāhrada become auspi-cious and assuming a heavenly form, wear-ing heavenly garlands and becoming rich in fragrance, they reach the world of the cows (? मोदन्ति गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44) 13. 105. 46, 48 (for citation see Karatoyinī). D. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa (तीर्थं महाह्रदम्) 13. 151. 23, 2. E. Epic event: Lomaśa advised Yudhiṣṭhira to bathe in this lake and then proceed to other तीर्थस् 3. 113. 25. F. Past event: Sage Kāśyapa practised austerities at this lake; once while he was bathing in the lake (अप्सूपस्पृशतः) he happened to see Apsaras Urvaśī; his semen spilled in water which was drunk by a female deer; Ṛṣyaśṛṅga was born at this lake from this female deer 3. 110. 12-16; the holy her-mitage of Ṛṣyaśṛṅga adorned the Mahāhrada (तस्याश्रमः पुण्य एषो विभाति महाह्र-दं शोभयन्) 3. 113. 25.
महिता: Mahitā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 20, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
महिरोही: Mahirohī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 29, 13; (for other details see Mahitā).
मही: Mahī f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Mārkaṇḍeya; all these rivers are famous as mothers of fire-hearths i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed 3. 212. 22 (for citation and Nī. see Kapilā).
महीधर: Mahīdhara m.: Name of a sacred moun-tain. Situated near Gayaśiras and the holy river Mahānadī 3. 93. 10; it was honoured by the virtuous royal sage Gaya who knew the धर्म (धर्मज्ञेनाभिसत्कृतम् । राजर्षिणा पुण्यकृता गयेन) 3. 93. 9; the Pāṇḍavas visited it 3. 93. 9.
महेन्द्र: Mahendra m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: In the east, beyond the Kaliṅgas, near the sea coast 1. 207. 5, 12-13 (समुद्रतीरेण); 3. 85. 3; 12. 2. 17, (समुद्रान्ते) 19. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) and auspicious (शिव) 3. 85. 16; excellent mountain, surpassing other moun-tains (गिरिवर, अत्य् अन्यान् पर्वतान्) 3. 85. 16, (पर्वतोत्तम) 1. 58. 4; 12. 2. 17; (गिरिश्रेष्ठ) 5. 175. 2; (शैलेन्द्र) 3. 117. 14; one of the mountains called ‘king of mountains’ (पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 5; adorned by ascetics (तापसैर् उपशोभितम्) 1. 207. 13; having shining Karṇikāra trees on it (शुभकर्णिकारवन्त्) 8. 66. 39. C. Characteristics: (1) Bhārgava Rāma Jāma-dagnya lived on the Mahendra (गिरिवरः … । महेन्द्रो नाम … भार्गवस्य महात्म-नः) 3. 85. 16; (जामदग्न्यनिषेवितम्) 3. 83. 14; he was there waited upon by seers who knew the Vedas, the Gandharvas and the Apsarases (महेन्द्रे … रामं नित्यम् उपासते । ऋषयो वेदविदुषो गन्धर्वाप्स-रसस् तथा) 5. 175. 2; 5. 187. 11; (अस्मिन् महेन्द्रे शैलेन्द्रे वसत्य् अमितविक्रमः जामदग्न्यः) 3. 117. 14, 11; he made it a rule to show himself to the Brāhmaṇas on this mountain on every fourteenth day of the month 3. 117. 16; (2) Mahendra listed by Brahman among mountains which are also to be looked upon as possessing the मध्यम गुण, i. e. they were characterised by the quality of रजस् ? 14. 43. 5, 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुण-प्रधानः); (3) Holy Rāmatīrtha and the Mataṅgakedāra located on it 3. 83. 14; so also the holy Brahmaśālā river flows on it 3. 85. 18. D. Epic events: (1) Arjuna, during his exile, saw it when he went beyond the Kaliṅgas and while going further along the seashore 1. 207. 13; (2) The Brāhmaṇas expressed their wish to visit Mahendra and other mountains in the company of the Pāṇḍa-vas 3. 91. 10; (3) After visiting the river Vaitaraṇī, Yudhiṣṭhira went to Mahendra and lived there for a night; he honoured there the ascetics, Bhṛgus, Aṅgirases and others, and expressed his wish to see Rāma Jāmadagnya 3. 114. 26; 3. 115. 1-4; he also honoured the Brāhmaṇas 3. 117. 18; Jāmadagnya appeared before the Pāṇḍavas and was honoured by them (स तम् आनर्च राजेन्द्रः); Yudhi-ṣṭhira too was honoured by him (पूजितस् तेन) 3. 117. 16-18; (4) Hotravāhana advised Ambā to go to Mahendra to see Jāmadagnya 5. 175. 1-2; (5) Jāmadagnya admitted to Ambā his inability to defeat Bhīṣma and returned to Mahendra 5. 187. 11; (6) When Droṇa refused to impart Brahmā-stra to Karṇa, the latter went to Mahendra to acquire it from Jāmadagnya 12. 2. 14; there Karṇa met many Gandharvas, Rākṣasas, Yakṣas and gods 12. 2. 17. E. Mythologi-cal and past events: (1) Pitāmaha (Brah-man), in bygone days, offered a sacrifice on the mountain Mahendra; the river Bhāgīrathī was in his सदस् (यत्र भागीरथी पुण्या सदस्यासीत्) 3. 85. 17; (2) After extirpat-ing the Kṣatriyas from this earth twenty one times Rāma Jāmadagnya practised austerities on mount Mahendra 1. 58. 4; after perform-ing a sacrifice and giving away the earth to Kaśyapa, Jāmadagnya took his residence on Mahendra 3. 117. 14; (3) Mārkaṇḍeya saw Mahendra, among other mountains, in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 104; (4) King Nahuṣa, after he became the king of heaven, enjoyed himself on Mahendra and at other places in the company of the Apsarases and the Deva-kanyās 5. 11. 9. F. Importance: Mahendra heads the list of the seven principal mountains (सप्तैते कुलपर्वताः) listed by Saṃjaya 6. 10. 10; finds mention in the Daivata Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2. G. Simile: Karṇa with arrows pierced in his body looked like the Mahendra with trees covering its peaks and valleys (महीरुहैर् आचितसानुकन्दरो यथा महेन्द्रः) 8. 66. 39.
महेन्द्रवाणी: Mahendravāṇī f.: Name of a river. Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2.
