महेन्द्रा: Mahendrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 21, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 21 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā).
महेश्वरपद: Maheśvarapada nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who practises chastity and is com-posed (ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः) if he visits this तीर्थ and bathes there he will get the fruit of a horse sacrifice (वाजिमेधफलं लभेत्) 3. 82. 103.
महोदय: Mahodaya m.: Name (?) or epithet of Durgaśaila. [See Durgaśaila]
माठरस्य: Māṭharasya vanam nt.: Name of a forest. Situated on the Varuṇasrotas mountain in the south (3. 86. 1); described as holy, auspicious and having many roots and fruits (पुण्यं बहुमूलफलं शिवम्) 3. 86. 7.
मातृतीर्थ: Mātṛtīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the तीर्थस् of Kośeśvara; the progeny of one who bathes there increases and he gets endless prosperity (प्रजा विवर्-धते राजन्न् अनन्तां चाश्नुते श्रियम्) 3. 81. 47.
माधवीतीर्थ: Mādhavītīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the Kuśasthalī in the west (2. 13. 49); the Yādavas were delighted to see it when they decided to settle down in Kuśasthalī (माधवाः … परां मुदम् अवाप्नुवन्) 2. 13. 52.
मार्कण्डेयस्य: Mārkaṇḍeyasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated at the confluence of Gomatī and Gaṅgā; described as world famous (लोकवि-श्रुत), and difficult to reach (दुर्लभ); by visiting it one gets the fruit of an Agni-ṣṭoma and rescues one's family (मार्कण्डेय-स्य राजेन्द्र तीर्थम् आसाद्य … अग्निष्टोमम् अवाप्नोति कुलं चैव समुद्धरेत् ॥ ) 3. 82. 70.
माला: Mālā f.: Name of a river. Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna went beyond Mithilā and reached the river Mālā (and Car-maṇvatī) (अतीत्य जग्मुर् मिथिलां मालां चर्मण्वतीम् नदीम्) 2. 18. 28.
मालिनी: Mālinī1 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: On the lovely table-land of the Himavant (प्रस्थे हिमवतो रम्ये) 1. 66. 8; flowing through the forest in which there was an excellent hermitage of Kaṇva (1. 64. 25) (प्रेक्षमाणो वनं तत् तु … आश्रमप्रवरं रम्यं ददर्श … मालि-नीम् अभितो राजन् नदीम्) 1. 64. 15, 18; (नदीम् आश्रमसंश्लिष्टाम्) 1. 64. 20; (नदीम् आश्रमसंबद्धाम्) 1. 64. 23; (अलंकृतं  … मालिन्या … महद् वनम्) 1. 64. 24. B. Description: Holy, whose water is holy (पुण्या) 1. 64. 18; (पुण्यतोया) 1. 64. 20; whose water caused happiness (सुखोदका) 1. 64. 18; whose banks were pleasing (रम्य-तीरा) 1. 64. 24; delightful to the mind in the forest meant for austerities (तपोवन-मनोरमा) 1. 64. 18; bringing in her current flowers and foam (पुष्पफेनप्रवाहिनी) 1. 64. 21; full of islets (द्वीपवती) 1. 64. 24; Cakravāka birds resting on her sandy banks (सचक्रवाकपुलिना) 1. 64. 21; adorned with sandy banks (पुलिनैर् उपशोभिताम्) 1. 64. 22; thronged by many birds (नैक-पक्षिगणाकीर्णा) 1. 64. 18; resorted to by monkeys and bears (वानरर्क्षनिषेविता) 1. 64. 21; resorted to by elephants in rut, tigers and lordly serpents (मत्तवारणशार्-दूलभुजगेन्द्रनिषेविता) 1. 64. 22; provid-ing residence to the Kiṃnaras (सकिंनर-गणावासा) 1. 64. 21; humming with the sound of the recitations of holy Vedic studies (पुण्यस्वाध्यायसंघुष्टा) 1. 64. 22; stationed (in the forest) like the mother of all beings (सर्वप्राणिभृतां तत्र जननीम् इव विष्ठिताम्) 1. 64. 20. C. Past event: (1) Viśvāmitra begot Śakuntalā on Menakā near the river Mālinī; Menakā left Śakuntalā, no sooner born, on the river Mālinī and return-ed to the assembly of Śakra (Indra) 1. 66. 8-9; (2) Duḥṣanta, while out for hunting, saw the river Mālinī near a hermitage in the forest 1. 64. 18. D. Simile: The hermi-tage of Kaṇva adorned by Mālinī compared with the place of Nara-Nārāyaṇa adorned by Gaṅgā (आश्रमपदम् … अलंकृतम् … मालिन्या … नरनारायणस्थानं गङ्ग-येवोपशोभितम्) 1. 64. 23, 24.
माल्यवत्: Mālyavant1 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: In the north, beyond the Śveta mountain and near Gandhamādana 3. 155. 33-34, 27; situated to the south of the Nīla and to the north of the Niṣadha moun-tain, spread towards the east (प्रागाय-तः) 6. 7. 7 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 9: माल्यवान् पूर्वसमुद्रावधिः); beyond Mālyavant is Gandhamādana and between the two is the circular, golden mountain Meru (परिमण्डलस् तयोर् मध्ये मेरुः कनकपर्वतः) 6. 7. 8. B. Extent: It extends over fifty thousand योजनस् (योजनानां सहस्राणि पञ्चाशन् माल्यवान् स्थितः) 6. 8. 27. C. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 155. 33; very attractive (सु-मनोहर) 3. 155. 32; big (महागिरि) 3. 155, 33; having lotus ponds, pools and big forests (पद्मसरोपेतं सपल्वलमहा-वनम्) 3. 155. 33; noisy with sounds of beasts and birds, crowded with many kinds of birds and resorted to by troops of monkeys (मृगद्विजसंघुष्टं नानाद्विजसमाकु-लम् । शाखामृगगणैश् चैव सेवितम्) 3. 155. 32; listed by Brahman among ‘kings of mountains’ (एते पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 5. D. Characteristics: (1) On the peak of the Mālyavant blazes the fire called Saṃvartaka, the fire that destroys the world (तथा माल्यवतः शृङ्गे दीप्यते तत्र हव्-यवाट् । नाम्ना संवर्तको नाम कालाग्निः) 6. 8. 26; (2) On the eastern peak there is a hill which marks the end of the east (तथा माल्यवतः शृङ्गे पूर्वे पूर्वान्त-गण्डिका) 6. 8. 27 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 7. 28: गण्डिका क्षुद्रपर्वतः); (3) Men who fall down from the world of Brahman are born there with the colour of gold (महा-रजतसंकाशा जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः । ब्रह्मलोकाच् च्युताः सर्वे) 6. 8. 28 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 7. 29: महारजतं काञ्च-नम्); all of them are expounders of the Veda; they practise austerities and observe chastity and for the protection of beings they enter the sun (सर्वे च ब्रह्मवादिनः । तपस् तु तप्यमानास् ते भवन्ति ह्य् ऊर्ध्व-रेतसः । रक्षणार्थं तु भूतानां प्र-विशन्ति दिवाकरम् ॥ ) 6. 8. 28-29; sixty six thousand of them surround the sun and march ahead of Aruṇa (the sun's charioteer); they are heated by the sun's heat for sixty six thousand years and then they enter the moon 6. 8. 30-31; are all the mountains listed by Brahman to be looked upon as characterised by the middle quality (मध्यम गुण, i. e. रजस्) ? 14. 43. 1. E. Epic events: (1) The Pāṇḍavas reached it on their way from the Śveta to the Gandhamādana; from there they saw the Gandhamādana 3. 155. 33-34; (2) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the Mālyavant mountain 6. 8. 1.

Mālyavant2 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Near Kiṣkindhā in the south 3. 264. 15-16, 26. B. Description: Its top described as auspicious (पृष्ठे माल्य-वतः शुभे) 3. 264. 40. C. Rāmāyaṇa events: (1) Vālin, when he came out of his cave, saw Sugrīva standing near the Mālyavant and challenging him with roars (स्थितं माल्यवतो ऽभ्याशे) 3. 264. 26, 16; (2) After killing Vālln, Rāma lived on its top for four months and was served by Sugrīva 3. 264. 40; during his stay Rāma, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, was protected by Sugrīva 3. 266. 1; (3) Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva went to Rāma on the Mālyavant and reported to him the arrangements made for the search of Sītā 3. 266. 21.
माल्यवन्त्: Mālyavant1 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: In the north, beyond the Śveta mountain and near Gandhamādana 3. 155. 33-34, 27; situated to the south of the Nīla and to the north of the Niṣadha moun-tain, spread towards the east (प्रागाय-तः) 6. 7. 7 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 9: माल्यवान् पूर्वसमुद्रावधिः); beyond Mālyavant is Gandhamādana and between the two is the circular, golden mountain Meru (परिमण्डलस् तयोर् मध्ये मेरुः कनकपर्वतः) 6. 7. 8. B. Extent: It extends over fifty thousand योजनस् (योजनानां सहस्राणि पञ्चाशन् माल्यवान् स्थितः) 6. 8. 27. C. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 155. 33; very attractive (सु-मनोहर) 3. 155. 32; big (महागिरि) 3. 155, 33; having lotus ponds, pools and big forests (पद्मसरोपेतं सपल्वलमहा-वनम्) 3. 155. 33; noisy with sounds of beasts and birds, crowded with many kinds of birds and resorted to by troops of monkeys (मृगद्विजसंघुष्टं नानाद्विजसमाकु-लम् । शाखामृगगणैश् चैव सेवितम्) 3. 155. 32; listed by Brahman among ‘kings of mountains’ (एते पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 5. D. Characteristics: (1) On the peak of the Mālyavant blazes the fire called Saṃvartaka, the fire that destroys the world (तथा माल्यवतः शृङ्गे दीप्यते तत्र हव्-यवाट् । नाम्ना संवर्तको नाम कालाग्निः) 6. 8. 26; (2) On the eastern peak there is a hill which marks the end of the east (तथा माल्यवतः शृङ्गे पूर्वे पूर्वान्त-गण्डिका) 6. 8. 27 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 7. 28: गण्डिका क्षुद्रपर्वतः); (3) Men who fall down from the world of Brahman are born there with the colour of gold (महा-रजतसंकाशा जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः । ब्रह्मलोकाच् च्युताः सर्वे) 6. 8. 28 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 7. 29: महारजतं काञ्च-नम्); all of them are expounders of the Veda; they practise austerities and observe chastity and for the protection of beings they enter the sun (सर्वे च ब्रह्मवादिनः । तपस् तु तप्यमानास् ते भवन्ति ह्य् ऊर्ध्व-रेतसः । रक्षणार्थं तु भूतानां प्र-विशन्ति दिवाकरम् ॥ ) 6. 8. 28-29; sixty six thousand of them surround the sun and march ahead of Aruṇa (the sun's charioteer); they are heated by the sun's heat for sixty six thousand years and then they enter the moon 6. 8. 30-31; are all the mountains listed by Brahman to be looked upon as characterised by the middle quality (मध्यम गुण, i. e. रजस्) ? 14. 43. 1. E. Epic events: (1) The Pāṇḍavas reached it on their way from the Śveta to the Gandhamādana; from there they saw the Gandhamādana 3. 155. 33-34; (2) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the Mālyavant mountain 6. 8. 1.

Mālyavant2 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Near Kiṣkindhā in the south 3. 264. 15-16, 26. B. Description: Its top described as auspicious (पृष्ठे माल्य-वतः शुभे) 3. 264. 40. C. Rāmāyaṇa events: (1) Vālin, when he came out of his cave, saw Sugrīva standing near the Mālyavant and challenging him with roars (स्थितं माल्यवतो ऽभ्याशे) 3. 264. 26, 16; (2) After killing Vālln, Rāma lived on its top for four months and was served by Sugrīva 3. 264. 40; during his stay Rāma, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, was protected by Sugrīva 3. 266. 1; (3) Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva went to Rāma on the Mālyavant and reported to him the arrangements made for the search of Sītā 3. 266. 21.
माहेश्वरी: Māheśvarī dhārā f.: Name of a sac-red place. By reaching it (समासाद्य) a pilgrim obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha and rescues his family 3. 82. 101.
मिश्रक: Miśraka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as the best (उत्तम) 3. 81. 76; according to a tradition Vyāsa mixed together all the तीर्थस् in this तीर्थ for the benefit of the twice-born (तत्र तीर्थानि राजेन्द्र मिश्रितानि महात्मना ॥ व्यासेन नृपशार्दूल द्विजार्थम् इति नः श्रुतम् । ) 3. 81. 76-77 (this explains the name of the तीर्थ); one who bathes in this तीर्थ has the benefit of bathing in all the तीर्थस् 3. 81. 77.
मुञ्जपृष्ठ: Muñjapṛṣṭha1 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Near Gayā; by visiting it (?) one is freed of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa 13. 26. 40.

Muñjapṛṣṭha2 m.: Name of a holy summit. A. Location: Situated on the summit of the Himavant, on the golden mountain Meru 12. 122. 3. B. Description: Wor-shipped by the divine sages (देवर्षिगण-पूजित) 12. 122. 2. C. Holiness: The place was resorted to by Rudra (स देशो रुद्रसेवितः) 12. 122. 4. D. Past event: Vasuhoma, the righteous king of the Aṅgas, repaired to it together with his wife 12. 122. 2; the region was named as Muñjapṛṣṭha by the sages after Rāma ordered cutting off the locks of his hair (?) at Muñjavaṭa (because Rāma's matted hair were like thickets of Muñja ?) (यत्र मुञ्जवटे रामो जटाहर-णम् आदिशत् ॥ तदाप्रभृति राजेन्द्र ऋषिभिः संशितव्रतैः । मुञ्जपृष्ठ इति प्रोक्तः स देशः) 12. 122. 3-4. [See Muñjavaṭa2, Muñjavant]
मुञ्जवट: Muñjavaṭa1 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to Mahādeva 3. 81. 18; by stay-ing there for a night one gets the status of a Gaṇapati (तत्रोष्य रजनीम् एकां गाण-पत्यम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 81. 18; there is also a Yakṣī there, famous in the world (तत्रैव च … यक्षी लोकपरिश्रुता); by approaching her one the gets holy worlds (पुण्याल्̃ लोकान्) 3. 81. 19; the area is known as the Gate of the Kurukṣetra (कुरुक्षेत्रस्य तद् द्वारम्) 3. 81. 20.

Muñjavaṭa2 m.: Name of a tree (?). Situated on the Muñjapṛṣṭha, on the summit of the Himavant, on the golden Meru; at Muñjavaṭa, Rāma (Jāmadagnya ?) ordered cutting off the locks of his hair (?) (तत्र शृङ्गे हिमवतो मेरौ कनकपर्-वते । यत्र मुञ्जवटे रामो जटाहरणम् आदिशत्) 12. 122. 3. [See Muñjapṛṣṭha2]
मुञ्जवत्: Muñjavant m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: On the top of the moun-tain Himavant (गिरेर् हिमवतः पृष्ठे मुञ्जवान् नाम पर्वतः) 14. 8. 1. B. Description: King of mountains (शैलराज) 14. 8. 2. C. Characteristics: (1) The mountain blazes with lustre like that of the morning sun; neither its outward appearance nor shape can be seen in any form, nor can it be described by men with their normal fleshy eyes (न रूपं दृश्यते तस्य संस्थानं वा कथंचन । निर्देष्टुम् प्राणिभिः कैश्चित् प्राकृतैर् मांसलोचनैः) 14. 8. 8; (2) There is neither heat nor cold there, neither wind nor sun; there is neither old age, nor hunger, nor thirst; and neither death nor fear 14. 8. 9; (3) On all the slopes of the mountain there is gold which is guarded by helpers of Kubera armed with weapons (तस्य शैलस्य पार्श्वेषु सर्वेषु … । धातवो जात-रूपस्य … रक्ष्यन्ते ते कुबेरस्य सहायैर् उद्यतायुधैः । ) 14. 8. 10-11. D. My-thological and past events: (1) Enraged and dejected at the sight of the creatures created by another creator (10. 17. 15), Bhava (Śiva) went away to the foot of the mountain Muñjavant (गिरेर् मुञ्जवतः पादम्) to practise austerities 10. 17. 26; he practised austerities according to his desire and convenience at the roots of big trees, on the edges, summits, and caves of the mountain (वनस्पतीनाम् मूलेषु टङ्केषु शिखरेषु च । गुहासु शैलराजस्य यथा-कामं यथासुखम्) 14. 8. 1-2; Mahe-śvara always lives there with Umā and is surrounded by hosts of different Bhūtas; there Rudras, Sādhyas, all the Vasus and various other gods, as well as the Gandharvas and the Apsarases, and Yātudhānas wait on him 14. 8. 3-6; god Śiva enjoys himself there in the company of the followers of Kubera (रमते भगवांस् तत्र कुबेरानुचरैः सह) 14. 8. 7; (2) Saṃvarta asked king Marutta to send his men to the Muñjavant to get gold from there for his sacrifice after paying homage to Mahādeva 14. 8. 31. [See Muñjapṛṣṭha2]
मुञ्जवन्त्: Muñjavant m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: On the top of the moun-tain Himavant (गिरेर् हिमवतः पृष्ठे मुञ्जवान् नाम पर्वतः) 14. 8. 1. B. Description: King of mountains (शैलराज) 14. 8. 2. C. Characteristics: (1) The mountain blazes with lustre like that of the morning sun; neither its outward appearance nor shape can be seen in any form, nor can it be described by men with their normal fleshy eyes (न रूपं दृश्यते तस्य संस्थानं वा कथंचन । निर्देष्टुम् प्राणिभिः कैश्चित् प्राकृतैर् मांसलोचनैः) 14. 8. 8; (2) There is neither heat nor cold there, neither wind nor sun; there is neither old age, nor hunger, nor thirst; and neither death nor fear 14. 8. 9; (3) On all the slopes of the mountain there is gold which is guarded by helpers of Kubera armed with weapons (तस्य शैलस्य पार्श्वेषु सर्वेषु … । धातवो जात-रूपस्य … रक्ष्यन्ते ते कुबेरस्य सहायैर् उद्यतायुधैः । ) 14. 8. 10-11. D. My-thological and past events: (1) Enraged and dejected at the sight of the creatures created by another creator (10. 17. 15), Bhava (Śiva) went away to the foot of the mountain Muñjavant (गिरेर् मुञ्जवतः पादम्) to practise austerities 10. 17. 26; he practised austerities according to his desire and convenience at the roots of big trees, on the edges, summits, and caves of the mountain (वनस्पतीनाम् मूलेषु टङ्केषु शिखरेषु च । गुहासु शैलराजस्य यथा-कामं यथासुखम्) 14. 8. 1-2; Mahe-śvara always lives there with Umā and is surrounded by hosts of different Bhūtas; there Rudras, Sādhyas, all the Vasus and various other gods, as well as the Gandharvas and the Apsarases, and Yātudhānas wait on him 14. 8. 3-6; god Śiva enjoys himself there in the company of the followers of Kubera (रमते भगवांस् तत्र कुबेरानुचरैः सह) 14. 8. 7; (2) Saṃvarta asked king Marutta to send his men to the Muñjavant to get gold from there for his sacrifice after paying homage to Mahādeva 14. 8. 31. [See Muñjapṛṣṭha2]
मुर्मुरा: Murmurā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Mārkaṇḍeya which are declared to be mothers of the fire-hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः) 3. 212. 24 (for Nī. see Kapilā).
मृगधूम: Mṛgadhūma m., n. (?): Name of a तीर्थ। One should proceed to it from the तीर्थस् Ahan and Sudina; situated on Gaṅgā; des-cribed as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्); by bathing there in the lake of Gaṅgā and by worshipping Mahādeva, wielding Śūla in his hand, one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha 3. 81. 85.
मेद्रथा: Medrathā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Mārkaṇḍeya which are declared to be mothers of the fire-hearths 3. 212. 23 (for other details see Mur-murā).
मेधातिथि: Medhātithi f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Mārkaṇḍeya which are declared to be mothers of the fire- hearths 3. 212. 22 (for other details see Murmurā).
मेधाविक: Medhāvika nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Having reached Medhāvika one should satisfy manes and gods; he thereby wins the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and gets remembrance and intellect (स्मृतिं मेधां च विन्दति) 3. 83. 52.
मेध्या: Medhyā f.: Name of a river. Situated in the west (प्रतीच्यां … दिशि । यानि तत्र पवित्राणि पुण्यान्य् आयतनानि च) 3. 87. 1; described as most holy (पुण्य-तमा) and always frequented by ascetics (सततं तापसायुता) 3. 87. 12; listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among rivers which are declared to be mothers of the fire-hearths 3. 212. 22 (for other details see Murmurā); finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 21, 2.
मेध्यारण्य: Medhyāraṇya nt.: Name (?) of a forest. Where the blind and dethroned king Dyumatsena lived with his wife and son Satyavant 3, 278. 7-9; described as big forest (महारण्य) 3. 278. 9; (महावन) 3. 280. 23; king Aśvapati went to Medhyā-raṇya forest with his daughter Sāvitrī 3. 279. 3.
मेना: Menā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa listed by Saṃjaya; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 22, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā).
मेरु: Meru1 m.: Name of a mountain, also referred to as Mahāmeru (1. 65. 36; 3. 160. 12, 14, 28; 9. 36. 20; 12. 14. 22-24; 12. 59. 122; 12. 321. 13; 13. 14. 156; 14. 44. 12). A. Location: In the Svarloka (उप-रिष्टाद् असौ लोको यो ऽयं स्वर् इति संज्ञि-तः । … मेरुः पर्वतराड् यत्र) 3. 247. 2, 8; in the north (उदीचीं दीपयन्न् एष दिशं तिष्ठति कीर्तिंआन् । महामेरुः) 3. 160. 12; 3. 155. 13-14; 12. 320. 9; 17. 2. 2; on the summit of the mountain Himavant (शृङ्गे हिमवतो मेरौ) 12. 122. 3; on the northern side of the Himavant (हिमवत्पार्श्व उत्तरे) 14. 4. 25; beyond the Himavant 17. 2. 2; between the Mālyavant lying to its east and the Gan-dhamādana lying to its west lies the circular mountain Meru 6. 7. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 9: नीलनिषधयोर् मध्ये मेरुस् तस्य प्राक् माल्यवान् पूर्वसमुद्रावधिः पश्चिम-समुद्रावधिर् गन्धमादन इत्य् अर्थः); Śuka after crossing the Varṣas of Meru and Hari (i. e. the Ilāvṛta and the Harivarṣa Varṣas) and that of Himavant (called Kiṃ-puruṣa) reached the Bhāratavarṣa (मेरोर् हरेश् च द्वे वर्षे वर्षं हैमवतं तथा । क्रमेणैव व्यतिक्रम्य भारतं वर्षम् आसदत्) 12. 312. 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 325. 14: मेरोर् वर्षं इलावृतम् । हरेर् वर्षं हरिवर्षाख्यम् । हैमवतं वर्षं किंपुरुषाख्यम्); to the north of Meru is the Kṣīroda (milky ocean) (मेरोर् उत्तरभागे तु क्षीरोदस्यानुकूलतः) 12. 323. 21; from the summit of the Meru one can see in the north-west Śvetadvīpa to the north of the Kṣīrodadhi (आलोकयन्न् उत्तर-पश्चिमेन ददर्श … क्षीरोदधेर् उत्तरतो हि द्वीपः श्वेतः स नाम्ना प्रथितः) 12. 322. 7-8; the Śvetadvīpa was at a distance of 32000 योजनस् in the north from the foot of the mount Meru (मेरोः सहस्रैः स हि योजनानां द्वात्रिंशतोर्ध्वं कविभिर् निरुक्तः) 12. 322. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 335. 9: मेरुमूलात् द्वात्रिंशत्सहस्रयोज-नाद् ऊर्ध्वम्); on its four sides (तस्य पार्-श्वे) are the four Dvīpas, viz. the Bhadrāśva, the Ketumāla, the Jambūdvīpa and the Uttara Kurus 6. 7. 11; to the north of the Mahāmeru is the Bhadrāśva 12. 14. 24; to the east of the Mahāmeru is the Śākadvīpa 12. 14. 23; to the west of the Mahāmeru is the Krauñca-dvīpa 12. 14. 22; on the western side of the Meru is the Ketumāla, to the south of the Nīla and to the north of the Meru are the Uttara Kurus, and to the east of the Meru is the Bhadrāśva 6. 7. 29; 6. 8. 2, 13; the river Śailodā flows between the Meru and the Mandara 2. 48. 2. B. Extent: Its extent is thirty three thousand योजनस् (त्रयस्त्रिं-शत् सहस्राणि योजनानाम् … मेरुः) 3. 247. 8; it is sixteen thousand योजनस् deep and eighty four (thousand) योजनस् high; it covers the worlds above, within and crosswise (योज-नानां सहस्राणि षोडशाधः किल स्मृतः ॥ उच्चैश् च चतुराशीतिर् योजनानां महीपते । ऊर्ध्वम् अन्तश् च तिर्यक् च लोकान् आवृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ ) 6. 7. 9-10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 11: अधस्तात् भूमेर् गर्भे); its peak was a hundred योजनस् high crosswise and above (शतयोजनविस्तारे तिर्यग् ऊर्ध्वम् च … संददर्श ह) 12. 320. 9. C.
