(अनेककल्पम् उद्विद्धम्) 1. 15. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 17. 9: अनन्तकल्पं अनन्तो विष्णुर् आकाशो वा तत ईषन् न्यूनम् । बहु-गुणत्वाद् अतिप्रमाणत्वाच् च । ईषद् असमा-प्तौ कल्पप् । उद्विद्धम् उच्चम्॑); its summits rise high (शिखरैः … उच्छ्रितैः) 6. 78. 26; very high (शृङ्गैर् अत्यर्थम् उच्-छ्रितैः) 6. 106. 33; circular (परिमण्डल) 6. 7. 8; steady, unshakable (अचल) 1. 15. 5; 6. 59. 8; 6. 74. 24; 7. 33. 18; (7. 149. 17); 8. 31. 62; firm (स्थैर्येण मेरोः) 8. 48. 9; its peak (शृङ्ग) unequalled (अप्रतिम) 12. 320. 8; immeasurable, immeasurable in all the worlds (अप्रमेय) 1. 15. 6; (अप्रमेयं … सर्वलोकेषु) 12. 274. 5; unassailable in all the worlds (अनाधृष्यं सर्वलोकेषु) 12. 274. 5; unassailable by impious persons (अना-धृष्यम् अधर्मबहुलैर् जनैः) 1. 15. 6; inaccessible to ordinary people even in thought (अगम्यं मनसाप्य् अन्यैः) 1. 15. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 17. 8: अगम्यं अप्राप्यम् अन्यैः प्राकृतैः); its region (देश) free from dust (विरजस्) 3. 160. 16; free from diseases (अनामय) 3. 160. 14; famous (कीर्तिमन्त्) 3. 160. 12; has many peaks (अङेकशृङ्गवन्त्) 9. 44. 13; golden moun-tain (कनकपर्वत) 3. 102. 2; 3. 186. 103; 6. 7. 8; 12. 59. 122; 12. 122. 3; (काञ्-चनपर्वत) 13. 101. 6; (हिरण्मय) 3. 247. 8; (काञ्चन) 1. 216. 34; (7. 60. 17); it has gold as its ornament (काञ्चनाभरण) 1. 15. 6; its peak (शृङ्ग) is golden (रुक्-ममय) 12. 320. 8; it excels with its peaks, shining with gold, the lustre of the sun (आक्षि-पन्तं प्रभां भानोः स्वशृङ्गैः काञ्च-नोज्ज्वलैः) 1. 15. 5; (शिखरैः काञ्चन-मयैः) 6. 78. 26; (7. 96. 4); its foot (पाद) is golden (काञ्चन) 14. 4. 25; its slopes (गिरितट) are ornamented with gold (हेम-धातुविभूषित) 12. 274. 6; it is covered all over with splendid, golden houses (भवनैर् आवृतः सर्वैर् जाम्बूनदमयैः शुभैः) 6. 7. 15; its surface (पृष्ठ) is full of many jewels (बहुरत्नाचित) 1. 15. 9; its peak (शृङ्ग) is adorned with all kinds of jewels (सर्वरत्नविभूषित) 12. 274. 5; very large number of jewels on Meru alluded to in 13. 27. 97; it is a mass of lustre (तेजोराशि) 1. 15. 5; burning (ज्वलन्त्) 1. 15. 5; lustrous (श्रीमन्त्) 7. 33. 18; of great lustre (महा-द्युति) 1. 216. 34; it is illuminated with heavenly herbs (दिव्यौषधिविदीपित) 1. 15. 7; it is yellow (पीत) 12. 320. 8; its peaks (शृङ्ग) and tops (पृष्ठ) are shining (शुभ) 12. 320. 8-9; 1. 15. 9; its peak (शृङ्ग) is heavenly (दिव्य) and splendid (रुचिर) 12. 320. 8; highly lustrous (महाद्युति) 1. 216. 34; it is very lustrous all around like the sun and like smokeless fire (आदित्यतरुणाभासो विधूम इव पावकः) 6. 7. 9; it brightens the north (उदीचीं दीपयन्न् एष दिशं तिष्-ठति) 3. 160. 12; lustrous (चित्र) 1. 15. 6; Meru looked upon as an excellent crest of the earth (पृथिवीम् … मेरुवरोत्तंसाम्) 1. 159. 20; Meru and Mandara are the two ornaments of the earth (मेरुमन्दरभूष-णाम् … वसुंधराम्) 3. 187. 10; pleasing (रम्य) 12. 327. 18; the forest on it is pleasing (रम्य), full of flowers (सुपुष्पित) and agreeable due to the singing of the Kin-naras (किन्नरगीतजुष्ट) 13. 105. 20; its peak (शृङ्ग) has forests of Karṇikāra trees (कर्णिकारवनायुत) 12. 310. 11; on the northern side of the mountain is a forest of the Karṇikāra trees which is heavenly, aus-picious, pleasing, flowering in all seasons and which has grown out of the crevices in its slabs (पार्श्वे तस्योत्तरे दिव्यं सर्वर्तुकुसुमं शिवम् । कर्णिकारवनं रम्यं शिलाजाल-समुद्गतम् ॥ ) 6. 7. 22; the mountain has many rivers and forests (नदीवृक्षसमन्-वित) 1. 15. 8; full of heavenly flowers and fruits (दिव्यपुष्पफलान्वित) 6. 7. 15; re-sounding with the sounds of various, attrac-tive birds (नानापतगसंघैश् च नादितं सुमनोहरैः) 1. 15. 8; resorted to by gods and the Gandharvas (देवगन्धर्वसेवित) 1. 15. 6; also by the Siddhas and the Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारणसेवित) 12. 327. 18; haunted by fierce beasts of prey (व्यालैर् आचरितं घोरैः) 1. 15. 7; also see the next section C. Characteristics and the entry Jyotiṣka: the peak on mountain Meru. C. Characteri-stics: (1) Lustre is the chief characteristic of Meru (प्रभां मेरोः) 13. 98. 10; (2) Aśvatthāman had the गौरव (respectability, respy. heaviness) of Meru (मेरुगौरवम्) 9. 5. 8; (3) Kaṇiṅka (Bharadvāja) told king Śatruṃtapa that one should adopt what is best in Meru, i. e. its best characte-ristics (मेरोः … यच् छ्रेष्ठं तत् समा-चरेत्) 12. 138. 21 (according to Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 140. 21 these are अचञ्चलत्वम् अनु-ल्लङ्घनीयत्वं; according to Arjunamiśra सर्वोच्चप्रकृतित्वं; according to Vimala-bodha कोषबहुलत्वं सर्वोच्चप्रकृतित्वं च; see Editor's notes, Cr. Ed. Vol. 14, p. 936); (4) Prajāpati dwells in his residence (ब्रह्-मसदस्) on the Mahāmeru while creating the worlds; he dwells there with gods 3. 160. 13, 16; on the summit of Meru there is the abode (सदन) of Svayaṃbhū (Brahmadeva) 13. 92. 7; Meru forms the pericarp of the lotus (i. e. the earth) (कर्णिका तस्य पद्-मस्य मेरुः); sitting on it Brahman creates the world 12. 175. 37; (5) The seven mind-born sons of Brahman, Dakṣa and others, also live on the Mahāmeru 3. 160. 14; (6) beyond the residence (सदन) of Brahman on the Meru shines the highest place (परं स्थानम्) of Nārāyaṇa 3. 160. 17-18; (7) There god Paśupati (Śiva) himself sports with Umā and other divine beings (दिव्यैर् भूतैः समावृतः) wearing a garland of Karṇikāra flowers reaching down up to his feet and illuminating the surroundings on the mountain with his three eyes; the Siddhas there can see him 6. 7. 23-24; (8) The seven high-souled sages and Kaśyapa Prajāpati visit the mountain on every पर्-वन् day 6. 7. 19; (9) On the top of Meru, Uśanas Kāvya sports with the Daityas (तस्यैव मूर्धन्य् उशनाः काव्यो दै-त्यैः … ) 6. 7. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 22: रमत इति शेषः); (10) The gods have their gardens there (यत्र देवोद्यानानि) 3. 247. 8; there the hosts of gods, the Gan-dharvas, the Asuras and the Rākṣasas always sport in the company of the Apsarases 6. 7. 16; (11) There Brahman, Rudra and Śakra, the king of gods, come together and offer various sacrifices giving many दक्षिणास् (स-मेत्य विविधैर् यज्ञैर् यजन्ते ऽनेकदक्-षिणैः) 6. 7. 17; (12) All the jewels and the six jewelled mountains (षड् एते रत्न-पर्वताः 6. 7. 2) belong to Meru (तस्य हीमानि रत्नानि तस्येमे रत्नपर्वताः) 6. 7. 20 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 22: तस्य काव्यस्य); from it Kubera gets one fourth share and from what he has obtained he gives to men a portion of its sixteenth part (तस्-मात् कुबेरो भगवांश् चतुर्थं भागम् अश्नुते । ततः कलांशं वित्तस्य मनुष्ये-भ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥ ) 6. 7. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 6. 23: कलांशं षोडशभागस्यापि लेशम्); (13) Tumburu, Nārada, Viśvāvasu, Hahā, Huhū and the foremost among gods gather together and praise (mount Meru) with praises 6. 7. 18; (14) The sun (आदित्य) drags behind him all the luminaries and going round Meru, keeping it to the right, he dispels darkness (एतं ज्योतींषि सर्वाणि प्रकर्षन् भगवान् अपि । कुरुते वितमस्कर्मा आदि-त्यो ऽभिप्रदक्षिणम्) 3. 160. 24; the sun goes to the Asta mountain and, passing the twilight there (संध्याम् अतिक्रम्य) he goes to the north; again continuing his journey along Meru (स मेरुम् अनुवृत्तः सन्) the sun goes eastwards 3. 160. 25-26; 3. 102. 2-3; this path of the sun is unhindered (मार्-गम् एतद् असम्बाधम् आदित्यः परिवर्तते) 3. 160. 29; this route of the sun round Meru was ordained by the Creator of the world (एष मार्गः प्रदिष्टो मे येनेदं निर्मितं जगत्) 3. 102. 4; similarly the moon, along with the नक्षत्रस्, moves round Meru dividing the duration of the month into पर्-वन्स् and returns to Mandara (स मासं विभजन् कालं बहुधा पर्वसंधिषु । तथैव भगवान् सोमो नक्षत्रैः सह गच्छति ॥ ) 3. 160. 27-28; besides the sun, the moon and the नक्षत्रस्, Vāyu also moves round Meru keeping it to the right (अनु-पर्येति … वायुश् चैव प्रदक्षिणम्) 6. 7. 14; (15) The seven divine sages (देव-र्षयः), chief among whom is Vasiṣṭha, also set on this mountain and again rise there (अत्रैव प्रतितिष्ठन्ति पुनर् अत्रोदयन्ति च) 3. 160. 15; (16) All birds on mount Meru are golden (सौवर्णान् प्रेक्ष्य वाय-सान्) 6. 7. 12; seeing them the bird Sumukha, son of Suparṇa, thought of leaving mount Meru since it made no distinction between the best, the intermediate, and the lowest (मेरुर् उत्तममध्यानाम् अधमानां च पक्षि-णाम् । अविशेषकरो यस्मात् तस्माद् एनं त्यजाम्य् अहम् ॥ ) 6. 7. 13; (17) There is a large, good-looking (सुदर्शन 13. 105. 20) Jambū tree called Sudarśana (सुदर्शनो नाम) on mount Meru 6. 8. 18; the river formed by the juice of the fruit of this tree flows round Meru and goes to the Uttara Kurus (मेरुं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा संप्रयात्य् उत्तरान् कुरून्) 6. 8. 23; (18) From the summit of mount Meru the river Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī falls down with terrific speed in the Cāndra-masa lake 6. 7. 26-27; (19) Various tribes like the Khaśas, the Ekāśanājyohas (?), the Pradaras, the Dīrghaveṇus, the Paśupas, the Kuṇindas, the Taṅgaṇas, and the Parataṅ-gaṇas live in the valley of the mountains Meru and Mandara (मेरुमन्दरयोर् मद्-ह्ये) 2. 48. 2-3; (20) Swans and vultures go to Meru by passing through a hole in the Krauñca mountain made by Skanda 3. 214. 31. D. Holiness: One who falls down along the precipice of Meru is freed of all blemishes (मेरुप्रपातं प्रपतन् … मुच्-यते सर्वकिल्बिशैः) 12. 36. 14; Brāhmaṇas who are truthful, learned, kind to all beings, who study the Itihāsa and the Purāṇa, who offer honey offerings to Brāhmaṇas (मध्-वाहुत्या जुह्वति च द्विजेभ्यः) go to the regions of Meru 13. 105. 21-22. E. Im-portance: (1) While narrating his विभूतिस् Bhagavān told Arjuna that he was Meru among the mountains (मेरुः शिखरिणाम् अहम्) 6. 32. 23; (2) Meru is the ultimate place where the knowers of Brahman go (ब्रह्मविदां गतिः) 3. 160. 12; (3) Śiva is the Mahāmeru among mountains (पर्वता-नां महामेरुः) 13. 14. 156; (4) Mahā-meru was the first to be created among all the mountains (पर्वतानां महामेरुः सर्वेषाम् अग्रजः स्मृतः) 14. 44. 12; (5) When Śiva appointed some one in each class as its head he made Meru the chief of the mountains (पर्वताणां पतिम्) 12. 122. 28; (6) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2. F. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana (Vyāsa) taught the four Vedas, and the Mahābhārata as the fifth, to his five pupils Sumantu, Jaimini, Paila, Vaiśaṃpāyana, and Śuka (his son) on Meru 12. 327. 16-18; (2) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the nor-thern and the eastern side of Meru (मेरोर् अथोत्तरं पार्श्वं पूर्वं चाचक्ष्व सं-जय) 6. 8. 1; (3) On his way northwards to the Śveta mountain, Yudhiṣṭhira saw Meru and other mountains 3. 155. 14; (4) Draupadī, while comforting Yudhiṣṭhira who was dejected, reminded him that he once ran over the Krauñcadvīpa with his दण्ड (दण्डेन मृदितस् त्वया) which lay to the west of Mahāmeru, so also the Śākadvīpa to the east of Mahāmeru, and Bhadrāśva to the north of Mahāmeru 12. 14. 22-24; (5) Vyāsa, while practising austerities in order to obtain a son, recited Śivastava on Meru 13. 18. 2; (6) The Pāṇḍavas, on their great journey (महाप्रस्थान), saw Meru when they went beyond the Himavant 17. 2. 2. G. Mythological and past events: (1) God (Śiva) once sat on the summit of Meru (गिरितटे) in a पर्यङ्क posture (पर्यङ्क इव विभ्राजन्न् उपविष्टो बभूव ह) 12. 274. 6; (2) Formerly Mahādeva sported on the peak of Meru in the company of the Bhūtas (भूतगणैर् वृतः) 12. 310. 11; (3) Formerly Nārāyaṇa became the great sage Vaḍavāmukha; while practising austerities on Meru he invited the ocean, but it did not come 12. 329. 48 (2); (4) When gods were afflicted by the food offered to them which was proper for manes (निवापान्न) they went to Pitāmaha on Meru 13. 92. 7; (5) Bharadvāja asked Bhṛgu how Brahman created the creatures while sitting in the middle of Meru (मेरुमध्ये स्थितो ब्रह्मा) 12. 176. 1; (6) Gods mounted the top of Meru and sat down to think of the way to obtain अमृत; there Nārāyaṇa told Brahman that gods and Asuras together should churn the Kala-śodadhi to get अमृत 1. 15. 9-13; (7) Sixty-six thousand ऋषिस् who follow Sūrya (सूर्या-नुगामिभिस् तात ऋषिभिः) narrated the Pañca-rātra doctrine (12. 326. 100) to gods who had assembled on Meru 12. 326. 109; (8) Vindhya told the sun to go round it as it went round Meru 3. 102. 2; (9) Dānava Hiraṇyakaśipu was able to shake Meru (हिरण्यकशिपुर् यो ऽभूद् दानवो मेरु-कम्पनः) 13. 14. 52; (10) Mṛtyu, con-ceived as a woman, was reluctant to carry out the instruction of Brahman to destroy creatures; she went to Meru and stood there motionless like a log of wood for doing good to creatures (भूतानां हितकाम्यया) 12. 250. 22; (11) Gaṅgā, unable to bear the embryo planted in her by Agni, cast it off on Meru 13. 84. 64; (12) Meru was present at the consecration of Kumāra (Ska-nda) as the chief of the army of gods 9. 44. 13, 16; after the consecration, Meru gave his two followers (अनुचरौ) Kāñcana and Hemamālin to Skanda; he also gave him Sthira and Atisthira 9. 44. 43-44; (13) An ascetic named Suvarṇa and Manu sat together on a stoneslab on Meru and told each other stories of Brahmarṣis, gods and Daityas from the Purāṇas 13. 101. 6-7; (13) A Brāhmaṇa Gautama offered to take king Dhṛtarāṣṭra (really Indra) to Meru, if he returned to the Brāhmaṇa his elephant; but the latter did not wish to go there 13. 105. 20-21; (14) Mahāmeru gave gold to (Pṛthu) Vainya when he was anointed king by Viṣṇu and others 12. 59. 122; (15) King Marutta went to Meru and performed a sacrifice at the foot of the mountain; his sacrificial enclosure was close to the mountain (तस्यैव च समीपे स यज्ञवाटो बभूव ह); for this sacrifice Marutta used utensils made of gold obtained from Meru 14. 4. 25-27; (16) Ekata, Dvita and Trita told Bṛhaspati that the country where they practised austerities in order to see Nārāyaṇa lay to the north of Meru and on the shores of the ocean of milk 12. 323. 21; (17) Rāma (Jāmadagnya ?) ordered the removal of his matted locks (?) at a place called Muñjavaṭa on Muñja-pṛṣṭha on Meru (यत्र मुञ्जवटे रामो जटाहरणम् आदिशत्) 12. 122. 3; (18) On the slope (पार्श्व) of Meru was the her-mitage of Vasiṣṭha where he practised auste-rities 1. 93, 6-7; Vasiṣṭha, grieved over the death of his sons, jumped down from the summit of Meru to end his life (but he did not die) 1. 166. 41; (19) The great sage Sthūlaśiras practised austerities on the north-eastern side of Meru (प्रागुत्तरे दिग्भागे) 12. 329. 47 (1); (20) When Śuka was born, Gaṅgā came in her original form (स्व-रूपिणी) on the summit of Meru to bathe Śuka with her water 12. 311. 12; (21) Śuka reached the Bhāratavarṣa after crossing the two Varṣas of Meru and Hari 12. 312. 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 325. 14: मेरोर् वर्षं इलावृतम् । हरेर् वर्षं हरिवर्षाख्यम्); when Śuka moved through the sky he saw before him the two summits of Meru and Himavant closely connected with each other; undeterred Śuka went on flying and suddenly the two peaks split into two; that was a marvel; Śuka passed beyond the two peaks and the mountain (Meru or Himavant ?) could not stop his movement; the mountain was split into two 12. 320. 8, 10-11, 13; (22) In order to go to the Śvetadvīpa Nārada flew up in the sky and reached the top of Meru 12. 322. 6; after seeing Hari on the Śvetadvīpa, Nārada returned to Meru; from Meru Nārada proceeded to Gandha-mādana and reached the Viśālā Badarī to see Nara and Nārāyaṇa 12. 331. 22; 12. 321. 13; (23) Mārkaṇḍeya saw, among other mountains, Meru in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 103; (24) When Gaṅgā fell down from heaven Śiva held the river on his head on Meru (or Himavant ?) and from there the river reached the earth (दिवश् च्युता शिरसात्ता भवेन गङ्गावनीध्रात्) 13. 27. 89 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 26. 89: अवनीध्रस्य मेरोः हिमवतो वा पर्वतस्य; on 13. 26. 90: अवनीध्रात् पृथिवीं प्राप्नोतीति शेषः). H. Similes: (1) Various warriors taking part in the battle compared with Meru: (a) Epic war: (i) Aśvatthāman showered (अभ्यवर्षत्) arrows on Śaineya (Sātyaki) as a cloud showers rain on Meru 7. 141. 13; (ii) Aśvatthāman, showered with arrows by Añjanaparvan, grandson of Bhīma, was affli-cted as is Meru by the showers of rain sent by the cloud 7. 131. 45; (iii) Eight sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra showered arrows on Abhi-manyu as do clouds on Meru 6. 75. 25; (iv) Ghaṭotkaca showered arrows on Karṇa and others as a cloud showers rain on Meru 7. 149. 17; (v) Ghaṭotkaca covered (प्र-च्छादयाम् आस) Bhagadatta with arrows as a cloud covers Meru 6. 79. 31; (vi) Aśva-tthāman with Śikhaṇḍin's three arrows stuck on his forehead compared with Meru with its three high, golden summits 6. 78. 26; (vii) Arjuna with arrows, shot at him by Duḥśā-sana, stuck on his forehead looked like Meru with its very high peaks 6. 106. 33; (viii) Arjuna was equal to Meru in steadiness (स्थैर्येण) 8. 48. 9; (ix) Bhīma was unshakable (अचल) like Meru 6. 59. 8; 8. 31. 62; (x) Abhimanyu did not shake and remained steady like Meru when struck by five arrows of Durjaya and Vikarṇa 6. 74. 24; (xi) Jayadratha stood steadfast at the entrance of the Cakravyūha like Meru (श्री-मान् मेरुर् इवाचलः) 7. 33. 18; (xii) Arjuna, covered with gold on his golden cha-riot, shone like the blazing sun on Meru (स रथे … काञ्चने काञ्चनावृतः) 7. 60. 17; (xiii) Sātyaki with his golden bracelet (अङ्गद), helmet (शिरस्त्राण) and armour (वर्मन्) and golden shaft shone like the peak of Meru 7. 96. 4; (xiv) Bhīṣma with his raised silvery staff with five stars on it (केतुना पञ्चतारेण … राजतेन) looked like Meru with moon on it (चन्द्रमा इव मेरुणा) 6. 44. 48 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 46. 50: अत्र चन्द्रकेत्वोर् मेरुसरथभीष्म-योश् चोपमो (? उपमानो) पमेयभावः । भीष्मस्य रुक्मरथत्वात्); (xv) Arjuna was best among warriors as Meru is among the mountains 5. 63. 5; (b) Outside the epic war: (i) Rāma (Jāmadagnya) with blood issuing from the wounds all over his body appeared like Meru throwing out the red mine-rals (मेरुर् धातून् इवोत्सृजन्) 5. 180. 30; (c) Other contexts: (i) Śiva's body, when he was dressed like a Kirāta which made him look like a golden tree, appeared like another Meru (कैरातं वेषम् आस्थाय काञ्चन-द्रुमसंनिभम् । विभ्राजमानो वपुषा गिरिर् मेरुर् इवापरः ॥ ) 3. 40. 2; (ii) (Gāndhārī, Kuntī, and other) Kaurava women mounted the seats (in the arena) as the women of gods mount mountain Meru (आरुरुहुर् मञ्चान् मेरुं देवस्त्रियो यथा) 1. 124. 14; (iii) Yājñasenī did not leave the Pāṇḍavas as the lustre of the sun does not leave Meru (मेरुं अर्कप्रभा यथा) 3. 80. 4; (iv) The Raivataka mountain, richly decorated for the festival and the Yādavas moving on it, looked like Meru with the hosts of sages on it 14. 58. 8; (v) Kṛṣṇa's chariot appeared like the summit of Meru (मेरुशिखरप्रख्यम्) 5. 81. 21; (vi) Nārada told the huge Śālmali tree on the Himavant that since many birds, ele-phants, and other kinds of beasts resorted to it and since it offered shelter to travellers (सार्थाधिवासैश् च) it shone like Meru 12. 150. 17; (vii) A tree called Mahāśaṅkha at the Śaṅkhatīrtha was as tall as Mahāmeru 9. 36. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 9. 37. 31: नगं वृक्षम्); (viii) The burning Khāṇḍava forest looked like the highly lustrous, golden Meru 1. 216. 34 (also see the next section Idioms). I. Idioms: (1) For describing unexpected or impossible events: (i) Fall of Bhāradvāja (Droṇa) was like displacing Meru (विपर्यासं यथा मेरोः) 7. 165. 73; (ii) Dhṛtarāṣṭra could not bear the felling of Droṇa as he could not bear the shifting of Meru 7. 33. 18 (मेरोर् इव विसर्पणम्) 7. 8. 12; (iii) Karṇa's death was as unbelievable and unexpected (अश्रद्धेयम् इवाद्भुतम्) as is the tossing about (पर्यसनम्) of Meru 8. 5. 3; (iv) In the opinion of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, wishing to conquer Droṇa in battle was as unheard of as wind uprooting Meru (न हि शुश्रुम वातेन मेरुम् उन्मथितं गिरिम्) 5. 158. 15; (v) also in his opinion if the Pāṇḍavas were to win the war it would be like wind blowing away Meru (अनिलो वा वहेन् मेरुम्) 5. 158. 16; (vi) in the opinion of Saṃjaya one may carry off Meru (अपि मेरुं वहेत् कश्चित्) but it would not be possible for any one to overpower the Vṛṣṇi heroes 7. 119. 27; (iii) Kṛṣṇa's out of place great delight (अतिहर्षो ऽयम् अस्थाने 7. 155. 6) and the lightness of his heart (तथैतल् लाघवम्) over the death of Ghaṭotkaca was (as unbelievable) as the shifting of Meru (मेरोर् इव विसर्पणम्) 7. 155. 10; (iv) Menakā told Indra that Viśvāmitra by his तपस् could abbreviate Mahāmeru and quickly turn it around (संक्षिपेच् च महामेरुं तूर्णम् आवर्तयेत् तथा) 1. 65. 36 (Nī., who reads तूर्णम् आवर्तयेद् दिशः, on Bom. Ed. 1. 71. 36: आवर्तयेद् एकीकुर्यात्); (v) Karṇa could split asunder even Meru (निर्-भिन्द्याम् … अपि मेरुम्) with his special arrow which he had reserved for Kṛṣṇa or Arjuna 8. 27. 59; (vi) Only a person who could transgress the lustre of Meru would (do such an unthinkable act as) killing one who had taken resort with him ( … प्र-भां मेरोः … एतन्य् अतिक्रमेद् यो वै स हन्याच् छरणागतम्) 13. 98. 10; (2) To express great difference: (i) According to Śakuntalā the difference between her and king Duḥṣanta was as great as between Meru and the mustard seed (आवयोर् अन्तरं पश्य मेरुसर्षपयोर् इव) 1. 69. 3; (ii) It may be possible to tell the number of all the jewels on Meru (मेरोः … सर्वरत्नैः संख्या … वक्तुम् शक्यम्) but it was not possible to describe or measure the virtues of the Gaṅgā waters 13. 27. 97. [See Kanaka-parvata]

Meru2 m.: Name of a mountain in the Śākadvīpa, also referred to as Mahāmeru (6. 12. 23). One of the seven mountains of the Śāka-dvīpa 6. 12. 13; described as great (परम) and resorted to by gods, sages and Gandharvas (देवर्षिगन्धर्वयुतः) 6. 12. 14; all the seven mountains of the Śākadvīpa are adorned with gems (मणिभूषिताः) and are mines of jewels (रत्नाकराः) 6. 12. 13; the Varṣa of Mahāmeru is called Mahākāṣa 6. 12. 23; the extent of these seven mountains doubles as one proceeds from one to the other (तेषां योजनविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः) 6. 12. 22.
मैनाक: Maināka1 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: To the north-east of Indra-prastha (प्रागुदीचीम् अगाद् दिशम्) 2. 3. 7; to the north of Kailāsa, and close to the Hiraṇyaśṛṅga mountain (उत्तरेण तु कैला-सं मैनाकं पर्वतं प्रति । हिरण्य-शृङ्गो … गिरिः) 2. 3. 8, 2; 6. 7. 40; 3. 145. 39; near the Kailāsa, the Gandhamādana and the Meru mountains (अवेक्षमाणः कैलासं मैनाकं चैव पर्वतम् । गन्धमादन-पादांश् च मेरुं चापि शिलोच्चयम् ॥ ) 3. 155. 14; near the Uśīrabīja and the Kāla-śaila mountains in the north; from there one could reach the Śveta and the Mandara moun-tains (उशीरबीजं मैनाकं गिरिं श्वेतं च भारत । समतीतो ऽसि कौन्तेय काल-शैलं च पार्थिव ॥ … श्वेतं गिरिं प्र-वेक्ष्यामो मन्दरं चैव पर्वतम् । ) 3. 140. 1, 4; Maināka could be seen from the Naranārāyaṇāśrama at the Visālā Badarī on the Himālaya 3. 145. 10, 16, 39. B. Des-cription: Immeasurable and unassailable (अप्रमेय, अनाधृष्य) 3. 149. 13; full of many kinds of birds (नानाद्विजगणायुत) 3. 145. 39; called the king of mountains (पर्वतराजन्) 3. 135. 4; (also see the next section C). C. Characteristics: As re-vealed in comparisons: (i) not shakable (नाकम्पयद् … मैनाकम् इव पर्वतम्) 6. 45. 19; 7. 46. 15; 7. 74. 28; 7. 99. 2; 6. 43. 64; 6. 88. 23; immovable (न चचाल … मईनाक इव पर्वतः) 9. 18. 43; (ii) huge (महाकायः … व्यदृश्यत मैनाक इव पर्वतः) 7. 150. 58-59; (iii) Great and irresistible (महान्तम् इव मैनाकम् असह्यम्) 7. 3. 4; (also see the section G). D. Holiness: (1) A place in the cave of the Maināka was known as Vinaśana; by ascending the mountain and by reaching this place it was possible to destroy evil fortune that is disgraceful and unspeakable (this ex-plains the name Vinaśana) (एतद् विनशनं कुक्षौ मैनाकस्ग … एनं पर्वतराजानम् आरुह्य … अयशस्याम् असंशब्द्याम् अलक्ष्मीं व्यपनोत्स्य् अथ ॥ ) 3. 135. 3-4; (2) One who has observed chastity for a month if he performs the संध्या ceremony after bathing on Maināka he gets the fruit of a Sarva-medha (मैनाके पर्वते स्नात्वा तथा सं-ध्याम् उपास्य च कामं जित्वा च वै मा-सम् सर्वमेधफलं लभेत्) 13. 26. 56. E. Epic events: (1) Asura Maya went to Maināka to reach the lake Bindusaras on the Hiraṇyaśṛṅga mountain 2. 3. 2, 8; (2) Lomaśa referred to the holy place Vinaśana on Maināka and advised the Pāṇḍavas to ascend the mountain 3. 135. 3-4; (3) The Pāṇḍa-vas had crossed Maināka before entering the Śveta and the Mandara mountains 3. 140. 1, 4; (4) The Pāṇḍavas could see Maināka from the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa at Badarī 3. 145. 39; Yudhiṣṭhira could see it while on his way northwards to the Śveta mountain from the Nārāyaṇāśrama 3. 155. 14. F. Past events: (1) Nārāyaṇa practis-ed severe austerities on Maināka 7. 172. 52; (2) At the Vinaśana in the cave on Mai-nāka, Aditi, in bygone days, cooked food (for gods) to get a son (अदितिर् यत्र पुत्रार्थं तद् अन्नम् अपचत् पुरा) 3. 135. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 135. 3: अन्नं ब्रह्मौद-नम् । अदितिः पुत्रकामा साध्येभ्यो देवे-भ्यो ब्रह्मौदनम् अपचद् इत् श्रुतेः). G. Similes: Various heroes compared with Maināka. (1) For its unshakableness: (i) Śrutakarman, son of Sahadeva, could not he shaken by the arrows of Sudakṣiṇa like Maināka 6. 43. 64; similarly (ii) Abhi-manyu 6. 45. 19; 7. 46. 15; (iii) Sātyaki 7. 99. 2; (iv) Kṛṣṇa (by the hit of a गदा) 7. 74. 28; (v) Ghaṭotkaca, seeing the Kau-rava army led by their heroes advance against him, did not shake like Maināka 6. 88. 23; (vi) Similarly Bhīma did not move from his chariot seat when attacked by the Kaurava army (न चचाल रथोपस्थे मैनाक इव पर्वतः) 9. 18. 43; (2) For its huge-ness: Ghaṭotkaca rising up, assuming a huge form having hundred heads and hundred stomachs (महाकायः शतशीर्षः शतोद-रः), looked like Maināka 7. 150. 58-59; (3) For its hugeness and irresistibility: Bhīṣma lying on his bed of arrows was like the huge and irresistible Maināka felled down (महान्तम् इव मैनाकम् असह्यं भुवि पातितम्) 7. 3. 4; (4) Hanūmant was im-measurable and unassailable like Maināka (अप्रमेयम् अनाधृष्यम्) 3. 149. 13; (5) Arjuna avoided Droṇa who stood like Maināka 7. 67. 17; (6) Kirmīra, obstruct-ing the entrance of the Kāmyaka forest stood there like Maināka 3. 12. 15; (7) All (kings) were inferior to king Maithila (Janaka) as are other mountains to Maināka (सर्वे राज्ञो मैथिलस्य मैनाकस्येव पर्-वताः) 3. 134. 5.
Maināka2 m.: Name of a mountain in the west. Located in the west (प्रतीच्याम्) 3. 87. 1; it has holy lakes on it (पुण्यह्रद) 3. 87. 9.

Maināka3 m.: Name of a mountain in the Krauñcadvīpa. A. Location: One of the six mountains of the Krauñcadvīpa; it lies beyond the moun-tain Andhakāra and beyond Maināka lies the mountain Govinda 6. 13. 17-18; the name of the region (देशांस् तत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि 6. 13. 20) related to Maināka is Prāvaraka (?) 6. 13. 21. B. Extent: The extent of the mountains of the Krauñcadvīpa doubles as one proceeds from the one to the other (परस् तु द्विगुणस् तेषं विष्कम्भः) 6. 13. 19. C. Description: Excellent mountain (पर्-वतोत्तम) 6. 13. 18.
मोघा: Moghā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 22, 13; (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
मचक्रुक: Macakruka m., nt. (?): Place name, (or name of a तीर्थ, short for Macakruka-tīrtha ?). It is mentioned along with Tarantuka, Arantuka, and the lakes of Rāma as form-ing the boundary of Kurukṣetrasamanta-pañcaka which is called as the Uttaravedi of Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) (तरन्तुका-रन्तुकयोर् यद् अन्तरं रामह्रदानां च मचक्रुकस्य । एतत् कुरुक्षेत्रसमन्त-पञ्चकं पितामहस्योत्तरवेदिर् उच्यते ॥ ) 3. 81. 178 = 9. 52. 20.
मणलूर: Maṇalūra, Maṇipūra nt.: Name of a city. A. Location: On the (eastern) seacoast (समुद्रतीरेण शनैर् मणलूरं जगाम ह) 1. 207. 13. B. Epic events: Arjuna, during his exile, visited it from the Mahen-dra mountain; he met there king Citra-vāhana; while he was in that city he happened to see Citravāhana's daughter Citrāṅgadā (तां ददर्श पुरे तस्मिन्) 1. 207. 13-15; Arjuna lived in this town for three years (उवास नगरे तस्मिन् कौन्तेयस् त्रिहिमाः समाः) 1. 207. 23; (2) Having freed the five तीर्थास् of the crocodiles, Arjuna returned to Maṇalūra to meet Citrāṅgadā; he begot on her a son Babhru-vāhana 1. 209. 23-24; (3) The horse of Yudhiṣṭhira's Aśvamedha reached the coun-try of the king of Maṇipūra (मणिपूर-पतेर् देशम् उपायात्) 14. 77. 46. (4) When the Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī set out for their great journey (महाप्रस्थान), Citrāṅgadā left Hāstinapura for Maṇipūra (चित्राङ्गदा ययौ चापि मणिपूरपुरं प्रति) 17. 1. 26. C. Mention in titles: (1) Citravāhana, father of Citrāṅgadā, called Maṇalūreśvara 1. 207. 14; (2) Ba-bhruvāhana, who ruled after Citravāhana, called Maṇipūrapati 14. 77. 46; 14. 78. 39; 14. 81. 21; 14. 82. 1; 14. 88. 19; Maṇipūre-śvara 14. 78. 2; 14. 81. 1; 14. 82. 18, 23.
मणिमती: Maṇimatī f.: Name of a city. Formerly a Daitya named Ilvala and his younger brother Vātāpi lived in the town Maṇimatī (इल्वलो नाम दैतेय आसीत् … । मणिमत्यां पुरि पुरा वातापिस् तस्य चानु-जः ॥ ) 3. 94. 4 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 96. 1 seems to take दुर्जया as an epithet ‘invin-cible’ of Maṇimatī: दुर्जयायां वातापि-पुर्यां मणिमतीसंज्ञायां; Durjayā is mentioned in 3. 94. 1). [See Agastyāśrama, Durjayā]
मथुरा: Mathurā f.: Name of a city. A. Famous for: (1) Milch cows of holy complexion; Kṛṣṇa gave to the Pāṇḍa-vas, as a part of dowry, large number of such milch cows from the place around Mathurā (माथुरदेश्यानां दोग्ध्रीणां पुण्यवर्चसाम् । … ददौ जनार्दनः प्री-त्या) 1. 213. 42-43; (2) Men around Mathurā known for their skill in wrestling (मथुराम् अभितश् च ये । एते नियुद्ध-कुशलाः) 12. 102. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 101. 5: नियुद्धं बाहुयुद्धम्). B. Epic events: (1) Krṣṇa and the other Yādavas lived happily at Mathurā when Jarāsandha, after the death of Haṃsa and Dibhaka, left fighting and returned to his city 2. 13. 44; (2) Kṛṣṇa and the Yādavas fled from Mathurā out of fear of Jarāsandha and went to Dvārakā 2. 13. 65. C. Past event: Nārāyaṇa had prophesied to Nārada that at the close of the conjunction of Dvāpara and Kali he would be born in Mathurā for the death of Kaṃsa (द्वापरस्य कलेश् चैव संधौ पर्यवसानिके । प्रादुर्भावः कंसहेतोर् मथुरायां भविष्यति) 12. 326. 82.
मरुद्गणानाम्: Marudgaṇānām āyatanam: nt. Name of a holy resort (temple ?) of the Marud-gaṇas. A. Location: In a holy forest, not very far from the sea and the तीर्थ called Śūr-pāraka (शूर्पारकं ददर्श ॥ तत्रोदधेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशम् … वनम् आससाद) 3. 118. 8-9; (स तत्र … मरुद्गणानाम् … आयतनानि तेषां ददर्श) 3. 118. 10-11, 13. For B. Description and C. Epic event: see Bhagasya āyatanam.
महाश्रम: Mahāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। A. Description: One that frees from all sins (सर्वपापप्रमोचन) 3. 82. 48; B. Holiness: (1) By staying there for a night and by abstaining from food for one time in a day one lives in auspicious worlds (महा-श्रमे वसेद् रात्रिम् । … एककालं नीराहारो लोकान् आवसते शुभान्) 3. 82. 48; (2) By bathing there, by regularly offering Agni-hotra, and by fasting for a month, one who is pure, obtains perfection at the end of a month (महाश्रम उपस्पृश्य यो ऽग्निहोत्र-परः शुचिः । एकमासं निराहारः सिद्धिं मासेन सो व्रजेत्) 13. 26. 16.
महेच्छ: Maheccha nt.: Name of a city. To the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; described as having abundant grain (बहुधान्याक); Nakula brought it under his control (वशे चक्रे) in his expedition to the west before the Rājasūya 2. 29. 6.
महेन्द्रस्य: Mahendrasya Vaiśravaṇasya ca sadman nt.: The house of Mahendra (Indra) and Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera). The eastern direction is so called; it is guarded by Indra and Vaiśravaṇa; it was pointed out by Dhaumya to Yudhiṣṭhira holding him by his right hand (प्राचीं दिशम् अभिप्रेक्ष्य महर्षिर् इदम् अब्रवीत् ॥  … इन्द्रवैश्रवणाव् एतां दिशं पाण्डव रक्षतः । … एतद् आहुर् महेन्द्रस्य राज्ञो वैस्रवणस्य च … सद्म) 3. 160. 3, 5-6; it is adorned by mountains, forest regions and woods (पर्वतैश् च वनान्तैश् च कान-नैश् चोपशोभिताम्) 3. 160. 5; people, sages, Siddhas, Sādhyas and gods worship sun rising from there 3. 160. 7.
माण्डव्यस्य: Māṇḍavyasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of the आश्रम of the sage Māṇḍavya. A. Epic event: One of the holy places where Ambā lived to practise austerities to be able to kill Bhīṣma; these आश्रमस् were of high-souled ascetics who were holy (आश्रमं पुण्यशीलानां तापसानां महा-त्मनाम्) 5. 187. 23; she bathed there day and night and practised austerities (तत्र पुण्येषु देशेषु साप्लुताङ्गी दिवानिशम् । व्यचरत् … ॥ … माण्डव्यस्याश्रमे … एतेषु तीर्थेषु तदा काशिकन्या … आप्लावयत गात्-राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः ॥ ) 5. 187. 24, 27-28. B. Past event: Māṇḍavya once observed the vow of silence and stood, with raised hands, under a tree at the entrance of his आश्रम (माण्डव्यः … स आश्रमपदद्वारि वृक्षमूले महातपाः । ऊर्ध्वबाहुर् महायोगी तस्थौ मौनव्रता-न्वितः ॥ ) 1. 101. 2-3; once, some Dasyus, who stole wealth and were chased by guar-dians, reached the hermitage of Māṇḍavya; they left the stolen property in the residence of Māṇḍavya and hid themselves (ते तस्यावसथे लोप्त्रं निदधुः) 1. 101. 4-5.
मार्कण्डेयाश्रम: Mārkaṇḍeyāśrama m.: The आश्रम of Mārkaṇḍeya. A. Location: In the Dvaitavana (पुनर् द्वैतवनं … आजगाम युधिष्ठिरः … मार्कण्डेयाश्रमं प्रति) 3. 295. 3. B. Description: Delightful (रम्य) and having sweet roots and fruits (स्वादुमूलफल) 3. 295. 3. C. Epic event: (1) The Pāṇḍa-vas and Draupadī lived in this आश्रम after they left the Kāmyaka forest (न्य-वसन् पाण्डवास् तत्र कृष्णया सह) 3. 295. 4; (2) Formerly, when Bhīṣma went out for hunting he reached the आश्रम of Mārkaṇḍeya where he saw many sages assembled together; Bhīṣma heard there the narrative (कथैषा कथिता) of Viṣṇu in which he (Viṣṇu) appeared in the form of a boar (पुराहं मृगयां यातो मार्क-ण्डेयाश्रमे स्थितः । तत्रापश्यं मुनि-गणान् … ॥ कथैषा कथिता तत्र कश्यपेन महऋषिणा) 12. 202. 4-6.
माहिष्मती: Māhiṣmatī f.: Name of a city. A. Location: In the south, near the river Narmadā (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम्) 2. 28. 1; (दक्षिणाभिमुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 8; (नर्मदाम् अभितो ययौ) 2. 28. 9; (तथा माहिष्मतीवासी नीलः … दक्षिणापथवासि-भिः) 5. 19. 23. B. Characterized generally as पुरी 2. 28. 11, 22-23, 34; once as राष्ट्रम् 2. 28. 25. C. Special features: (1) Agni always lived in the city of Māhiṣ-matī (ततः सांनिध्यम् अद्यापि माहिष्म-त्यां विभावसोः) 13. 2. 32; (तत्र माहिष्-मतीवासी भगवान् हव्यवाहनः । श्रूयते) 2. 28. 17. (2) Under the rule of Duryo-dhana (not Kaurava) his town and king-dom (नगरं विषयश् चास्य) were full of jewels, riches, cattle and different kinds of corn (सस्यैश् चापि प्र्थग्विधैः) 13. 2. 14; nobody in his kingdom (विषये) was wret-ched, distressed, afflicted by disease, or emaciated 13. 2. 15; (3) King Nīla asked as a boon from Agni freedom from fear (विभावसुः ॥ वरेण छन्दयाम् आस तं नृपम् … अभयं स च जग्राह स्वसैन्ये वै महीपतिः ॥ ) 2. 28. 20-21; hence who-ever wished to subjugate the city Māhi-ṣmatī was burnt down by fire 2. 28. 22; (4) Also as a result of the boon of Agni, women of the city Māhiṣmatī, under the rule of Nīla, could not be withheld from their desire (?); so women of the town were unrestrained and they behaved ac-cording to their desire (तस्यां पुर्यां तदा चैव माहिष्मत्याम् … । बभूवुर् अनभिग्राह्या योषितश् छन्दतः किल ॥ एवम् अग्निर् वरं प्रादात् स्त्रीणाम् अप्रतिवारणे । स्वैरिण्यस् तत्र नार्यो हि यथेष्टं प्रचरन्त्य् उत ॥ ) 2. 28. 23-24; (5) Due to the fear of Agni kings avoided that city (वर्जयन्ति च राजानस् तद् रा-ष्ट्रं … । भयाद् अग्नेर्) 2. 28. 25; Agni told Sahadeva that he would continue to protect the city as long as the descendents of Nīla ruled it 2. 28. 54. D. Epic events: (1) Sahadeva in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya marched on Māhiṣmatī from Avantī; Māhiṣmatī was then ruled by king Nīla (पुरीं माहिष्म-तीम् ययौ) 2. 28. 11; Sahadeva could not subjugate it as it was protected by Agni (2. 28. 26; 13. 2. 32); but when he pleased Agni, the latter withdrew and Nīla recei-ved Sahadeva (पावके विनिवृत्ते तु नीलो राजाभ्ययात् तदा । सत्कारेण … सहदेवम्) 2. 28. 36; (2) King Nīla of Māhiṣmatī went with his southern warriors, using dark weapons (swords ?) to Duryodhana to help him in war with the Pāṇḍavas (ततो माहिष्मतीवासी नीलो नीलायुधैः सह । महीपालो महावीर्यैर् दक्षिणापथवासि-भिः) 5. 19. 23; (3) King Nīla of Māhi ṣmatī, wearing dark armour and, fighting with a host of chariot fighters, will des-troy Duryodhana's enemies for he (Nīla) has formerly formed enmity with Sahadeva (नीतो माहिष्मतीवासी नीलवर्मधरस् तव । रथवंशेन शतृऊणां कदनं वै करि-ष्यति ॥ ) 5. 163. 4-5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 166. 4: रथवंशेन रथसंघेन); (कृतवैरः पुरा चैव सहदेवेन) 5. 163. 5 (a reference to 2. 28. 11-15). E. Past events: (1) Daśāśva, the tenth son of Ikṣvāku, once ruled Māhiṣmatī 13. 2. 6; (2) In Daśāśva's lineage was born Duryo-dhana; when Agni asked for Sudarśanā, daughter of Duryodhana, the latter in return asked as dowry (शुल्क) Agni's continuous presence in Māhiṣmatī; hence Agni was always present in Māhiṣmatī (13. 2. 31-32); Agni's presence in Māhiṣmatī was witnessed by Sahadeva in his expedi-tion before the Rājasūya (दृष्टं हि सह-देवेन दिशो विजयता तदा) 13. 2. 32 (a reference to 2. 28. 13-15). (3) When Arjuna Kārtavīrya ruled at Mahīṣmatī, he ruled the entire earth (कार्तवीर्यो ऽभवत् प्रभुः । … माहिष्मत्यां महाबलः ॥ … शशास सर्वां पृथिवीं हैहयः) 13. 137. 3-4.
मित्रस्य: Mitrasya Varuṇasya ca āśramaḥ m.: The आश्रम of Mitra and Varuṇa. On the river Yamunā (यमुनायां जगाम ह) 9. 53. 13; Balarāma went to the आश्रम of Mitra and Varuṇa from the Kārapacanatīrtha (संप्राप्तः कारपच-नं तीर्थप्रवरम् । … तस्माच् चापि जगा-म ह । आश्रमं परमप्रीतो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च ॥ ) 9. 53. 11-13; formerly Indra, Agni and Aryaman were very pleased to be in this आश्रम (इन्द्रो ऽग्निर् अर्यमा चैव यत्र प्राक् प्रीतिम् आप्नुवन्) 9. 53. 13; Balarāma bathed there in Yamunā and heard stories from the sages and the Siddhas; when Nārada arrived there, Balarāma heard from him about the duel that was going to be fought between Bhīma and Duryodhana; hearing it, Balarāma went from the आश्रम to Kurukṣetra 9. 53. 14-15; 29-31, 37.
मिथिला: Mithilā f.: Name of a city. A. Location: In the eastern Kosala country, beyond Sarayū river and near Mālā and Carmaṇvatī rivers (संतीर्य सरयूं रम्यां दृष्ट्वा पूर्वांश् च कोस-लान् । अतीत्य जग्मुर् मिथिलां मालां चर्-मण्वतीम् नदीम् ॥ ) 2. 18. 28; the (capi-tal) town of the Videhas (विदेहानां पुरीम्) 12. 308. 11; 1. 105. 11. B. Descrip-tion: Pleasing (रम्या) 3. 198. 7; 12. 308. 12; its grove (मिथिलोपवन) was pleasing (रम्य) and of luxurious growth (महर्-धिमन्त्) 12. 312. 22; auspicious (शुभा) 3. 198. 6; full of fords for religious practices (धर्मसेतुसमाकीर्णा) 3. 198. 6; in which festivals of sacrifices were held (यज्ञो-त्सववती 3. 198. 6; busy with constant festi-vals (नित्योत्सवसमाकुला) 3. 198. 8; full of prosperous people (समृद्धजनसंकुला) 12. 308. 12; full of happy and well nourish-ed people (हृष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णा) 3. 198. 8; thronged by men and women (नरनारी-समाकुला) 12. 312. 22; it had gates and watchtowers (गोपुराट्टालकवती) 3. 198. 7; adorned by houses and protective walls (गृहप्राकारशोभिता) 3. 198. 6; surrounded by many tall houses (विमानैर् बहुभिर् वृताम्) 3. 198. 7; full of market goods (पण्यैश् च बहुभिर् युक्ताम्) 3. 198. 7; its main roads were well distributed (सुवि-भक्तमहापथा) 3. 198. 7; having many horses, chariots, elephants and carriages (अश्वै रथैस् तथा नागैर् यानैश् च बहु-भिर् वृताम्) 3. 198. 8; crowded with ele-phants, horses and chariots (हस्त्यश्वरथ-संकीर्ण) 12. 312. 22-23; full of activities (बहुवृत्तान्ता) 3. 198. 9. C. Its ruler: The city was ruled and protected by king Janaka (मिथिलां जनकेन सुरक्षिताम्) 3. 198. 5; hence Janaka called Mithilādhipa 12. 211. 1, 3; Mithileśvara 12. 308. 8, 12; 12. 312. 6; Maithila 12. 308. 4; 12. 312. 7; also Vide-harāja 12. 268. 3. D. Epic events: (1) Pāṇḍu reached Mithilā and defeated the Videhas in a battle 1. 105. 11; (2) Kṛṣṇa, with Bhīma and Arjuna, while on their way to the Magadha country, reached Mi-thilā after crossing the river Sarayū 2. 18. 28. E. Past events: (1) A certain Brāhmaṇī once advised the Brāhmaṇa Kauśika to go to Mithilā where lived a hunter who would teach him the nature of धर्म (मिथिलायां वसन् व्याधः स ते धर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यति) 3. 197. 41; 3. 205. 2-3; the Brāhmaṇa deci-ded to go to Mithilā to meet the hunter and question him on the nature of धर्म 3. 198. 2-5; the Brāhmaṇa reached the town and enquired about the Vyādha who knew धर्म (धर्मव्याध) 3. 198. 7-9; the Vyādha already knew that the Brāh-maṇa was directed to go Mithilā by the Brāhmaṇī 3. 198. 13; (2) King Janaka, engaged in meditating on the धर्मस् rela-ted to the condition after death, lived in Mithilā (जनकः … मिथिलायां जनाधिपः । और्ध्वदेहिकधर्माणाम् आसीद् युक्तो विचिन्-तने ॥ ) 12. 211. 3 (But Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 218. 3: ऊर्ध्वं देहाद् इत्य् ऊर्ध्व-देहम् अशरीरं ब्रह्म तत्प्राप्तिकराणाम् और्ध्वदेहिकानां विचिन्तने युक्तः); (3) A certain sage by name Pañcaśikha, son of Kapilā, while wandering on earth reached Mithilā 12. 211. 6; (4) Sulabhā reached Mithilā to meet Janaka and to know from him the nature of मोक्ष 12. 308. 12; (5) Śuka proceeded to Mithilā on foot to know the nature of धर्म and मोक्ष 12. 312. 6-7, 12; Śuka reached the grove on the out-skirts of Mithilā (मिथिलोपवन) before entering Mithilā 12. 312. 22; (6) Janaka told a certain Brāhmaṇa that when he got the ancestral kingdom he was not certain about his own territory; he sought it on earth, and when he did not find it there, he sought it in Mithilā; when he did not find it even there, he sought it in his subjects (पितृपैतामहे राज्ये वश्ये जनपदे सति । विषयं नाधिगच्छामि विचिन्वन् पृथिवीम् इमाम् ॥ नाध्यगच्छं यदा पृथ्व्यां मि-थिला मार्गिता मया । नाध्यगच्छं यदा तस्यां स्वप्रजा मार्गिता मया) 14. 32. 8-9 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 14. 32. 8: विषयं विशेषेण सिनोति बध्नातीति तं बन्धकं ममतास्पदं नाधिगच्छामि विचिन्वन् अन्वेषमाणो ऽपि); concerning his own indifference to the opposīte pairs of feelings, his disattached condition, and while visualizing his liberation, Janaka is reported to have sung a गाथा in which he said that even if the whole Mithilā was ablaze, nothing belonging to Janaka was burnt (अपि गाथाम् इमां गीतां जनकेन वदन्त्य् उत । निर्द्वन्-द्वेन विमुक्तेन मोक्षं समनुपश्यता ॥ अनन्तं बत मे वित्तं यस्य मे नास्ति किंचन । मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां न मे दह्यति किंचन ॥ ) 12. 17. 17-18; 12. 171. 55-56; with a change in the first quarter the गाथा also appears as: गीतं विदेह-राजेन … सुसुखं बत जीवामि यस्य मे नास्ति किंचन । मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां … 12. 268. 3-4.
मुरचीपत्तन: Muracīpattana nt.: Name of a city. One of the places subjugated by Sahadeva in his expedition to the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; दक्षि-णाभिमुखो ययौ 2. 28. 8) before the Rājasūya (मुरचीपत्तनं तथा । … वशे चक्रे) 2. 28. 45-46.
मेरुव्रज: Meruvraja nt.: Name of a city. A. Events: (1) As advised by Rāja-dharman, the king of the cranes, the Brāh-maṇa Gautama, went to Meruvraja, the city of the Rākṣasa king Virūpākṣa (इत्य् उक्तः प्रययौ राजन् गौतमः … । … मेरु-व्रजं नाम नगरम्) 12. 164. 17, 19, 15; (2) The Rākṣasas returned to Meruvraja with Gautama and the dead body of Rāja-dharman 12. 166. 14. B. Description: Hav-ing arched doorways made of stone (शै-लतोरण); having rampart walls built with stones (शैलप्राकारवप्र); having mecha-nical bolts made of stone (शैलयन्त्रार्गल) 12. 164. 19.
मोदापुर: Modāpura nt.: Name of a city. One of the places subjugated by Arjuna in his expedition to the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां तस्माद् दिशम् 2. 24. 1) before the Rājasūya 2. 24. 10.
मग: Maga m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada of Śākadvīpa and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the four Janapadas of Śākadvīpa (तत्र॥।जनपदाश् चत्वारो … । मगाश् च) 6. 12. 33. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य), respected by people (लोकसंमत) 6. 12. 33. C. Characteristic: The Maga people comprised mostly Brāhmaṇas who were devoted to their duty (मगा ब्राह्मण-भूयिष्ठाः स्वकर्मनिरता नृप) 6. 12. 34; in all the four Janapadas of Śākadvīpa there was no king, no punishment, nor officers to give punishment; by following one's धर्म, people protected one another and also their धर्म (न तत्र राजा राजेन्द्र न दण्डो न च दण्डिकाः । स्व-धर्मेणैव धर्मं च ते रक्षन्ति पर-स्परम् ॥ ) 6. 12. 36.
मडक: Maḍaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. On the second day of war, warriors from Maḍaka were among the twelve Jana-padas which were stationed at the right wing of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of Pāṇḍavas (व्यूहः क्रौञ्चा-रुणो नाम) 6. 46. 39; (मडका लडकाश् चैव … एते जनपदा राजन् दक्षिणम् पक्षम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 6. 46. 49-50.
मणीचक: Maṇīcaka m.: Name of a Varṣa of of the Śākadvīpa. It was related to the mountain Śyāma (वर्षाणि तेषु कौरव्य … श्यामस्य तु मणीचकः) 6. 12. 22, 24.
मण्डप: Maṇḍapa m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: South (दक्षिणापथ-जन्मानः … चूचुपा मण्डपैः सह) 12. 200. 39; B. Description: see Utsa B. above pp. 638-639.
मत्तमयूरक: Mattamayūraka m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: West of Khāṇḍava-prastha (see Epic event below). B. Des-cription: Heroic (शूर) 2. 29. 5. C. Epic event: They were in the army of king Kārtikeya of Rohītaka; Nakula fought a mighty battle with them in his expedition to the west before the Rājasūya (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 10; (कार्तिकेयस्य दयितं रोहीतकम् उपाद्रवत् ॥ तत्र युद्धं महद् वृत्तं शूरैर् मत्तमयूरकैः ॥ ) 2. 29. 4-5.
मत्स्य: Matsya m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people; the country designated as जनपद, राष्ट्र, or विषय; their capital town referred to as Matsyanagara. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (मत्स्याः सुकुट्यः) 6. 10. 38; situated around Kuru country (परितः कुरून्) 4. 1. 9; at one place Matsyas are said to lie to the east of Indraprastha (2. 27. 1, 8-9) and at another place to the south of it (2. 28. 1-2, 4); designated as जन-पद or राष्ट्र in 4. 1. 8-9; 4. 29. 8; 6. 18. 13; as विषय in 4. 29. 19, 23-24; its internal divisions also referred to as राष्ट्र (pl.) 4. 29. 9; Matsyas distinguished from the Aparamatsyas (i. e. Matsyas of the borderland ?) 2. 28. 4. B. Description: (i) of the country: delightful (रमणीय, रम्य), having ample food (बह्वन्न), well-protected (गुप्त) 4. 1. 8-9; (बहुधा-न्यसमाकुल) 4. 29. 8; very prosperous (सुसमृद्ध) 4. 29. 24; (ii) of their warriors (on the side of both Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas): heroic (वीर) 7. 42. 18; (शूर) 4. 31. 1, 10; 6. 18. 13; 7. 8. 27; 7. 21. 24; strong, very strong (बलवन्त्), (महाबल), of great heroism (महा-वीर्य) 4. 31. 2; 7. 13. 36; 7. 21. 24; valor-ous (विक्रान्त, पराक्रान्त) 5. 52. 2; 7. 21. 24; great chariot-fighters (महारथ), arrogant in battles (युद्धदुर्मद), skill-ed in fighting with arrows (धनुर्वेद-विशारद) 4. 31. 2; 6. 70 33; 7. 21. 24; having arms as large as परिघ (परिघ-बाहु) 4. 31. 10; ready to give up their lives in battles (तनूत्यज्) 6. 18. 13; not of cruel appearance (अनृशंसरूप) 5. 47. 33. C. Characteristic nature: According to a certain Brāhmaṇa (8. 30. 57), Matsyas knew the eternal धर्म; they practised the ancient धर्म (मत्-स्याः … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम् । … धर्मं पुराणम् उपजीवन्ति) 8. 30. 60-62, 75; according to Rākṣasa Kalmāṣa-pāda, Matsyas were truth incarnate (सत्यं मत्स्याः) 8. 30. 73. D. Epic events: (1) Pāṇḍavas, after their escape from Vāraṇāvata, passed through Matsyas, Trigartas and other countries 1. 144. 2; (2) Matsyas, afraid of Jarāsandha. fled from the north to the south (तथोत्तरां दिशं परित्यज्य भयार्दिताः । … मत्स्याः  … दक्षिणां दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 2. 13. 27; (3) Bhīma in his expedition to the east (2. 26. 1) defeated Matsyas 2. 27. 8-9; (4) Sahadeva in his expedition to the south (2. 28. 1) brought under control the king of Matsyas (मत्स्यराजं॥।वशे चक्रे) and also defeated Aparamatsyas (अपरमत्स्यांश् च व्यजयत्) 2. 28. 2, 4; (5) Matsya country was one of those suggested by Arjuna to Yudhiṣṭhira for their stay during अज्ञातवास 4. 1. 9-10; (6) Virāṭa offered Kaṅka the ruler-ship of Matsyas (प्रशाधि मत्स्यान्) 4. 6. 11; (7) When Bṛhannaḍā (Arjuna) arrived in the court of Virāṭa, he (Virāṭa) told him to protect Matsyas 4. 10. 7; (8) In the fourth month of अज्ञातवास there was a grand festival in the Matsya country in honour of Brahman (अथ मासे चतुर्थे तु ब्रह्मणः सुमहोत्सवः । आसीत्॥।मत्स्येषु) 4. 12. 12; during the wrestling match, when Ballava (Bhīma) whirled his opponent round, Matsyas were struck with wonder 4. 12. 22; (9) Sairandhrī (Draupadī) lamented that no one among the Matsyas, nor any one of those present in the assembly showed any knowledge of धर्म (स्वधर्मस्थो न च मत्स्यः कथंचन । सभासदो ऽप्य् अधर्मज्ञा॥।) 4. 15. 25; Yudhiṣṭhira blamed Sairandhrī (Draupadī) for dis-turbing the dice-game of Matsyas which was in progress in the royal assembly (विघ्नं करोषि मत्स्यानां दीव्यतां राज-संसदि) 4. 15. 34; (10) Bhīma assured Draupadī that he would kill Matsyas if they came to know that it was he who had killed Kīcaka 4. 21. 33; (11) Suśarman informed Duryodhana that he was for-merly often insulted by the Matsyas 4. 29. 2; (12) When the cattle-raid was report-ed to Virāṭa he ordered his army to get ready to fight (सेनां मत्स्यानां सम-योजयत्) 4. 30. 8; Matsyas encountered Trigartas in the evening (सूर्ये परिणते सति); Matsyas and Trigartas fought with one another anxious to get control of the cattle 4. 31. 1-2; (the battle is des-cribed in 4. 31. 3-24; 4. 32. 1 ff.); when Virāṭa was held captive by Trigartas, Matsyas who were much oppressed by Trigartas fled in fright (प्राद्रवन्त भयात् मत्स्यास् त्रिगर्तैर् अर्दिता भृशम् ॥ तेषु संत्रास्यमानेषु) 4. 32. 10-11; (13) It was decided that after Trigartas had left for the Matsya country the previous evening, Duryodhana should attack Virāṭa the next morning (4. 42. 10-11); it was also decided that Trigartas should first capture a large section of the cattle of Matsyas 4. 42. 9-10; accordingly the Trigar-tas reached the Matsya country and cap-tured their cattle 4. 33. 1, 4; when Virāṭa was released from the captivity of the Trigartas he told Kaṅka, Ballava and others that they had become the rulers of Matsyas (तस्माद् भवन्तो मत्स्यानाम् ईश्वराः सर्व एव हि) 4. 32. 39; Uttara told Bṛhannaḍā that he did not mind if the Kauravas drove away a large number of cows of Matsyas 4. 36. 24; Duryodhana told Bhīṣma that since the Kauravas wished to fight with the army of Matsyas they were looking for Uttara (उत्तरं मार्गमाणानां मत्स्यसेनां युयुत्सताम्) 4. 42. 8 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 4. 47. 8: उत्तरं गोग्रहं मार्गमाणानाम् इच्छताम् अस्मा-कम् । अनादरे षष्ठी॑अस्मान् अनादृत्येत्य् अर्थः); Duryodhana reminded Bhīṣma that Kauravas had marched on Matsyas for the sake of Trigartas since the Trigar-tas had reported many wrongs done to them by Matsyas (मत्स्यानां विप्रकारांस् ते बहून् अस्मान् अकीर्तयन्); (14) At the invitation of Virāṭa and Drupada, kings assembled (in the town of Virāṭa) to take side of Pāṇḍavas 5. 5. 14; (15) Karṇa told Bhīṣma that Yudhiṣṭhira wanted to get his share of kingdom because he had the support of Matsyas (बलम् आश्रित्य मत्स्यानाम्) 5. 21. 21; (16) Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Matsyas greeted Yudhiṣṭhira (मत्स्याः प्रतिनन्दन्ति) 5. 49., 7; however, they did not respect Dhṛta-rāṣṭra (मत्स्यास् त्वाम् अद्य नार्चन्ति) 5. 53. 17; (17) Arjuna told Saṃjaya that Duryodhana would repent to have waged war when Virāṭa, with his army of Matsyas who in appearance were not cruel, would enter the vital section of the army of their enemies (मर्मान्तरे शत्रुचमूं प्र-वेष्टा । मत्स्यैः सार्धम् अनृशंसरूपैः) 5. 47. 33; Saṃjaya too had earlier told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Matsyas were valorous (पराक्रान्ताः) 5. 52. 2; (18) Matsyas enumerated among those who were to fight on the side of Pāṇḍavas 5. 56. 12, 33; (19) Duryodhana assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra that he would defeat Matsyas (मत्स्यांश् च … श्रो-तासि विजितान् मया) 5. 60. 25; Karṇa assured Duryodhana that he would kill Matsyas with his ब्रह्मास्त्र 5. 61. 5; (20) Yudhi-ṣṭhira was prepared for peace for only five villages although he was supported, among others, by Matsyas ( … मत्स्यैश् च मधुसूदन । भवता चैव नाथेन पञ्च ग्रामा वृता मया) 5. 70. 14; (21) Mat-syas included among those who protected the army of Duryodhana (राजचमूं समे-ताम् । … गुप्ताम् … समत्स्यैः) 5. 158. 19-20; they are listed among the twelve heroic Janapadas whose chariot-fighters protected Bhīṣma in the war (द्वादशैते जनपदाः सर्वे शूरास् तनूत्यजः । महता रथ-वंशेन ते ऽभ्यरक्षन् पितामहं ॥ ) 6. 18. 13-14; at the start of the war, Matsyas were stationed in the middle of the army (सर्वसैन्यस्य मध्ये) 6. 20. 12 (were these Matsyas on the side of the Kauravas from Aparamatsya of the south who had fled from the main stock due to fear of Jarāsandha ? 2. 28. 4; 2. 13. 27); (22) On the first day of war, Bhīṣma killed (पातयाम् आस) Matsyas (those fighting for Pāṇḍavas) 6. 45. 54; (23) On the second day, he showered many arrows on them (ववर्ष शरवर्षाणि) 6. 48. 9; Matsyas (on the Pāṇḍavas' side) led by Bhīma attacked Niṣādas 6. 50. 8; later, when Bhīma killed Kaliṅgas, they honoured him 6. 50. 110; (24) On the third day, Matsyas led by Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa were stationed at the head of the Garuḍavyūha (6. 52. 2) of Kauravas 6. 52. 4; those who fought on the side of Pāṇḍavas raised a loud roar when they attacked the army of Kauravas 6. 55. 126; (25) On the fifth day, Matsyas marched on Duryodhana and Śakuni 6. 67. 20; they surrounded Arjuna fighting with Bhīṣma (परिवव्रुस् तदा पार्थम्) 6. 70. 33; (26) On the tenth day, Bhīṣma alone killed innumerable horses and elephants as also seven great warriors (सप्त महारथाः) from Matsyas and Pāñcālas; he also killed five thousand chariot-fighters and fourteen thousand foot-soldiers (पञ्च सहस्राणि रथिनाम् … । नराणां च … सहस्राणि चतुर्-दश) 6. 113. 21-22. Matsya and Pāñcāla warriors, while attacking Bhīṣma, raised cries (किलकिलाशब्दः); they covered him (छादयाम् आसुः) with excellent horses, hosts of chariots and elephants and foot-soldiers 6. 113. 47-48; (27) Dhṛtarāṣṭra enquired who opposed Droṇa when he wanted to fight with the chariot-fighters (रथानीकम्) of Virāṭa, the Matsya 7. 9. 67; he imagined that Dhṛṣṭadyumna must have killed Droṇa when he was encircled and excessively distracted by Matsyas and the rest (तैर् वृतः सर्वतः  … मत्स्यैर् अन्यैश् च भूमिपईः व्याकुली-कृतम् आचार्यम्) 7. 8. 27-28; (28) On the eleventh day, after assuming charge of the Kaurava army when Droṇa attacked Pāṇḍavas, their heroes and army, includ-ing Matsyas, checked his advance (and that of his army); that angered Droṇa (पर्यगृह्णंस् ततः सर्वे समायान्तम् … संगृह्यमाणां तां दृष्ट्वा … वाहिनीम्) 7. 7. 4, 7; assisted by Matsyas Virāṭa opposed Karṇa 7. 13. 36; Pāṇḍavas along with Matsyas held back Kaurava chariot-fighters headed by Aśvatthāman 7. 15. 11; (29) On the twelfth day, Matsyas attacked Droṇa when he killed Satyajit; they fled when Droṇa killed Śatānīka; Droṇa defeated Matsyas 7. 20. 18, 22-23; mighty Droṇa threw Matsyas into disorder (व्यक्षोभयत्) who were very much anger-ed due to the death of a Pāñcālya prince; when they got killed they trembled (मत्स्याः समकम्पन्त) 7. 20. 49, 53; pushed back by the arrows of Droṇa they were shaken (चलितान्) 7. 21. 7; Karṇa pointed out to Duryodhana Matsyas who, when instigated by Bhīma, followed him 7. 21. 23; the war between Matsyas and Kekayas (on the side of Kauravas) in which horses, elephants and chariot-fighters were not afraid became extremely confused (उत्पिञ्जलकं युद्धम् … अभीताश्वरथ-द्विपम्) 7. 24. 21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 25. 21: उत्पिञ्जलकम् अत्यन्ताकुलम्); (30) On the thirteenth day, when Abhimanyu attempted to break through the चक्रव्यूह Matsyas were to follow him 7. 34. 22; led by Yudhiṣṭhira they attacked the army of Droṇa to break it (द्रोणानीकं बिभित्स-वः) 7. 39. 17; striking Matsyas arranged properly their forces (व्यूढानीकाः प्र-हारिणः) and attacked Kaurava army; as a result Kaurava army turned back 7. 41. 3-4; Matsyas tried to attack Jayadratha 7. 42. 18; when Abhimanyu's death was reported to Subhadrā she expressed her disgust for Matsyas and others who could not help Abhimanyu (धिक् … मत्स्याञ् … ) 7. 55. 13; (31) On the fourteenth day, Matsyas led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, rushed straight towards Droṇa in order to help Sātyaki (आजग्मुर् अञ्जसा) 7. 73. 50; Droṇa defeated hundreds and thousands of Matsyas (अजयन् महाबाहुः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः) 7. 85. 31; Droṇa uttered loudly his own name while attacking oppo-nents (नाम विश्राव्य संयुगे) and killed many Matsyas (प्रचक्रे कदनं महत्) 7. 98. 26; Yudhiṣṭhira remembered Arjuna's former victory over Kauravas when Pāṇḍas vas lived in the town of Matsyas 7. 103. 38; at the advent of night, Matsyas led by Virāṭa attacked Droṇa (सायाह्ने 7. 129. 5; बभूव रजनी घोरा 7. 129. 12) 7. 129, 7; (32) During the night-war (14th-15th day) Matsyas followed Arjuna and Bhīma who intended to oppress respectively the sou-thern and the northern flanks of Kaurava army (बीभत्सुर् दक्षिणं पार्श्वम् उत्त-रं तु वृकोदरः) 7. 132. 40-41; 7. 136. 14; Duryodhana asked Karṇa to protect the army which was engulfed by angered Matsyas (मत्स्यकैकेयैः … । वृतान् समन्-तात् संक्रुद्धैर्) 7. 133. 2-3; when every-body believed that Duryodhana was killed by Bhīma, Matsyas rushed towards Droṇa to fight with him with utmost effort (सर्वो-द्योगेनाभिजग्मुर् द्रोणम् एव युयुत्सया) 7. 141. 60; Droṇa defeated all Matsyas and even killed many of them (मत्स्यांश् चैवाजयत् सर्वान् … हतेषु मत्स्येषु) 7. 161. 32. 35; (33) On the fifteenth day, Yudhiṣṭhira urged Matsya heroes (नरर्-षभान्) to go to help Bhīma and others; then their chariot-fighters attacked Droṇa 7. 164. 48-53; Droṇa killed five hundred Matsyas with his ब्रह्मास्त्र (पञ्चशतान् मत्स्यान्) 7. 164. 85, 79; later, Kṛpa inform-ed Aśvatthāman that when Matsyas tried to attack Droṇa they perished as dictated by Fate (संख्ये द्रोणरथं प्राप्य व्यनशन् कालचोदिताः) 7. 165. 101; Aśvat-thāman promised Duryodhana that he would rout Matsyas by his नारायणास्त्र (विद्रावयिष्यामि) 7. 166. 52; when Pāṇḍava army was routed by Aśvatthāman, Arjuna supported by Matsyas faced Kauravas 7. 172. 3; (34) On the sixteenth day, Matsyas and the rest surrounded Karṇa with their chariots, horses, elephants and valorous foot-soldiers and struck him with various weapons; bent on killing Karṇa they spoke harsh words to him (भाषन्तो वाग्भिर् उग्राभिः सर्वे कर्णवधे वृताः) 8. 21. 26-27; Karṇa scattered them away (अपोवाह) and killed them 8. 21. 28-29; (35) On the seventeenth day, Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman and Śakuni fought with Matsyas; prepared for the fight (दंशिताः), they attacked Karṇa and struck him with various wea-pons and showers of arrows 8. 32. 17, 43-44; the surviving Matsyas (मत्स्यशेषाः), to help Yudhiṣṭhira, checked Karṇa 8. 33. 22; Matsyas and others, protected by Arjuna were able to reduce the army of Kauravas (कृतः शत्रुगणक्षयः) 8. 51. 6; Kṛṣṇa remembered that earlier in the war, Bhīṣma had killed Matsyas with arrows 8. 51. 27; when Matsyas were gett-ing killed (वध्यमानाः) they attacked Karṇa and afflicted him with arrows (शरसंघैः समार्दयन्); but Karṇa killed them with sharp arrows 8. 56. 24; later, when Dhṛtarāṣṭra was informed that Karṇa was killed by Arjuna he remembered Karṇa's former victory over Matsyas 8. 5. 18; (36) On the last day of the war, Matsyas, especially, were again delighted while encouraging Yudhiṣṭhira to fulfil his vow to kill Śalya (ततः प्र-हर्षः … पुनर् आसीत् … । मत्स्यानां च विशेषतः । प्रतिज्ञां … धर्मराजस्य पूरयन् ॥ ) 9. 15. 26-27; beholding the feat of Śālva, Matsyas uttered cries of despair; their excellent heroes obstru-cted the elephant of Śālva from all sides (हाहाकारैर् नादयन्तः स्म युद्धे । द्विपं समन्ताद् रुरुधुर् नराग्र्याः) 9. 19. 21; (37) Night of the eighteenth day: after the massacre in the camp of Pāṇḍavas, Aśvatthāman boasted that he had killed all the surviving Matsyas and reported the event to Duryodhana (मत्स्यशेषाश् च सर्वे विनिहता मया) 10. 8. 150; 10. 9. 49; the event later reported to Kuntī by Yudhiṣṭhira 15. 44. 33-34; (38) Gāndhārī pointed out to Kṛṣṇa the women of noble family of Virāṭa (मत्स्यराजकुलस्त्रियः) trying to take away Uttarā from the dead body of Abhimanyu; then they themselves, more afflicted, cried and lamented over the death of Virāṭa 11. 20. 27-28. E. Past event: King Sahaja of Cedis and Matsyas listed by Bhīma among eighteen kings who extirpated their kinsmen, friends and rela-tives 5. 72. 16. F. Mostly Virāṭa, occa-sionally some others, designated in various ways as king or the best of the Matsyas: A. मद्र: Madra, Madraka m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people; referred to as Madraka specially when derision was in-tended (8. अध्यायस् 27, 30); otherwise मद्रक for मद्र very likely due to metrical reasons. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (सौधा मद्रा … ) 6. 10. 40. B. Origin: Bhadrā, wife of Vyuṣitāśva, gave birth to four Madra sons (सा … सुषुवे देवी … चतुरो मद्रान् सुतान् … ) 1. 112. 33. C. Description: Of their warriors; brave (शूर) 9. 17. 4, 14, 35; heroic (वीर) 9. 7. 23; 9. 17. 1, 17; energetic (तरस्विन्) 9. 22. 25; of great valour (महावीर्य) 8. 31. 21; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 8. 32. 19; 9. 6. 7; 9. 17. 5, 11; skilled in fight-ing while riding elephants (गजयोधिन्; गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 2-3; great archers (महेष्वास) 9. 17. 23; versed in the science of archery (धनुर्वेदविद्) and difficult to be conquered by enemies (अजेयाः शत्रुभिर् युधि) 6. 57. 13; of the people in general; wicked (दुरात्मन्) 8. 27. 71, 74; vile, of despicable speech (नराधम, क्षुद्रवाक्य) 8. 27. 73; untruthful, not straightforward (नित्यं चानृतिको ऽनृजुः) 8. 27. 74; croocked (जिह्म) 8. 30. 62; imprudent (अचेतस्) 8. 30. 55; fickle (मद्रको हि सचापलः) 8. 27. 80; their country rated by Karṇa as reprehensible (कुदेश), sinful (पापदेश) 8. 27. 67-68, 70, 91. D. Their nature, behaviour: Although they lived in countries they led the life of Dasyus (सर्वे विषयवासिनः । … सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः ॥ ) 12. 65. 15; Karṇa repeated for Śalya गाथास् describing the nature and behaviour of Madrakas, which were once recited by certain Brāhmaṇas in the royal assembly of Kurus: a Madraka was a habitual violator of contracts; who-ever hated Brāhmaṇas was a Madraka; there could be no companionship with a Madraka; Madrakas were wicked to the bitter end (मित्रध्रुङ् मद्रको नित्यं यो नो द्वेष्टि स मद्रकः । मद्रके संगतं नास्ति … यावदन्तं हि दौरा-त्म्यं मद्रकेष्व् इति नः श्रुतम् ॥ ) 8. 27. 73-74; Madraka men and women united with one another without regard for family or any other relationship; they could never be religious; they ate churn-ed meal, drank wine, ate beef, roared and danced 8. 27. 75-78; one should neither form friendship nor have enmity with Madrakas with whom religion was lost and whose unauspicious deeds were well known (मद्रकेषु विलुप्तेषु प्रख्याता-शुभकर्मसु । नापि वैरं न सौहार्दं मद्रकेषु समाचरेत् ॥ ) 8. 27. 79; one should not touch Madrakas (मद्रकेषु च दुःस्पर्शम्) 8. 27. 80; Madraka women are severely criticized for their shameful acts and licentious behaviour 8. 27. 85-89; from beginning to the end Madrakas followed reprehensible bad paths; they were म्लेच्छस् born in sinful countries and had no sense of religion; there could be no question of their knowing धर्म (शक्यं वक्तुं भवेद् बहु । आ केशाग्रान् नखाग्राच् च वक्तव्येषु कुवर्त्मसु ॥ मद्रका … धर्मं विद्युः कथं त्य् थ । पापदेशोद्भवा म्लेच्छा धर्माणाम् अविचक्षणाः ॥ ) 8. 27. 90-91; one of the old Brāhmaṇas who had visited many countries, when he met Dhṛtarāṣṭra, he condemned Bāhlīkas and also Madras (मद्रांश् च कुत्सयन् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्) 8. 30. 9; therefore what he said despising specifically the Bāhlīkas applied also to Madrakas 8. 30. 10-26; a certain Brāh-maṇa told an artisan (शील्पिन्) what he had heard about Madrakas: among Madrakas in every family there was only one wise person, the rest behaved as they liked; their behaviour led to confusion of धर्म (भवत्य् एकः कुले विप्रः शिष्टान्ये कामचारिणः । एतन् मया श्रुतं तत्र धर्मसंकरकारकम् । ) 8. 30. 55-56; another Brāhmaṇa told the Kuru assembly describing Madras as croocked and said that all countries, except Madras and Pañcanadas, followed the ancient धर्म (धर्मं पुराणम् उपजीवन्ति सन्तो मद्रान् ऋते पञ्चनदांश् च जिह्मान्) 8. 30. 62; according to a Rākṣasa named Kalmāṣapāda, who was held by a king, Madra women were as good as the dirt on the bodies of women (स्त्रीणां मद्रस्त्रियो मलम्) 8. 30. 68; he further said that the dirt on the bodies of Madra-kas, whose sacrifices were performed by those whose sacrificial priests were of warrior class, would be the dirt of the king if he did not release Kalmāṣapāda (राजयाजकयाज्यानां मद्रकाणां च यन् मलम् । तद् भवेद् वै तव मलं यद्य् अस्मान् न विमुञ्चसि ॥ ) 8. 30. 71. E. Epic events: (1) Bhīṣma went to the town of Madras (मद्राणां पुटभेदनम्) and bought Mādrī, the daughter of the Madra king, for Pāṇḍu 1. 105. 4-5; (2) At the birth of Arjuna (जातमात्रे कुमारे तु 1. 114. 28) a noncorporeal voice prophesied that he (Arjuna) would bring Madras under control (मद्रान् वशे कृत्वा) 1. 114. 31; (according to a later reference, this event happened a week after Arjuna was born सप्ताहजाते त्वयि 8. 48. 6); (3) Nakula in his expedition to the west before the Rāja-sūya (2. 29. 2; 1. 23. 10) went to Śākala, the town of Madras (मद्राणाम् पुट-भेदनम्) and subdued Śalya with affection (प्रीतिपूर्वेण … चक्रे वशे बली) 2. 29. 13; (4) Madra Kṣatriyas brought wealth in hundreds as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira (मद्रकेकयाः । … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 13, 16; (5) On the second day of war, Madrakas were to protect Bhīṣma (मद्रकाः … भीष्मम् एवाभिरक्षन्तु) 6. 47. 7, 9; (6) On the third day, Madrakas (मद्रकाः) were posted at the ‘neck’ (ग्रीवायाम्) of the Gāruḍavyūha of Kauravas 6. 52. 2, 5; (7) On the fourth day, principal Madra warriors (मद्राश् च … मुख्याः) with Trigartas and Kekayas, thirtyfive thousand strong, encircled Arjuna and Abhimanyu; then Dhṛṣṭadyumna, assisted by a large army, attacked Madraka army (मद्रका-नीकम्) and killed them, each one with ten arrows (मद्रकान् हत्वा दशभिर् दशभिः शरैः) 6. 57. 12-13, 16, 19; (8) On the fifth day, Madras collected round the king of Kaliṅgas 6. 67. 13; (9) On the sixth day, Madras led by Bhaga-datta (प्राग्ज्योतिषः) stood at the chest (उरसि) of the Krauñcavyūha of Kauravas 6. 71. 18, 14; (10) On the eleventh day, Madras led by Duryodhana followed Karṇa in the Śakaṭavyūha of Kauravas 7. 6. 6-7, 15; (11) On the twelfth day, Suśarman, supported by Madrakas (सहितो मद्रकैर् अपि), took oath to kill Arjuna 7. 16. 20; on that day, Madras stood at the neck (ग्रीवायाम्) of the Suparṇavyūha (7. 19. 4) by hundreds of thousands with elephants, horses, chariots and foot-soldiers (मद्रकेकयाः । गजाश्वरथपत्त्यौघास् तस्थुः शतसहस्रशः ॥ ) 7. 19. 8; Madras were also posted at the back of the Vyūha (पृष्ठे … पौण्ड्रमद्रकाः) 7. 19. 11; (12) During the night war, Yudhiṣṭhira killed a large number of Madrakas (मद्रकाणां गणान् युधि) 7. 132. 25; Arjuna did the same 7. 136. 5; (13) In the summary narration of the first fifteen days of war Saṃjaya mentioned Madrakas among those who were killed by Arjuna (मालवा मद्रकाश् चैव) 8. 4. 46; (14) Dhṛtarāṣṭra remembered that Karṇa had once defeated Madrakas and made them pay tribute (अजईषीद्॥। मद्रकान् … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 18, 20; (a reference to Karṇa's दिग्विजय before Duryodhana's Vaiṣṇavayāga (3. 241. 29, 32; 3. App. I. 24. 28-34); (15) On the sixteenth day, Śalya with his large army of Madra warriors stood at the left foot of the Makaravyūha of Kauravas (अनुपादस् तु वामस् … महत्या सेनया सार्धं मद्रदेशसमु-त्थया ॥ ) 8. 7. 19, 14; on the same day, elephant drivers drove Madra and other warriors, skilled in fighting battles while riding elephants; they showered Dhṛṣṭadyumna with arrows, तोमरस् and नाराच arrows; Dhṛṣṭadyumna pierced the enemy elephants with arrows—each one with ten, six or eight arrows; the Pāṇḍava warriors succeeded in routing the attack of the elephants (हस्तिभिस् तु महामात्रास् … पार्षतम् अभ्ययुः ॥ … गजयोधिनः … मद्रा दशार्णा … गजयुद्धेषु कुश-लाः … ॥ ) 8. 17. 1-6; (एवं हत्वा तव गजान्) 8. 17. 28; (16) On the seventeenth day, Duryodhana, protected by Madras and Kekayas, followed Duḥśāsana, who was at the back (व्यूहस्य पृष्ठतः) of the Bārhaspatyavyūha of Kauravas 8. 31. 19, 21, 26; Duryodhana protected by Madra महारथस् was guarding Karṇa from all sides 8. 32. 19; angered Bhīma fought with Madras along with Kurus and Kekayas; he killed their chariot-fighters by thousands along with their charioteers, horses, ele-phants and foot-soldiers 8. 40. 69, 71-73; (17) On the eighteenth day, when Śalya was consecrated as the सेनापति of Kaura-vas, Madrakas were delighted and they praised Śalya (हृष्टाश् चासन् … मद्रकाश् च  … । तुष्टुवुश् चैव) 9. 6. 7; Śalya was at the head of the Sarvatobhadravyūha (मुखं व्यूहस्य) along with Madraka heroes (मद्रकैः सहितो वीरैः) 9. 7. 23, 19; (18) On the eighteenth day, Duryodhana tried to check seven hundred chariot-fighters of Madras who rushed forward from the main army to continue to fight even after the death of Śalya (मद्रराजपदानुगाः । रथाः सप्त शता वीरा निर्ययुर् महतो बलात् ॥ न गन्तव्यं न गन्तव्यम् इति मद्रान् अवारयत्); though they were repea-tedly asked to stop marching forward, Madras entered the army of Pāṇḍavas to kill Yudhiṣṭhira; intent on fighting (कृत-चित्ताः स्म योधने) they made twangs from their bows and fought with Pāṇḍavas 9. 17. 1-4; Arjuna rushed to help Yudhi-ṣṭhira who was oppressed by great Madra chariot-fighters desirous of doing what was dear to the king of Madras (धर्म-पुत्रं च पीडितम् । मद्रराजप्रिये युक्तैर् मद्रकाणां महारथैः ॥ ); encircled by Pāṇḍavas, Madra heroes repeatedly agitated their army (ते समन्तात् परिवृताः पाण्डवैः पुरुषर्षभाः । क्षोभयन्ति स्म तां सेनाम्॥। । ;अक्षोभ्यत तदा राजन् पाण्डूनां ध्वजिनी पुणः); fighting whole-heartedly the Madra chariot-fighters made their opponents tremble (त्यक्ता-त्मानः … कम्पयन्ति स्म) 9. 17. 5, 9-11; they shouted loudly asking the where-abouts of Yudhiṣṭhira and other Pāṇḍava warriors; Draupadī's sons and Sātyaki attacked them; Madras, with the wheels of their chariots and flag-staffs broken, were killed by Pāṇḍavas 9. 17. 12, 14-15; when they again rushed at Pāṇḍavas, Duryodhana tried to pacify them urging them to return; but no one listened to him 9. 17. 16-17; Śakuni blamed Duryodhana since Madras were being killed in the very presence of Kaurava heroes; he reminded him that Kurus and Madras had decided to fight together (सहितैर् नाम योद्धव्यम् इत्य् एष समयः कृतः) 9. 17. 17-20; when Duryodhana complained that the Madra warriors did not listen to him when he tried to check them, Śakuni told him that angered fighters do not obey the orders of their seniors; that was not the time either to get angry with Madras or neglect them (अलं क्रोद्धुं तथल्तेषां नायं काल उपेक्षितुम्); he advised Duryo-dhana collectively to go to save the great (Madra) archers who were loyal to Śalya (परित्रातुं महेष्वासान् मद्रराजपदानु-गान्) 9. 17. 21-24; accordingly Duryo-dhana with his large army went to the help of Madra warriors; Pāṇḍavas, seeing Madra warriors fighting, attacked them; in the battle that ensued Madras were killed 9. 17. 25-28; the battle described 9. 17. 30-37; when Duryodhana's army realized that the large army of Śalya was being killed, they again turned away from the scene of fight (ततो हतम् अभिप्रेक्ष्य मद्रराजबलं महत् । दुर्योधनबलं सर्वं पुनर् आसीत् पराङ्मुखम्) 9. 17. 38; Śakuni told the energetic (तरस्विनः) Madra warriors to attack the vanguard of the Pāṇḍava army and that he himself, would take in the rear (युध्यध्वम् अग्रतो यावत् पृष्ठतो हन्मि पाण्डवान्); they raised sound and attacked Pāṇḍavas who showered arrows and killed the army of Śalya; seeing that, Duryo-dhana's army again turned away; Śakuni again blamed them and pointed out that the Madra army consisting of ten thousand horses and fighting with bright lances had fought heroically and brought about great destruction of the enemies (अनीकं दश-साहस्रम् अश्वानां … । आसिद् गान्धारराजस्य विमलप्रासयोधिनाम् । बलेन तेन विक्र-म्य वर्तमाने जनक्षये) 9. 22. 24-30.
