9. 16. 56; 14. 59. 22; (xv) मद्रेश्वर: (i) Śalya 1. 2. 173; 6. 43. 28; 6. 79. 42, 53; 6. 80. 53; 6. 110. 27; 6. 112. 39; 7. 44. 9; 7. 95. 16; 8. 23. 2, 43; 8. 27. 30; 9. 6. 33; 9. 12. 4; 9. 12, 25, 36; 9. 14. 19; (ii) father of Mādrī (not named) 1. 103. 5; (xvi) मद्राणाम् ईश्वर-: Śalya 1. 181. 8; 6. 67. 19; 7. 14. 32; 7. 70. 39; 7. 165. 77; 8. 34. 11, 15; 9. 6. 10; 9. 11. 25; 9. 12. 17; 9. 14. 28, 30; D. The best (lit. the bull) of the Madras: मद्राणां ऋषभ- Śalya 6. 67. 19; 9. 11. 25.
मधुमत्: Madhumant m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa; listed along with Pārasīkas, hence, perhaps, belonged to the north-west (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तिलकाः पारसीकाश् च मधुमन्तः) 6. 10. 51.
मधुमन्त्: Madhumant m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa; listed along with Pārasīkas, hence, perhaps, belonged to the north-west (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तिलकाः पारसीकाश् च मधुमन्तः) 6. 10. 51.
मध्यदेश: Madhyadeśa, Madhyama deśa m. (sg.): The midland country and its people. A. Epic events: (1) Vṛṣṇis (2. 13. 51, 59) and Mādhavas (2. 13. 52) who, along with Kṛṣṇa, left Mathurā (2. 13. 44) and went to Kuśasthalī in the west always remembered the Madhyama deśa (वीराः स्मरन्तो मध्यमं देशं … ) 2. 13. 59; (2) Many kings of midland (बहवो राजानो मध्यदेशजाः) attended the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhita 2. 31. 17; (3) The warriors of Madhyadeśa along with others comprised the unassailable royal army of Kauravas (राजचमूं … दुराधर्षैर् … कुरुमध्य-देशैर् … ) 5. 158. 19-20. B. Past events: (1) Once a large settlement of Brāhmaṇas existed in a part of the Madhyadeśa between the rivers Gaṅgā and Yamunā and adjacent to the mountain Yāmuna (मध्यदेशे … गङ्गायमुनयोर् मध्ये यामुनस्य गिरेर् अधः) 13. 67. 3; Yama told Brāhmaṇas of this settlement the importance of gifting sesame seeds and lamps 13. 67. 15-27; (2) A Brāhmaṇa named Gautama (12. 162. 33) of the Madhyadeśa (मध्यदेशीयः 12. 162. 29) happened to visit a settlement of the Dasyus (दस्युग्राम 12. 162. 37) and lived there; when another Brāhmaṇa later visited the same settlement he recognized Gautama as one who belonged to the Madhyadeśa and asked him how he came to live like a Dasyu (मध्यदेशपरिज्ञातो दस्युभावं गतः कथम्) 12. 162. 44; when asked by Virūpākṣa, the chief of Rākṣasas, Gautama told him that he belonged to Midland but he lived in the house of a Śabara (मध्य-देशप्रसूतो ऽहं वासो मे शबरालये) 12. 165. 5.
मध्यमिकाय: Madhyamikāya m. (pl.): Designation of a people (living in the Madhyama country ?). They lived to the west of Khāṇḍava-prastha (खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; Nakula brought them under control, along with the Vāṭadhāna Brāhmaṇas, during his expedition to the west (2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 10) before the Rāja-sūya (वशे चक्रे॥।तथा मध्यमिकायांश् च वाटधानान् द्विजान् अथ) 2. 29. 6-7. [See Madhyadeśa].
मनोनुग: Manonuga m. (sg.): Name of a Deśa of Krauñcadvīpa. It was related to the second mountain Vāmana of the Krauñcadvīpa; the Deśa after Manonuga was called Uṣṇa (वामन-स्य मनोनुगः ॥ मनोनुगात् परश् चोष्णो देशः) 6. 13. 20-21, 17; all Deśas of Krauñcadvīpa were frequented by gods and Gandharvas (एते देशा महाराज देव-गन्धर्वसेविताः) 6. 13. 23.
मन्दक: Mandaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (गोविन्दा मन्दकाः) 6. 10. 42.
मन्दग: Mandaga m. (sg. pl.): Name of a Janapada of the Śākadvīpa. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the four Janapadas of Śākadvīpa (तत्र जनपदाश् चत्वारो … मन्दगास् तथा) 6. 12. 33. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य), respected by the people (लोक-संमत) 6. 12. 33. C. Characteristic: The Śūdras of this Janapada always observed their धर्म (शूद्रास् तु मन्दगे नित्यं पुरुषा धर्मशीलिनः) 6. 12. 35; for another characteristic common to all Janapadas of Śākadvīpa see Maga.
मरध: Maradha m. (pl.): Name of a people. Listed by Saṃjaya, along with Cīnas, among the northern Mlecchas of Bhārata-varṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … तथ-इव मरधाश् चीनास् … ) 6. 10. 63, 65; (they were also probably reckoned as a Janapada (6. 10. 37) or a Deśa (6. 10. 68)); these म्लेच्छ tribes were known to be rough (दारुणा म्लेच्छजातयः) 6. 10. 64.
मरु: Maru, Marubhūmi, Marubhauma m. f. (sg., pl.): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; मरुभौमाश् च मारिष) 6. 10. 46; to the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha (प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 5; 2. 23. 10; Kāmyaka forest was at the northern extremity of Maru-bhūmi (काम्यकं काननोत्तमम् । मरु-भूमेः शिरः ख्यातम्) 3. 244. 13; near the sea, where once Sarasvatī flew (13. 139. 26; see Past event below). B. Characte-ristic: As mostly unfertile land, it is con-trasted with those producing abundant corn (मरुभूमिं … तथैव बहुधा-न्यकम्) 2. 29. 5. C. Epic events: (1) Nakula brought completely under control the whole of Marubhūmi in his expedition to the west before the Rāja-sūya (मरुभूमिं च कार्त्स्न्येन … वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 5-6; (2) Since there was not enough room in Hāstinapura, the large army of Kauravas spread beyond the land of five rivers even up to the whole of Marubhūmi (न हास्तिनपुरे राजन्न् अव-काशो ऽभवत् तदा । … ततः पञ्चनदं चैव … मरुभूमिश् च केवला । … एष देशः … बभूव कौरवेयाणाम् बलेन सुसमाकुलः ॥ ) 5. 19. 28-29, 31; (3) After the mutual killings of Yādavas, Vasudeva remembered that once Kṛṣṇa had killed the kings of Marubhūmi ((विदेहान्) अकरोत् … मरुभूमौ च पार्थिवान्) 16. 7. 9-10. D. Past event: Utathya asked Sarasvatī to disappear in the Maru country; he wanted the land, when deserted by the river, to be unholy; in that land which was thus thoroughly pounded, Varuṇa handed over Utathya his wife who was abducted by him (अदृश्या गच्छ भीरु त्वम् सरस्वति मरुं प्रति । … अपुण्य एष भवतु देशस् त्यक्तस् त्वया शुभे ॥ तस्मिन् संचूर्णिते देशे भद्राम् आदाय वारिपः । अददाच् छर-णं गत्वा भार्याम् आङ्गिरसाय वै) 13. 139. 26-27.
मर्त्य: Martya m. (pl.): Name of a coun-try (?). The Aśokatīrtha, abounding in आश्र-मस्, was located in the Martya country (?) in the south (दक्षिणस्यां तु पुण्यानि शृणु तीर्थानि भारत) 3. 86. 1; (अशोक-तीर्थं मर्त्येषु) 3. 86. 10.
मलद: Malada m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the eleventh day of war, their warriors were among those who, led by Duḥśāsana, protected the extreme end of the left wing of Droṇa's army (दुःशासन-मुखा यत्ताः सव्यं पार्श्वम् अपालयन् ॥ तेषां प्रपक्षाः … शूद्राश् च मलदत्ः सह) 7. 6. 4-6; (or were they among those who, led by Duryodhana, followed Karṇa ? तवात्मजं पुरस्कृत्य सूतपुत्रस्य पृष्ठ-तः 7. 6. 7).
मल्ल: Malla m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; distinguished as Uttara, Uttama Mallas and Dakṣlṇa Mallas; called जनपद and also राष्ट्र (4. 1. 8-9). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (मल्लाः सुदेष्णाः) 6. 10. 45; between Gopālakaccha and the Himālayas 2. 27. 3-4; little to the east of Khāṇḍavaprastha and then to the north; Bhīma first went to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1, 7, 9; 2. 23. 9) before he reached the country of Mallas 2. 27. 3, 11 (see Epic event below); listed by Arjuna among the countries around Kurus (परितः कुरून् … मल्लाः शाल्वा युगन्धराः) 4. 1. 9. B. Description: Pleasant (रम्य, रमणीय), protected (गुप्त), producing abundant corn (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 8-9. C. Epic event: Bhīmasena in his expedition to the east before the Rājasūya defeated Uttaramallas, Uttamamallas along with the king of the Mallas and then also defeated the Dakṣiṇamallas (सोत्तमान् अपि चोत्तरान् । मल्लानाम् अधिपं चैव पार्थिवम् व्यजस् यत् प्रभुः ॥ ) 2. 27. 3; (ततो दक्षिणस् मल्लांश् च … तरसैवाजयद् भीमो … ) 2. 27. 11. (See the next).
मल्लक: Mallaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षि-णा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (मालका मल्लकाश् चैव) 6. 10. 61. [See Malla].
मशक: Maśaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada of the Śākadvīpa. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the four Janapadas of Śākadvīpa (तत्र … जनपदाश् चत्वारो … मशकाश् चैव) 6. 12. 33. B. Description; Holy (पुण्य), respected by people (लोकसं-मत) 6. 12. 33. C. Characteristic: In Maśaka all Kṣatriyas were religious; they fulfilled all wishes (of the people) (मश-केषु तु राजन्या धार्मिकाः सर्वकामदाः) 6. 12. 34; for another characteristic which is common to all four Janapadas of Śāka-dvīpa, see Maga.
महाकाश: Mahākāśa m.: Name of a Varṣa of the Śākadvīpa. Listed by Saṃjaya among the Varṣas of Sākadvīpa; it was related to mountain Mahāmeru (वर्षाणि तेषु … महामेरुर् महाकाशो … ) 6. 12. 23.
महौजस्: Mahaujas m. (pl.): Name of a people. Varapra, the king of Mahaujas people, listed by Bhīmasena among the eighteen kings who in the past extirpated their kinsmen, friends and relatives (अष्टादशेमे राजानः … । ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान् ॥ ) 5. 72. 11; (वर-प्रश् च महौजसाम्) 5. 72. 15.
मह्युत्तर: Mahyuttara m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (मह्युत्तराः प्रा-वृषेया … ) 6. 10. 49.
माकन्दि: Mākandi f.: Name of the southern part of the Pāñcāla country. A. Location: Region south of Gaṅga up to the river Carmaṇvatī (माकन्दीम् अथ गङ्गायास् तीरे … । दक्षिणांश् चैव पाञ्चालान् यावच् चर्मण्वती नदी) 1. 128. 15; (राजासि दक्षिणे कूले भागीरथ्याहम् उत्तरे । ) 1. 128. 12. B. Its Capital: Kāmpilya, the best of the towns (काम्-पिल्यं च पुरोत्तमम्) 1. 128. 15. C. Description: It had many Janapadas (माकन्दीम्॥।जनपदायुताम्) 1. 128. 15. D. Epic event: Defeated Drupada was offered by Droṇa half of the kingdom of the Pāñcāla country (1. 128. 10); Dru-pada then went to Mākandī and settled down at Kāmpilya 1. 128. 15.
मागध: Mā̆gadha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people: also called Magadha-rāṣṭra (1. 105. 10); its capital town Rāja-gṛha (1. 105. 10; 1. 196. 17; 14. 83. 2). A. Location: Listed twice by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (विदेहका मागधाश् च) 6. 10. 44; (बहिर्गिर्याङ्ग-मलदा मागधा मानवर्जकाः) 6. 10. 48; in the east, beyond Suhmas and Prācya-suhmas; beyond the rivers Gaṅgā and Śoṇa and near the mountain Goratha (see below Epic events No. 5 and 6). B. Description: The country of Magadha was large, charming, rich in cattle, having water all the year round, free from disease, abounding in excellent dwelling houses and bright (एष पार्थ महान् स्वादुः पशुमान् नित्यम् अम्बुमान् । निरामयः सुवेश्ंआढ्यो निवेशो मागधः शुभः) 2. 19. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 21. 1; निवेशो विन्यासः); the Magadha land was covered with Kurava trees (कुरवोरश्छदं … मागधं क्षेत्रम्) 2. 18. 29; it could not be avoided by clouds due to the presence of the serpent Maṇi (अपरिहार्या मेघानां मागधेयं मणेः कृते) 2. 19. 10; the Magadha warriors were brave (शूर) 7. 82. 35, ener-getic (तरस्विन्) 8. 31. 11, and performers of exploits (पराक्रान्त) 5. 52. 2; skilled in fighting while riding elephants (गज-योधिन्, गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 2-3; their women were long-eyed (आयतनेत्र) and had sweet voice (सुस्वर) 11. 25. 8: C. Characteristic of the people: Karṇa told Śalya that Magadhas knew what the eternal धर्म was (मगधास् तथा ॥ … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्) 8. 30. 60-61; Māgadha elders followed the prescribed धर्मस् (मागधाश् च शिष्टान् धर्मान् उपजीवन्ति वृद्धाः) 8. 30. 75; Magadhas understood the intentions of others (even if they were not expressed in so many words) (इङ्गितज्ञाश् च मग-धाः) 8. 30. 79. D. Epic events: (1) Bhīṣma defeated all Māgadha warriors when he forcibly carried away two prin-cesses for Vicitravīrya 13. 44. 37; (2) Pāṇḍu in his conquest of the earth killed Dārva, the protector of Magadharāṣṭra, at Rājagṛha (गोप्ता मगधराष्ट्रस्य) 1. 105. 10; (3) At the birth of Jarāsandha, his father Bṛhadratha ordered a festival for the Magadha people in honour of the Rākṣasī Jarā (आज्ञापयच् च … मागधेषु महोत्स-वम्) 2. 17. 5; (4) Once the sage Caṇḍa-kauśika happened to visit the Magadha country (मगधान् उपचक्राम) 2. 17. 8; (5) Kṛṣṇa, along with Bhīma and Arjuna, left Khāṇḍavaprastha for the Magadha country (प्रतस्थुर् मागधं प्रति); proceeding towards the east, they reached the Magadha land after crossing the rivers Gaṅgā and Śoṇa; when they reached the Goratha mountain they saw the capital town of Magadha (उत्तीर्य गङ्गां शोणं च सर्वे ते प्राङ्मुखास् त्रयः … जग्मुर् मागधं क्षेत्रम् ॥ … गोरथं गिरिम् आसाद्य ददृशुर् मागधं पुरम् ॥ ) 2. 18. 21, 29-30; they proceeded towards the capital town of the Magadha country (माग-धं पुरम्) and attacked the very beautiful surroundings of the चैत्यक of Māgadhas (मागधानां सुरुचिरं चैत्यकान्तम् उपाद्रवन्) 2. 19. 12, 17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 21. 15: चैत्यकं नगरसूचकम्); when they had entered the town, the Magadha people, seeing them, were wonderstruck 2. 19. 19, 27; Kṛṣṇa advised Jarāsandha not to disregard others because he had the support of the large and strong army of Māgadhas (मागधैर् विपुलैः सैन्यैर् बाहुल्यबलदर्पितैः) 2. 20. 18; hearing the loud roar of Bhīma and Jarāsandha the people of Magadha were much afraid, their pregnant women lost their foetus (स्त्रीणां गर्भाश् च सुस्रुवुः); they wondered whether the Himālaya had broken down or whether the earth was being torn apart (किं नु स्विद् धिमवान् भिन्नः किं नु स्विद् दीर्यते मही । इति स्म मागधा जज्ञुर् … ) 2. 22. 8-9; when the Magadha people saw Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma and Arjuna riding the chariot of Jarāsandha, they were astounded 2. 22. 19; (6) Bhīma in his expedition before the Rājasūya went towards the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 27. 1; 2. 23. 9); he defeated Suhmas and Prācyasuhmas and then marched on Magadha; there he pacified the son of Jarāsandha and collected tribute from him (ततः सुह्मान् प्राच्यसुह्मान् … विजित्य … मागधान् उपयाद् … ॥ जारासन्धिं सान्त्व-यित्वा करे च विनिवेश्य ह) 2. 27. 14, 16; Later, Sahadeva (not Bhīma) is said to have defeated Magadhas in battle (यः काशीन् अङ्गमगधान् … युधाजयत् । तेन  … सहदेवेन) 5. 49. 28; (7) On the second day of war, Droṇa, along with Māgadhas and others, followed Bhīṣma in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas 6. 47. 12, 10: (8) On the third day, Māgadhas, equipped for battle, stood at the right wing of the Garuḍavyūha of Kauravas (मागधाश् च … दक्षिणं पक्षम् आसाद्य स्थिता व्यूहस्य दंशिताः) 6. 52. 8, 3; (9) On the fourth day, the Magadha army of ten thousand energetic elephants led by Jayatsena (not named) attacked Bhīma (अनीकं दशसाहस्रं कुञ्जराणां तर-स्विनां । मागधं पुरतः कृत्वा भीम-सेनं समभ्ययात् ॥ ) 6. 58. 31; (10) On the eighth day, Bhagadatta, along with Māgadha warriors and others follow-ed Droṇa in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas 6. 83. 8; (11) On the twelfth day, Māgadhas and others were stationed at the back (पृष्ठे) of the Suparṇavyūha of the Kauravas 7. 19. 11, 4-5; (12) On the fourteenth day, when Vyāghradatta was killed by Sātyaki, Māgadhas rushed towards Sātyaki and showered him with arrows and तोमरस् by thousands and also with भिण्डिपाल, प्रास and मुद्गर; but Sātyaki easily defeated them all and they fled 7. 82. 33-36; (13) After the death of Droṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lamenting, recalled Kṛṣṇa's exploits which included his victory over Māgadhas 7. 10. 15; (14) On the sixteenth day, Māgadhas (on Pāṇḍavas' side) attack-ed the Kaurava army (मागधाश् चापि दुद्रुवुः) 8. 8. 19; (15) The same day, Māgadhas and others on the side of Kaura-vas, skilled in fighting while riding ele-phants, were driven by the elephant-riders towards Dhṛṣṭadyumna; they showered him with arrows, तोमरस् and नाराचस्; Dhṛṣṭadyumna pierced the elephants of the enemies with arrows-each one with ten, six or eight arrows; Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Pāṇḍava heroes succeeded in routing the attack of elephants (हस्तिभिस् तु महामात्रा … पार्षतम् अभ्ययुः ॥ … गज-योधिनः । … मागधास् ताम्रलिप्तकाः ॥ गजयुद्देषु कुशलाः … ) 8. 17. 1-6; (एवं हत्वा तव गजान् ॥ ) 8. 17. 28; (16) On the seventeenth day, Kṛpa, along with the energetic Māgadha warriors, stood on the right side of the Bārhaspatyavyūha (8. 31. 26) of the Kauravas (कृपः शारद्वतो राजन् मागधश् च (for मागधाश् च ?) तरस्विनः । सात्वतः कृतवर्मा च दक्षि-णं पक्षम् आश्रिताः ॥ 8. 31. 11 (the cr. edn. adopts the reading मागधः (sg.); but it is almost certain that we have to read मागधाः (pl.); the plural तरस्विनः is hardly meant to include Kṛpa, Kṛtavar-man and some Māgadha prince (sg.); he cannot be Jayatsena since he was already killed by Abhimanyu; adjective like तरस्विनः are used with reference to general warriors; there are variant read-ings to support मागधाः; the editor has no note on the stanza); the same day, Bhīma killed many Māgadhas (siding with Kauravas) 8. 49. 79; (17) On the eighteenth day, to praise Bhīma before his duel with Duryodhana, Kṛṣṇa reminded him that he had formerly killed many Māgadhas along with other warriors 9. 32. 32; (18) After the war Gāndhārī pointed out to Kṛṣṇa Māgadhī women, who in grief had discarded their gold ornaments, surrounding the dead body of Jayatsena and weeping; they rolled on the ground; their wailing sound deluded the mind of Gāndhārī ( … प्ररुदिता मागध्यः पश्य योषितः ॥ प्रकीर्ण-स्वर्णाभरणा रुदन्त्यः शोककर्शिताः । … मागध्यः शेरते भुवि ॥ ) 11. 25. 7, 9; (आसां … मनःश्रुतिहरो नादो मनो मोहयतीव मे) 11. 25. 8; (19) While recounting Kṛṣṇa's past exploits, Vasu-deva remembered that Kṛṣṇa had slain Māgadha Kings (चक्रे (विदेहान्) कालिङ्ग-मागधान्) 16. 7. 10. E. Past events; (1) The eight sons of Asurī Kālakā were born as kings; the first of them, the great Asura, was Jayatsena who was the illustrious king of the Magadha country (कालकायास् तु ये पुत्रास् तेषाम् अष्टौ नराधिपाः । जज्ञिरे … ॥ मगधेषु जयत्-सेनः श्रीमान् आसीत् स पार्थिवः । अष्टानां प्रवरस् तेषां कालेयानां महासुरः ॥ ) 1. 61. 45-46; (2) Kākṣīva(t) and others were born of Śūdrā Auśīnarī from the magnanimous sage Gautama in Maga-dha; Gautama took his residence in Magadha; since the kings favoured him, he took resort with the Magadha dynasty (शूद्रायां गौतमो यत्र महात्मा सं-शितव्रतः । औशीनर्याम् अजनयत् काक्षीवा-दीन् सुतान् ऋषिः ॥ गौतमः क्षयणाद् अस्माद् अथासौ तत्र वेश्मनि । भजते मागधं वंशं स नृपाणाम् अनुग्रहात् ॥ ) 2. 19. 5-6; (3) Ambuvīca was formerly the king at Rājagṛha who ruled over the Māgadha chieftains (श्रूयते हि पुरा कश्चिद् अम्बुवीच इति श्रुतः । आसीद् राजगृहे राजा मागधानां महीक्षिताम् ॥ ) 1. 196. 17. F. Some persons designated after the Magadha country or its people as one be-longing to Magadha, or the king of Magadha, or the foremost among the Magadhas, or the protector of Magadha country: A. One belonging to Magadha: (a) मागध: (1) Jayatsena, son of Jarā-sandha 5. 19. 8; 6. 104. 14, 56; 6. 110. 29 (cf. 31); 8. 4. 31; 9. 2. 17, 34; in the following references Jayatsena is probably meant although he is not directly named 2. 49. 7 (or Sahadeva ?); 6. 17. 27; 6. 18. 15; 6. 58. 312, 42-43; 6. 77. 3; 7. 47. 7; (2) Jarāsandha 2. 13. 21, 45; 2. 14. 18; 2. 17. 19; 2. 20. 21-24; 2. 21. 3, 18; 8. 5. 22; 12. 5. 1; (3) Jalasandha 5. 164. 24; 7. 91. 28; (4) Daṇḍadhāra 8. 13. 3; (5) Bṛhadratha 2. 17. 11; (6) Meghasandhi 14. 83. 14-16, 26; 14. 84. 1; (7) Sahadeva (son of Jarā-sandha) 5. 56. 8; 5. 154. 10; 8. 4. 85; (8) Unidentified 8. 31. 11 (but we have proba-bly to read मागधाश् च; see above Epic events No. 16); (b) मागधी (f.) (1) Amṛtā 1. 90. 43; (2) Saṃpriyā 1. 90. 42; B. King of Magadha (or of Māgadhas): (a) मगधराज्: Bṛhadratha 1. 57. 29; (b) मगधाधिप: Jarāsandha 15. 32. 12; (c) मगधाधिपति: (1) Bṛhadratha 2. 16. 12; 2. 17. 7, 21; मागधानाम् अधिपति-Jayatsena 8. 51. 23; 11. 25. 7; (d) मग-धेश्वर: Meghasaṃdhi (grandson of Jarāsandha 14. 83. 3) 14. 83. 10; C. Chief or foremost among Māgadhas: (a) मागधेन्द्र: Jarāsandha 5. 50. 38; (b) मागधानां प्रवरः: Daṇḍadhāra 8. 13. 5; D. Protector of the Magadha country: गोप्ता मागधराष्ट्रस्य: Dārva 1. 105. 10.
माचेल्लक: Mācellaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Epic events: (1) During the war, their warriors were on the side of Kauravas; in the evening of the eleventh day of the war (7. 16. 1-2), in the camp of Kauravas Mācellakas were among those who, led by Suśarman, took the oath to kill Arjuna (सुशर्मा … माचेल्लकैर् … सहितो … सो ऽशपद् भ्रातृभिः सह) 7. 16. 19-20; (2) On the twelfth day, Arjuna killed Mācella-kas and others; they, too, heavily showered arrows of different kinds on Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna so that the two became invisible; considering them killed, Mācellakas and others were pleased; they shook their upper garments (वासांस्य् आदुधुवुस् तदा) and sounded various instruments; they roared loudly; Arjuna scattered away their arrows with वायव्यास्त्र 7. 18. 16-20, 22; (3) On the fourteenth day, Mācellakas were among those ten thousand warriors who, driven in chariots, followed Jaya, Kṛtavarman and others to check the advance of Arjuna towards Jayadratha (तेषां दशसहस्राणि रथानाम् अनुयायिनाम् । … माचेल्लका ललि-त्थाश् च … नरव्याघ्रम् अवारयन् … न्यवारयन्त) 7. 66. 37-38, 41, 43.
माद्रेय: Mādreya m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तत्रेमे … शाल्व-माद्रेयजाङ्गलाः) 6. 10. 37.
मानवर्जक: Mānavarjaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37. 5; (मागधा मानवर्जकाः) 6. 10. 48.
मर्तिकावत: Martikāvata m. (sg.): Name of a country. A. Epic event: Kṛṣṇa reached Mār-tikāvata from Dvārakā to attack Śālva; he crossed many countries, mountains full of woods, lakes and rivers to reach Mārtikā-vata (समतीत्य बहून् देशान् गिरींश् च बहुपादपान् । सरांसि सरितश् चैव मार्ति-कावतम् आसदम् ॥ ) 3. 21. 14. B. Certain kings designated after the name of the country: मार्तिकावतक: (1) Citraratha 3. 116. 6; (2) Bhoja 7. 47. 8; (3) Śālva 3. 15. 16. [See Addenda Mārtikāvata, name of a town].
मालक: Mālaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा  … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (मालका मल्लकाश् चैव) 6. 10. 61.
मालव: Mālava1 m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; sometimes mentioned along with Kṣullakas. A. Designation: Distinguished as eastern, western and northern Mālavas; they were included among the twelve Janapadas (प्राच्याः प्रतीच्योदीच्यमाल-वाः ॥ द्वादशैते जनपदाः) 6. 18. 13-14; 6. 114. 76-77. B. Location: To the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha (see Epic event (1) below). C. Description: Their warriors were brave and prepared to sacrifice their lives (शूर, तनूत्यज्) 6. 18. 14; 7. 132. 23; strong (बलवन्त्) 6. 112. 107; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 6. 112. 107, 111. D. Epic events: (1) Nakula in his expedition to the west (निर्याय खाण्डव-प्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 10) before the Rājasūya subjugated Mālavas (वशे चक्रे … । मालवान् पञ्चकर्-पटान् ॥ ) 2. 29. 6; their Kṣatriyas brought wealth in hundreds as tribute for the Rājasūya (सह क्षुद्रकमालवैः ॥ … आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो) 2. 48. 14-16; (2) In the war, they were to be faced by the five Kekaya brothers who were on the side of Pāṇḍavas (भ्रातरः पञ्च केकयाः । … तेषाम् एव कृतो भागो मालवाः) 5. 56. 17-18; (3) Mālava warriors were among the twelve Janapadas who, riding chariots, were to protect Bhīṣma in the war (महता रथवंशेन ते ऽभ्यरक्षन् पितामहम्) 16. 18. 13-14; (4) On the second day of war, in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas, Duryodhana, assisted by Mālava warriors and others gave protection to the army of Śakuni (तथा क्षुद्रकमालवैः । अभ्य-रक्षत … सौबलेयस्य वाहिनीम्) 6. 47. 10, 16; (5) On the third day of war, Kṣudra-kas and Mālavas, led by Droṇa and others, rushed towards Arjuna as directed by Bhīṣma; they were killed by Arjuna with the use of the Māhendra अस्त्र (क्षुद्रक-मालवाश् च । किरीटिनं त्वरमाणाभिसस्रुर् निदेशगाः शान्तनवस्य) 6. 55. 74; (निपाति-ताः क्षुद्रकमालवाश् च) 6. 55. 130, 110, 120; (6) On the eighth day of war, Bhīṣma, supported by Mālavas and others, led the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas; he was followed by Droṇa accompanied by Kṣu-drakas and Mālavas (अग्रतः सर्वसैन्या-नां भीष्मः … ययौ । मालवैर् दाक्षि-णात्यैश् च … ॥ ततो ऽनन्तरम् एवासीद् भारद्वाजः … । … तथा क्षुद्रकमाल-वैः ॥ ) 6. 83. 5-7; (7) On the ninth day, Mālavas were among those who did not abandon Bhīṣma although they were being killed by sharp arrows (संग्रामे नाजहुर् भीष्मं वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः) 6. 102. 7; (8) On the tenth day, exhorted by Duryodhana (6. 112. 102, 105) the great Mālava chariot-fighters (महारथाः 6. 112. 107, 111) attacked Arjuna; he struck them with heavenly weapons (दिव्यान्य् अस्त्राणि) which burnt them; afflicted by arrows, they did not attack Arjuna (ते शरार्ता … नाभ्यवर्तन्त … वानरध्वजम्); Arjuna killed them 6. 112. 109-116; on that day also they did not abandon Bhīṣma although they were struck with arrows and were afficted due to wounds (शरार्ता व्रण-पीडिताः । संग्रामे न जहुर् भीष्मम् युध्यमानं किरीटिना ॥ ) 6. 114. 76-77; (9) At the end of the eleventh day in the camp of Kauravas, Mālavas were among those thirty thousand chariot-fighters who, led by Suśarman, took oath to kill Arjuna (रथानाम् अयुतैस् त्रिभिः) 7. 16. 19-20; (10) On the twelfth day, Arjuna pierced Mālavas with arrows, but they continued to shower arrows of diffe-rent kinds on him (व्यसृजन् शरवर्षाणि पार्थे नानाविधानि च) so that Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna could not be seen by others; Mālavas thought that the two were killed and were delighted; they sounded instruments, roared, and waived their upper garments (वासांस्य् आदुधुवुस् तदा); Arjuna removed (the screen produced by) the shower of their arrows by employing वायव्यास्त्र (वायव्यास्त्रेण तैर् अस्तां शरवृष्टिम् अपाहरत्) 7. 18. 16-22; (11) During the night war (14th-15th day), Yudhiṣṭhira killed many heroic Mālavas and others (मालवाञ् शूरान् … गणान्) 7. 132. 23; 7. 136. 3; (12) After the death of Droṇa, on the sixteenth day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra while recounting Kṛṣṇa's former exploits mentioned his victory over Mālavas 7. 10. 17; (13) On the night of the seventeenth day, after the death of Karṇa (हते कर्णे … निशि 8. 1. 25) Saṃjaya mentioned Mālavas among those who were killed in the first seventeen days of war 8. 4. 46. E. Some persons referred to after the name of the country: A. One who belonged to Mālava: (i) मालव: (1) Indravarman 7. 164. 101; 7. 165. 115; (2) Sudarśana 7. 171. 56, 58; 7. 172. 9; (ii) मालवी (f.): Wife of king Aśvapati of the the Madra country 3. 277. 22; 3. 281. 58; 3. 283. 13.

Mālava2 m. (pl.): Common designa-tion of Sāvitrī's hundred brothers. They were born of Mālavī, wife of king Aśvapati of the Madra country (3. 277. 5-6) as a result of the boon given by Yama to Sāvitrī (पितुश् च ते पुत्रशतं भविता तव मातरि । मालव्यां मालवा नाम … भ्रातरस् ते भविष्यन्ति) 3. 281. 58; 3. 283. 13; they are described as god-like (त्रिदशोपमाः) and were to continue their line for ever (शाश्वताः पुत्रपौत्रि-णः) 3. 281. 58; they were very strong (भ्रातॄणां … शतम् । … सुमहाबलम्) 3. 283. 13.
मालवाणक: Mālavāṇaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा ॥।) 6. 10. 56, 5; (कोङ्कणा मालवाणकाः) 6. 10. 58.
मावेल्लक: Māvellaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their warriors fought on the side of Kauravas; in his report to Dhṛtarāṣṭra after the first seventeen days of war, Saṃjaya mentioned Māvellakas among those who were killed by Arjuna (मावेल्ल-कास् … ते हताः समरे राजन् पार्थेन … ) 8. 4. 47, 50.
माहिष: Māhiṣa m. (pl.): Name of Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37. 5; (माहिषकार्षिकाः) 6. 10. 45 [See the next].
माहिषक: Māhiṣaka, Mahiṣaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (उन्नत्यका माहिषका … ) 6. 10. 57; but they are also said to have resided near the southern ocean (प्रययौ भूयो दक्षिणं सलिलार्-णवम्) 14. 84. 10-11 (see Epic event). B. Description and characteristic: Fierce (रौद्रैर् माहिषकैर् अपि) 14. 84. 11 (रौद्र name of a different people or description of Māhiṣakas ?); a Brāh-maṇa reported to the Kuru assembly that Māhiṣakas practised bad धर्म and hence they should be avoided ( … उक्तवान् सभ्यो ब्राह्मणः कुरुसंसदि; … माहि-षकान् … दुर्धर्मांश् च विवर्जयेत्) 8. 30. 41, 45; they were originally a Kṣatriya community but became degraded to the status of a वृषल due to their disregard of Brāhmaṇas (माहिषकास् तास् ताः क्षत्रिय-जातयः ॥ वृषलत्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणा-नाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 33. 20-21. C. Epic event: Arjuna in his expedition before the Aśvamedha fought a fierce battle with the Māhiṣakas and others 14. 84. 11. [See Māhiṣa].
मुकुट: Mukuṭa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their king Vigāhana mentioned by Bhīma among the eighteen famous kings who extirpated their kinsmen, friends, and relatives (अष्टादशेमे राजानः प्रख्याता  … । ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान् ॥ … मुकुटानां विगाहनः । ।) 5. 72. 11, 16.
मुक्त: Mukta m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the third day of the war, Mukta warriors were among those who were posted at the left wing of the Garuḍavyūha (6. 52. 2-3) of the Kauravas (मुक्ताः पुण्ड्रविषस् तथा । … वामं पक्षम् उपा-श्रिताः) 6. 52. 9.
मुनिदेश: Munideśa m. (sg.): Name of a Deśa of the Krauñcadvīpa. Munideśa lay beyond Andhakāraka-deśa and beyond Munideśa lay Dundubhi-svanadeśa (अन्धकारकदेशात् तु मुनि-देशः परः स्मृतः । मुनिदेशात् परश् चैव प्रोच्यते दुन्दुभिस्वनः); all the Deśas of Krauñcadvīpa were frequented by gods and Gandharvas (देवगन्धर्वसेवि-ताः) 6. 13. 22-23.
मूषक: Mūṣaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya twice among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जन-पदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (विकल्पा मूषकास् तथा) 6. 10. 57; (मूषकाः स्तनबालाश् च) 6. 10. 62.
मेकल: Mekala m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (मेकलाश् चोत्कलैः सह) 6. 10. 39; (perhaps in the east, since they are mentioned along with Utkalas). B. Description: Their warriors skilled in fighting while riding elephants (गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः; गजयो-धिनः) 8. 17. 3, 2. C. Social status; Characterized as म्लेच्छस् 8. 17. 9; origi-nally Kṣatriyas, they were degraded to the status of वृषलस् since they disregarded Brāhmaṇas (मेकलाः … वृषलत्वम् अनु-प्राप्ता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 35. 17-18. D. Epic events: (1) On the second day of war, Droṇa supported by Mekalas and other warriors followed Bhīṣma who led the Mahāvyūha of the Kauravas (विदर्भैर् मेकलैश् चैव) 6. 47. 13, 10; (2) On the eighth day, Bṛhadbala along with Mekalas and others followed Bhagadatta (who followed Droṇa and Bhīṣma) in the Mahāvyūha of the Kauravas (मेकलैस् त्रैपुरैश् चैव) 6. 83. 9, 5; (3) On the sixteenth day, as ordered by Duryodhana, angry Mekalas and other warriors attacked Dhṛṣṭadyumna with elephants in order to kill him (हस्ति-भिस् तु महामात्रास् तव पुत्रेण चोदिताः ।  … क्रुद्धाः पार्षतम् अभ्ययुः ॥ … मेकला  … ); they showered him with तोमरस् and नाराच arrows; Dhṛṣṭadyumna repulsed their attack with नाराच arrows by hitting each elephant with six, eight, or ten arrows (एकैकम् दशभिः षड्भिर् अष्टा-भिर् अपि भारत । द्विरदान् अभिविव्याध) 8. 17. 1-6; later they attacked Nakula with elephants showering arrows and तोमरस् on him; the battle that ensued between chariot- and elephant-fighters described 8, 17. 20-28.
मौक: Mauka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (बोधा मौकास् तथैव च) 6. 10. 38.
मौलेय: Mauleya m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their Kṣatriyas and those of Vasātis and others brought wealth in hundreds as tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya (वसा-तयः समौलेयाः … ॥ आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 14, 16.
मौष्टिक: Mauṣṭika m. (pl.): Name of a people. As told by Karṇa to Śalya, according to the Rākṣasa Kalmāṣapāda, Mauṣṭikas were as good as the dirt of Mlecchas, and Śaṇḍas were the dirt of Mauṣṭikas (म्ले-च्छानां मौष्टिका मलम् । मौष्टिकानां मलं शण्डाः) 8. 30. 70 [See P. L. Vaidya's note on the stanza, Cr. Edn. Vol. 10, p. 687; “Mauṣṭikāḥ or Muṣṭikāḥ, probably a sub-caste of the Mlecchas. It is likely that the term came to be confound-ed with Auṣṭrikāḥ (a reading of the Central group of manuscripts), a people who made their living by trade in camels”].
म्लेच्छ: Mleccha m. (pl.): General characte-rization of peoples who are distinguished from those who are designated as Āryas. A. The following peoples are speci-fically designated as म्लेच्छस्: Aṅgas 7. 25. 17; 7. 68. 31; 8. 17. 2, 14-16, 17-18; Āndharas 3. 186. 29-30; Ābhīras 3. 186. 29-30; 16. 8. 45; Utkalas 8. 17. 20; Aurṇakas 3. 186. 29-30; Kāmbojas 3. 186. 29-30; 6. 10. 64; Kāliṅgas 8. 17. 20; Kośalas 8. 17. 3; Tāmraliptakas 8. 17. 2, 20; Daśārṇas 8. 17. 3; Dasyus of Pañcanada 16. 8. 43-44, 47, 58, 60; Niṣadhas 8. 17. 3, 20; Puṇḍras 8. 17. 3, 13; Pulindas 3. 186. 29; Madras 8. 17. 3; 8. 27. 91; Māgadhas 8. 17. 2; Mekalas 8. 17. 3, 20; Yavanas 3. 186. 29; 6. 10. 64; 8. 59. 12: Vaṅgas 8. 17. 2, 11; Śakas 3. 186. 29-30; Śūdras 3. 186. 29-30; Sindhusauvīras 8. 27. 91. B. Location: They, along with Āryas, inhabit the Bhāratavarṣa and drink the waters of Gaṅgā, Sindhu and Sarasvatī (6. 10. 12); in the north they are listed by Saṃjaya among the northern tribes of Bhāratavarṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना  … ॥ … म्लेच्छजातयः । ) 6. 10. 63, 64, 5; in the north (उदीच्यां दिशि यद् वृत्तं म्लेच्छेषु) 12. 162. 28; on the foot-hills of Himavant: Pāṇḍavas saw them on their way to Gandhamādana (देशान् म्लेच्छगणाकीर्णान् … ददृशुर् गिरिपादांश् च) 3. 145. 12; they lived also in the in-accessible places of the Himavant moun-tain (हिमवद्दुर्गवासिनाम्) 7. 87. 37; some lived on the Vindhya mountain as well (विन्ध्यनिलया म्लेच्छाः) 12. 59. 103; in forests in general (वनं … म्लेच्छतस्क-रनिषेवितम्) 3. 61. 2; located also in east and south (प्राच्याश् च दाक्षिणात्याश् च; ते म्लेच्छैः प्रेषिता नागाः) 8. 17. 2, 9; near the oceans: they lived by the gulf of the western ocean (reference to Nakula's expedition to the west 2. 29. 2) (सागर-कुक्षिस्थान् म्लेच्छान्) 2. 29. 15; along the eastern ocean (सागरानूपवासिभिः) -here they are mentioned along with Bhagadatta of the east 2. 31. 9-10; 2. 47. 12; along the ocean in general (सागरानूपगांश् चैव) 3. 48. 19; (सागरानूपवासिनः) 8. 51. 19; समुद्रवासिनः) 1. 202. 8; on the islands of the eastern ocean (reference to Bhīma's expedition to the east 2. 26. 1) (म्लेच्छनृपतीन् सागरद्वीपवासिनः) 2. 27. 25, 23; on the islands of the southern ocean (reference to Sahadeva's expedi-tion to the south 2. 28. 1) (सागरद्वीप-वासांश् च नृपतीन् म्लेच्छयोनिजान्) 2. 28. 44; along the seacoast in Vaṅga, Puṇḍra and Kerala (see epic event No. 15); they did not exist in the Varṣas of the द्वीपस् of Uttara Kuru (न तेषु दस्यवः सन्ति म्लेच्छजात्योऽपि वा … ) 6. 13. 15, 1. C. Different Origins: (1) In the bygone days, the sages churned the right thigh of king Vena whom they had killed; from it arose a dwarfish person (ह्रस्वा-ङ्गः); him, the sages said ‘sit down’ (निषीद); from him were born Niṣādas and other Mlecchas in hundreds and thousands living on Vindhya mountain (तस्मान् निषादाः संभूताः … ये चान्ये विन्ध्यनिलयाः म्लेच्छाः शतसहस्रशः) 12. 59. 101-103; (2) Mlecchas were produced by Nandinī, Vasiṣṭha's cow, from her foam; they and other peoples produced by Nandinī formed a large army; they wore different armours and held different wea-pons (म्लेच्छान् फेनतः सा ससर्ज ह ॥ तैर् विसृष्टैर् महत् सैन्यं नानाम्लेच्छ-गणैस् तदा । नानावरणसंछन्नैर् नाना-युधधरैस् तथा) 1. 165. 36-37 (perhaps, here the term म्लेच्छगण is used to in-clude Pallavas and others who were also then produced by Nandinī); the origin of Mlecchas from cows also referred to in 7. 68. 42 (गोयोनिप्रभवा म्लेच्छाः) and in 7. 87. 36 (सन्ति गोयोनयश् चात्र); (3) All Mleccha tribes sprang from Anu, the son of Yayāti (अनोस् तु म्लेच्छजातयः) 1. 80. 26; (4) Originally all were Brāhmaṇas (न विशेषो ऽस्ति वर्णानां सर्वं ब्राह्मम् इदं जगत्) 12. 181. 10; later, Brāhmaṇas who did not know (the धर्म and did not observe the vows and regulations) became different tribes such as Mlecchas (ब्रह्म चैतत् पुरा सृष्टं ये न जानन्त्य् अतद्विदः । तेषां बहुविधास् त्व् अन्यास् तत्र तत्र हि जातयः । … बहुधा म्लेच्छजातयः) 12. 181. 18; (5) Sinful men who lived under the influence of greed and temptation were born as Mlecchas who did not deserve to be associated with (असंवासाः प्रजा-यन्ते म्लेच्छाश् चापि न संशयः । नराः पापसमाचारा लोभमोहसमन्विताः ॥ ) 13. 112. 108. D. Description and characte-ristics: (1) Of Mlecchas in general: im-pure (अशुचि) 7. 68. 44; sinful (पाप) 1. 79. 13; (पापकर्तृ) 7. 87. 37; bad (असत्) 7. 87. 37; cruel, harsh in all acts, eat anything (म्लेच्छाः क्रूराः सर्वभक्षा दारुणाः सर्वकर्मसु) 3. 188. 52; 6. 10. 64; (परमदारुण) 2. 29. 15; lusting after the wives of their teachers, they follow the laws of animals and are therefore as good as born animals (गुरुदारप्रसक्तेषु तिर्यग्योनिगतेषु च । पशुधर्मिषु … म्लेच्छेषु) 1. 79. 13; their heads were shaven, or half shaven, or they wore twisted hair; their faces were bearded (मुण्डार्धमुण्डजटिलान् … जटिलाननान्) 7. 68. 44; they had queer appearances (नानाविकृतदर्शन) 7. 68. 37; Mlecchas were born in sinful countries and were igno-rant of धर्मस् (पापदेशोद्भवा म्लेच्छा धर्माणाम् अविचक्षणाः) 8. 27. 91; they lost knowledge and higher knowledge and hence behaved as they liked (प्रनष्टज्ञान-विज्ञानाः स्वच्छन्दाचारचेष्टिताः) 12. 181. 18; Rākṣasa Kalmāṣapāda told a certain king that Mlecchas were the dirt of human beings and Mauṣṭikas were the dirt of Mlecchas (मानुषाणां मलं म्लेच्छा म्लेच्छानां मौष्टिका मलम्) 8. 30. 70; all varṇas including Mlecchas observe fast (सर्वेषाम् एव वर्णानां म्लेच्छानां च … । उपवासे मतिर् … ) 13. 109. 1; they did not deserve to be associated with (असंवासाः) 13. 112. 108; Mlecchas understood only their own conventions (म्लेच्छाः स्वसंज्ञा-नियताः) 8. 30. 80 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 8. 45. 36: (स्वससंज्ञायां स्वीयैः कृतो यो धर्मसङ्केतस् तत्रैव नियताः वैदिकं धर्मं न मानयन्तीत्य् अर्थः); When the Pāṇḍavas left for Vāraṇāvata Vidura spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira in the speech of Mlecchas (unintelligible to others) (उक्तो म्लेच्छवाचासि पाण्डव) 1. 135. 6; (2) Mleccha warriors: Wore different kinds of dresses (नानावेषधर) 7. 68. 38; they were brave (शूर) 8. 31. 22, strong (बलिन्), furious (संरम्भिन्), fond of battles (युद्धशौण्ड) and firm-fisted (दृब्ध-पाणि) 8. 51. 19; 7. 87. 17; skilled in fighting battles (युद्धविशारद) 7. 103. 22; they did not turn their backs to the enemies (अनिवर्तिन्) 7. 98. 23; fought heroically with various kinds of weapons (नानायुधवीर्य-वन्त्) 5. 22. 21; (नानाशस्त्रौघसंवृत) 7. 68. 38; (विविधायुधपाणि) 7. 95. 13; they were skilled in fighting while riding elephants (गजयोधिन्, गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 2-3; their fights from ele-phant-backs often mentioned 7. 68. 37, 40, 46 (also horses); 7. 87. 16-18; 8. 31. 22; their elephant-force known as अञ्जनक; the elephants never turned back once they were goaded to attack the enemies; they preferred death to defeat (यद् एतत् कुञ्ज-रानीकं साहस्रम् अनुपश्यसि । कुलम् अञ्जनकं नाम … ; नैते जातु निवर्तेरन् प्रेषिता हस्तिसादिभिः । अन्यत्र हि वधाद् एषां नास्ति राजन् पराजयः) 7. 87. 16-17; (3) Mleccha Kings: Acted as their teachers (म्लेच्छाचार्याश् च राजानः) 12. 4. 8 (cf. S. B. Belvalkar's note on this stanza in Vol. 13, p. 638. 1: “Mleccha kings of the west were also the आचार्यस् or the spiritual heads of their domain”). E. Epic events: (1) Duḥṣanta ruled over the entire earth including the countries of the Mlecchas and Āṭavikas (आ म्लेच्छाटविकान् सर्वान्) 1. 62. 5; (2) Bhīma in his expedition to the east before the Rājasūya (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1, 7; 2. 23. 9) defeated Mleccha hordes who lived on the islands of the eastern ocean (ये च सागर-वासिनः । सर्वान् म्लेच्छगनांश् चैव विजिग्ये) 2. 27. 23; he made their kings pay tribute in the form of jewels and many other precious articles including gold, silver etc. (स सर्वान् म्लेच्छनृपतीन् सागर-द्वीपवासिनः । करम् आहारयाम् आस रत्नान्त् विविधानि च) 2. 27. 25-26; Sahadeva in his expedition to the south (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; 2. 23. 9) brought under control Mleccha kings living in islands and made them pay tribute for the Rājasūya (सागरद्वीपवासांश् च नृपतीन् म्लेच्छयोनिजान्; करदान् पार्थिवान् कृत्वा) 2. 28. 44, 54; Nakula in his expedition to the west (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रती-चीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 10) brought under control Mlecchas living along the western ocean (ततः सागरकुक्षि-स्थान् म्लेच्छान्) 2. 29. 15; 5. 49. 26; Mle-cchas were among those who made a crowd at the Rājasūya (सर्वे म्लेच्छाः … । पर्-यस्त इव लोको ऽयं युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने) 2. 48. 33; Kṛṣṇa saw Mlecchas among those who worked as attendants at the Rājasūya (अहम् अद्राक्षं यज्ञे ते परि-वेषकान्) 3. 48. 19; (3) Pāṇḍavas on their way to Viśālā Badarī saw countries inhabited by hordes of Mlecchas (देशान् म्लेच्छगणाकीर्णान्) 3. 145. 12; (4) Some Mlecchas had joined the army of Pāṇḍavas (पाण्डवार्थे निविष्टाः) 5. 22. 21; others had joined the army of Duryodhana (राजचमूं समेताम् । … म्लेच्छैः) 5. 158. 19-20; (5) Mlecchas and Āryas, who had gathered for war and who had seen or heard about the conduct of Pāṇḍavas wept with choked throats (म्लेच्छाश् चार्याश् च … ददृशुः शुश्रुवुस् तदा । तद् वृत्तं पाण्डुपुत्राणां रुरुदुस् ते सगद्-गदाः ॥ ) 6. 41. 103; (6) On the fourteenth day, countless Mlecchas, along with the elephants who carried them, were killed by Arjuna with the माया of his अस्त्रस् (अस्त्र-मायया); वडस्, कङ्कस् and wolves were glad to drink their blood 7. 68. 37, 42, 44, 46; 7. 69. 30; (7) On the same day, Sātyaki noticed the large army of Añjanaka elephants ridden by Mlecchas 7. 87. 16-18; having secured that large army of elephants of Mlecchas, Duryodhana had felt contempt for Pāṇḍavas (एतद् दुर्योधनो लब्ध्वा समग्रं नागमण्डलम् … अवमन्यत पाण्डवान् ॥ ) 7. 87. 37-39; Sātyaki pointed out to his charioteer the Mlecchas who, riding chariots, horses and elephants, and equipped with different weapons, desired to fight with him 7. 95. 13-14; (8) Duḥśā-sana, rebuked by Droṇa, attacked Sātyaki along with a large army of Mlecchas (सै-न्येन महता युक्तो म्लेच्छानाम् अनिवर्ति-नाम्) 7. 98. 23; (9) The same day, Bhīma defeated and passed beyond many hordes of Mlecchas in order to get near Arjuna 7. 103. 32; (10) On the fifteenth day, Bhīma while scolding Droṇa mentioned that he, like a Cāṇḍāla, had killed many hordes of Mlecchas 7. 165. 30; (11) On the sixteenth day, Mlecchas (8. 17. 9) riding elephants fought a severe battle with Dhṛṣṭadyumna and other Pāṇḍava promi-nent warriors 8. 17. 1-28 (for details of the battle see Mekala); (12) On the seventeenth day, Mlecchas riding elephants in rut, led by Aśvatthāman and others, followed the chariot-army of Duryodhana at the back of the Bārhaspatyavyūha (8. 31. 26) of Kauravas 8. 31. 19-20, 22; the same day, Kṛṣṇa in order to encourage Arjuna said that Mlecchas who had asso-ciated themselves with Kurus in the interest of Duryodhana could not be conquered by any one else except him (म्लेच्छाश् च … एते सुयोधनस्यार्थे संरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह । न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुं त्वदन्येन परंतप ॥ ) 8. 51. 19-20; Mlecchas, riding thirteen hundred elephants in rut, attacked, as directed by Duryodhana, Arjuna from one side (पार्श्वतः); they showered Arjuna with कर्णिन्, नालीक, and नाराच arrows as also with तोमरस्, प्रासस्, शक्तिस्, कम्पनस् and भिण्डिपालस्; Arjuna cut off the shower of their arrows and weapons with भल्ल and अर्धचन्द्र arrows; he killed their elephants with different kinds of महाशरस्; the elephants began to run in all directions 8. 59. 10-16; (13) After the war was over, while Saṃjaya was reporting events of the eighteenth day to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the latter remembered that once the whole earth, including the Mlecchas and Āṭavikas was sustained due to the graciousness of Duryodhana (इयं च पृथिवी सर्वा सम्लेछाटविका … । प्रसादाद् ध्रियते यस्य) 9. 31. 3; later, Saṃjaya in his account listed Mlecchas among those who were killed in the great war (म्लेच्छाश् च … निपातिताः) 9. 1. 26; Dhṛtarāṣṭra remembered that Duryodhana, before the war, counted Mlecchas among those who, in thousands, were ready to fight and give up their lives for him; it was with their support that he was going to fight with Pāṇḍavas (म्लेच्छाश् च बहुसाहश्राः … मदर्थम् उद्यताः सर्वे प्राणांस् त्यक्त्वा रणे प्रभो ॥ ) 9. 2. 18, 21-22; that they were killed by thousands, was due to bad fate according to Dhṛtarāṣṭra (हता … म्लेच्छाश् च बहुसाहस्रा किम् अन्यद् भागधेयतः । ) 9. 2. 36; (14) Mlecchācāryas were among those who attended the स्वयं-वर of the Kaliṅga princess at Rājapura 12. 4. 8; (15) Arjuna in his wanderings with the Aśvamedha horse had to fight with Mlecchas who were formerly, in the war, offended by him (म्लेच्छाश् चान्ये बहुविधा पूर्वं विनिकृता रणे) 14, 72. 24; when the horse wandered along the seacoast through Vaṅga, Puṇḍra and Kerala countries, Arjuna defeated many Mleccha armies many times (ततः समुद्र-तीरेण वङ्गान् पुण्ड्रान् सकेरलान् ॥ तत्र तत्र च भूरीणी म्लेच्छसैन्यान्य् अने-कशः । विजिग्ये) 14. 83. 30; at the end of the Aśvamedha sacrifice, the sacrificial priests distributed a large quantity of gold among the Brāhmaṇas; after that, what wealth (gold) remained that was taken away over a long period by Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras and Mleccha tribes (अनन्तरं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः क्षत्रिया जह्रिरे वसु । तथा विट्शूद्रसंघाश् च तथान्ये म्ले-च्छजातयः । कालेन महता जह्रुस् तत् सुवर्णम् ततस् ततः ॥ ) 14. 91. 25; (16) On Arjuna's way from Dvārakā to Hāstina-pura, Mlecchas abducted Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka women 16. 8. 61. F. Past events: (1) Demons Sunda and Upasunda conquered all Mleccha tribes living in the ocean (समुद्रवासिनः सर्वान् म्लेच्छ-जातीन् विजिग्यतुः) 1. 202. 8; (2) Damayantī, forsaken by Nala, entered a forest inhabited by Mlecchas and thieves (म्लेच्छतस्कर-सेवितम्) 3. 61. 2; (3) Indra taught king Māndhātṛ the duties of Dasyus which term included Mlecchas 12. 65. 14, 17-22; (4) Bhīṣma told Yudhiṣṭhira a story related to Mlecchas who lived in the north (the term Dasyu is used in the story for Mlecchas) 12. 162. 28 ff.; (5) Yayāti cursed his son Turvasu to the effect that he would be born among the Mlecchas (म्लेच्छेषु प्रभविष्यसि) 1. 79. 13. G. Future event: Mārkaṇḍeya foretold that in the Kali age (कलौ युगे 3. 186. 27) there would be many Mleccha kings on this earth; they would be sinful, given to lies and rule the world the wrong way (बहवो म्लेच्छराजानः पृथिव्यां … । मिथ्यानुशासिनः पापा मृषावादपराय-णाः) 3. 186. 29; when the end of the aeon will have arrived (युगान्ते समनुप्राप्ते 3. 186. 33; युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते 3. 188. 19, 43-44. 47, 54, 76, 81-83; युगान्ते 3. 186. 34; 3. 188. 35-37, 39, 49, 53, 73, 79; युगस्यान्ते 3. 188. 32; अल्पावशिष्टे तु तदा युगान्ते 3. 186. 24; क्षीणे युगे 3. 186. 54; युगे क्षीणे 3. 188. 66; गते युगे 3. 188. 69; संप्राप्ते युगसंक्षये 3. 188. 55; युगसंक्षये 3. 188. 62; युगक्षये 3. 186. 36, 43, 48; 3. 188. 6, 20-23, 25, 33, 41, 50-51, 78, 85; पूर्वरूपं क्षयस्य तत् 3. 186. 28; तदा संक्षेप्स्यते युगम् 3. 188. 59, 67-68; पश्चिमे काले 3. 188. 52) the world would be full of Mlecchas (म्लेच्छभूतं जगत् सर्वं … ) 3. 188. 29, 45; (म्लेच्छी-भूतं जगत् सर्वं … ) 3. 188. 37; (मही म्लेच्छसमाकीर्णा भविष्यति) 3. 188. 70); the condition of the world at the end of the aeon described in 3. 186. 24-57; 3. 188. 14-85; A Brāhmaṇa named Kalki Viṣṇuyaśas would be born in the Sambhala town; he would become a sovereign king (राजा चक्रवर्ती), destroy all the Mleccha hordes, and give a turn to the Yuga (युगस्य परिवर्तकः । … उत्सादयिष्यति तदा सर्वान् म्लेच्छगणान् द्विजः ॥ ) 3. 188. 89-93.
